# Introduction

Welcome to **ModelScript**, the open-core **computable digital thread** platform and polyglot engineering compiler designed for multi-domain physical modeling, formal verification, and AI-assisted systems engineering.

---

## What is the Computable Digital Thread?

Modern cyber-physical systems — from electric vehicles, utility power grids, and satellites to surgical robots and subsea flowlines — require tight coordination across **44 engineering languages and file formats** spanning **12 industry verticals**:

- **System Architecture, Requirements & Ontologies** (`SysML v2`, `KerML`, `ReqIF`, `OSLC 3.0`, `OWL2`, `AAS / DDP`)
- **Multi-Domain Acausal & Block-Diagram Simulation** (`Modelica 3.x`, `ModelScript .msx`, `MATLAB Simulink`, `FMI 2.0/3.0 FMU`, `SSP 1.0/2.0`)
- **Power Grids, Electronics & Embedded Control** (`PSCAD EMT`, `Siemens PSS/E`, `SPICE`, `IBIS`, `Touchstone`, `Gerber`, `PLCopen IEC 61131-3`, `AUTOSAR ARXML`, `CAN DBC`, `ANSI C`)
- **3D CAD Geometry, Multibody & Robotics** (`STEP AP214/AP242`, `OpenSCAD CSG`, `ROS URDF / Xacro`, `SIMPACK`, `MSC Adams`, `GENSYS`)
- **Continuum CAE, Process, Thermal & Fluid Networks** (`CalculiX / Abaqus FEA`, `SU2 / OpenFOAM CFD`, `Gmsh`, `VTK`, `OLGA`, `PipelineStudio`, `Aspen Plus`, `EnergyPlus`, `EPANET`, `EPA SWMM`, `SBML`, `THERM`, `RADIANCE`)

Traditionally, these disciplines operate in disconnected silos. Enterprise "digital threads" have historically been **passive and descriptive** — composed of static document links, heavyweight PLM databases, and manual spreadsheets that drift out of sync the moment a parameter changes.

**ModelScript makes the digital thread _computable_.**

Instead of passive hyperlinks, ModelScript treats every engineering artifact as **executable, Git-versioned source code** compiled into a shared WebAssembly representation and continuously checked by graph rewriting engines and mathematical solvers:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Architecture & Requirements<br/>(SysML v2 / ReqIF / OWL2)"] <-->|"Bidirectional TGG"| P["1D & Multibody Physics<br/>(Modelica / Simulink / PSCAD)"]
    P <-->|"Dynamic Kinematic & CSG Binding"| G["3D CAD & Robotics<br/>(STEP / OpenSCAD / URDF)"]
    P <-->|"ROM Surrogates & Field Coupling"| C["Continuum CAE & Flow<br/>(FEA / CFD / OLGA)"]
    A & P & G & C -->|"13 Nelson-Oppen Theory Oracles"| V["SARIF Proof Manifests<br/>& Regulatory DHF Dossiers"]
    M["AI Agents (@modelscript/mcp)"] <-->|"Closed-Loop Synthesis"| P & V
```

### Traditional Passive PLM vs. Computable Digital Thread

| Dimension                    | Traditional Passive PLM / MBSE                              | ModelScript Computable Digital Thread                                                          |
| :--------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Artifact Storage**         | Proprietary binary blobs in centralized SQL/PLM vaults      | Plain-text, human-readable source files versioned in Git                                       |
| **Cross-Domain Links**       | Manual, untyped hyperlinks that silently go stale           | Typed `@satisfies` / `@verifies` bindings & bidirectional Triple Graph Grammars (TGG)          |
| **Static Analysis**          | Checked manually during design reviews                      | **794 static lint rules** across **44 languages** evaluated on every keystroke and CI push     |
| **Requirement Verification** | Post-hoc spreadsheet sign-offs                              | Automated $\text{CDCL}(\mathcal{T})$ SMT, IC3/PDR, and Taylor-model reachability proofs        |
| **Code Review & Diffs**      | Opaque binary attachments or screenshot exports             | Structural AST/DAE diffs and visual schematic PR diffs (`msx pr-diff`)                         |
| **AI Copilot Integration**   | Unverified text generation prone to physical hallucinations | Closed-loop MCP server (`@modelscript/mcp`) grounded in DAE solvers and formal counterexamples |

---

## Core Pillars of ModelScript

### 1. Code-First Engineering Across 44 Languages

Every model, schematic, requirement, netlist, and mesh configuration lives as clean text in Git. Engineers diff, review, merge, and gate physical hardware designs using standard pull requests, SARIF code scanning, and reproducible CI/CD pipelines.

### 2. Zero-Allocation WebAssembly CST & DAE Arenas

Each language grammar compiles ahead-of-time via `@modelscript/dsl` (`buildParser`) into a native WebAssembly GLR parser (`parser.wasm`). Concrete syntax trees and flattened Differential-Algebraic Equations (`DAEBuilder`) reside in Struct-of-Arrays (SoA) linear memory with zero JavaScript object wrapper overhead, delivering consistent compiler performance across the CLI, VS Code, and browser WebWorkers.

### 3. Bidirectional Triple Graph Grammars (TGG) & Critical Pair Analysis

Keep system architecture, electronics, CAD, and physics in permanent synchronization. Declarative Double-Pushout (DPO) Triple Graph Grammar rules propagate architectural changes (`SysML v2`) forward into physical simulation models (`Modelica`, `SPICE`, `STEP`), while back-annotating numerical sizing results back into system requirements — verified for confluence via static Critical Pair Analysis (CPA).

### 4. Nelson-Oppen Multi-Theory Formal Verification (13 Theory Oracles)

Cross-domain verification is orchestrated by a $\text{CDCL}(\mathcal{T})$ Nelson-Oppen coordinator (`@modelscript/runtime`) that exchanges equality facts, interval contractors, and conflict clauses across **13 specialized domain theory oracles**:

1. **Ontology Theory (`OntologyTheoryOracle`)** — OWL2 Description Logic ($\mathcal{SROIQ}$) subsumption and disjointness
2. **Interval Constraint Theory (`ConstraintTheoryOracle`)** — SysML v2 / KerML HC4 revise and $\delta$-complete contractors
3. **Abstract Interpretation (`AbstractDomainOracle`)** — Relational Zone (Difference-Bound Matrix) and Octagon invariants
4. **Continuous Safety (`ContinuousSafetyOracle`)** — Sum-of-Squares (SOS) barrier certificates and Picard Taylor-model flowpipes
5. **Dynamic Simulation (`DynamicSimulationOracle`)** — DAE trajectory evaluation and Signal Temporal Logic (STL) robustness $\rho(\phi, \mathbf{x}, t)$
6. **3D Spatial Physics (`SpatialPhysicsOracle`)** — OpenCASCADE B-Rep minimum clearance, collision, and mass-property bounds
7. **CAE Contracts (`CaeContractOracle`)** — Structural FEA von Mises yield margins and CFD aerodynamic envelope contracts
8. **Causalization & Structural Matching (`CausalizationOracle`)** — Hopcroft-Karp matching, Pantelides DAE index, and algebraic loops
9. **Dimensional Analysis (`DimensionalOracle`)** — 7-base SI dimension exponent vector algebra ($\mathbb{Q}^7$) and affine unit conversions
10. **Assume-Guarantee Refinement (`EntailmentOracle`)** — Compositional contract refinement ($\mathcal{A}_2 \subseteq \mathcal{A}_1 \land \mathcal{G}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{G}_2$)
11. **Flow Conservation (`FlowAlgebraOracle`)** — Kirchhoff and fluid stream conservation ($\sum f_i = 0$) across connector graphs
12. **GD&T Tolerance Stack-Up (`ToleranceStackOracle`)** — Worst-case and RSS geometric tolerance stack-up from STEP AP242 PMI
13. **Uncertainty Quantification (`UqOracle`)** — Split conformal prediction intervals and First-Order Reliability Method (FORM) $\beta$ indices

### 5. Unified Multi-Language LSP & Incrementally Memoized Salsa Engine

A single background worker pool (`@modelscript/lsp`) indexes polyglot workspaces through an incremental Salsa query engine (`fetch → deep_verify → execute → backdate`). Engineers get cross-language go-to-definition, hover equations, unit checking, schematic rendering, and suspect-link diagnostics in VS Code, the browser IDE, and the native Tauri desktop studio.

### 6. AI-Native Closed-Loop Engineering (`@modelscript/mcp`)

Large language models struggle with physical engineering when left to guess differential equations in free text. `@modelscript/mcp` exposes **31 deterministic compiler, simulation, CAD, TGG, and formal verification tools** over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). AI agents iteratively draft code, run `modelica_lint`, integrate stiff DAEs with `modelica_simulate`, falsify requirements, and calibrate parameters via `modelica_diff_calibrate` until every formal proof passes.

# Installation

ModelScript runs from the same WebAssembly compiler core across browsers, desktop IDEs, headless CI runners, and AI agent hosts. Choose the surface that matches your workflow.

---

## For Users & Engineers

### 1. Zero-Install Browser Playground & Web IDE

To explore ModelScript without installing anything locally:

- **[Interactive Playground (`/playground`)](https://modelscript.org/playground)**: Try curated multi-domain examples, inspect live GLR syntax trees, run stiff DAE simulations, and view rendered schematics directly in your browser tab.
- **Full Web Studio (`https://ide.modelscript.org`)**: Multi-file workspace explorer, dockable 2D schematic and 3D OpenCASCADE CAD viewports, requirements traceability matrix, and in-browser WebWorker compilation.

### 2. Command-Line Interface (`msx`)

The `@modelscript/cli` package installs both the `modelscript` binary and its shorthand alias `msx` for local development, simulation sweeps, formal verification, and CI/CD automation (requires **Node.js ≥ 22**):

```bash
# Run any command via npx without global installation
npx @modelscript/cli --help

# Or install globally for system-wide access
npm install -g @modelscript/cli
msx --version
```

#### Accelerating Repeated CLI Runs with `--daemon`

When running frequent interactive checks or pre-commit hooks, start the persistent background compiler daemon so `msx` reuses warm WebAssembly parser instances and incremental Salsa caches over a local Unix socket (`~/.modelscript/daemon.sock`):

```bash
# Start the background daemon and inspect its status
msx daemon start
msx daemon status

# Pass --daemon to any command to reuse warm workspace caches
msx lint ./models --daemon
```

### 3. VS Code Extension

The official extension turns VS Code or Cursor into a complete multi-domain modeling studio:

1. Open VS Code and open the Extensions view (`Ctrl+Shift+X` or `Cmd+Shift+X`).
2. Search for **`ModelScript`** (`modelscript.modelscript`) and click **Install**.

The extension bundles the native WebAssembly Language Server (`@modelscript/lsp`), real-time diagnostics across all 44 supported formats, interactive schematic and Bode plot panels, the 3D WebGL CAD viewer, and the DAP time-travel simulation debugger.

### 4. AI Coding Assistants & MCP Server (`@modelscript/mcp`)

Connect AI agents (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or custom orchestrators) to ModelScript's **52 deterministic engineering tools** over the Model Context Protocol:

```bash
# Register @modelscript/mcp in Claude Code with a single command
claude mcp add modelscript -- npx -y @modelscript/mcp
```

For **Cursor** (`.cursor/mcp.json`), **Claude Desktop**, or **VS Code**, add the `stdio` server entry:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "modelscript": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelscript/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

See the [AI Agents & MCP Workflows Guide](./ai-agents.md) for closed-loop synthesis recipes and remote SSE gateway configuration.

### 5. Native Desktop Studio (Tauri v2)

For air-gapped networks, classified labs, or hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) benches, download the standalone native desktop application (`@modelscript/desktop`) from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/releases):

- **Linux**: Standalone `.AppImage` or Debian/Ubuntu `.deb` packages.
- **macOS**: Universal Apple Silicon / Intel `.dmg` disk image.
- **Windows**: 64-bit `.msi` installer or portable `.exe`.

The desktop studio embeds offline WebAssembly GLR parsers, local SQLite artifact caching, and native serial/UDP bridges for real-time HIL testing.

### 6. Containerized Enterprise Hub & Simulation Server

Deploy the self-hosted ModelScript Hub, package registry, REST/GraphQL/SPARQL APIs, and multi-tenant MCP gateway via Docker:

```bash
# Pull official multi-architecture containers
docker pull ghcr.io/modelscript/api:latest
docker pull ghcr.io/modelscript/web:latest

# Launch backend simulation cluster and web IDE
docker compose up -d
```

See the [Platform Administration Guide](./administration.md) for Kubernetes Helm charts, Slurm HPC worker provisioning, and PostgreSQL audit-ledger setup.

---

## For Contributors & Compiler Developers

To build and hack on the ModelScript monorepo locally, install **Node.js ≥ 24** (matching `.nvmrc`) and `npm`.

### 1. Clone & Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript.git
cd modelscript
npm install
```

### 2. Build Core Compiler & Language Runtimes

ModelScript compiles its native WebAssembly GLR parsers (`parser.wasm`), AssemblyScript flattening kernels, and TypeScript packages via Nx:

```bash
npm run build:libs    # Build core compiler packages and language runtimes
npm run build         # Build all monorepo packages and applications
```

### 3. Launch Local Development Servers

```bash
npm run dev           # Start API backend, LSP workers, and Web IDE
```

# Getting Started

This tutorial walks you through building a complete **computable digital thread** in ModelScript across five steps:

1. Authoring and linting a **Modelica** physical dynamics model (`BouncingBall.mo`)
2. Linking **SysML v2** safety requirements (`BouncingBallReq.sysml`) and running **formal verification** (`msx verify`)
3. Binding physical state trajectories to **3D CAD geometry** (`msx csg`)
4. Running **time-domain simulation**, rendering **SVG schematics**, and exporting an **FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation FMU** (`msx simulate`, `msx render`, `msx fmu`)
5. Closing the loop with an **AI Agent** via `@modelscript/mcp`

---

## Step 1: Create a Workspace & Physics Model

Create a new directory and initialize a `modelscript.json` workspace manifest:

```bash
mkdir bouncing-ball-thread && cd bouncing-ball-thread
msx init -y
```

Create `BouncingBall.mo` with a hybrid continuous-discrete impact model:

```modelica
model BouncingBall
  parameter Real e = 0.7 "Coefficient of restitution (0 < e < 1)";
  parameter Real g = 9.81 "Gravitational acceleration [m/s2]";
  parameter Real radius = 0.05 "Ball radius [m]";
  Real h(start = 1.0, fixed = true) "Center height above ground [m]";
  Real v(start = 0.0, fixed = true) "Vertical velocity [m/s]";
equation
  der(h) = v;
  der(v) = -g;
  when h <= radius and v < 0 then
    reinit(v, -e * pre(v));
  end when;
end BouncingBall;
```

Run the static analyzer to verify syntax, types, and equation balance (`2 variables, 2 equations`):

```bash
msx lint BouncingBall.mo
```

---

## Step 2: Add SysML v2 Requirements & Formal Verification

Now create `BouncingBallReq.sysml` next to `BouncingBall.mo` to capture architectural requirements and bind them to the physics model:

```sysml
package BouncingBallArchitecture {
  attribute def Meter;
  attribute def RestitutionCoeff;

  requirement def <'REQ-ENERGY-01'> PassiveReboundRequirement {
    doc /* The coefficient of restitution must remain strictly passive (0 < e <= 1)
         * so rebound height never exceeds initial drop height. */
    attribute e : RestitutionCoeff;
    require constraint { e > 0.0 and e <= 1.0 }
  }

  requirement def <'REQ-CLEARANCE-02'> PeakAltitudeBound {
    doc /* Peak rebound altitude after the first impact shall not exceed 0.60 m. */
    attribute hMax : Meter;
    require constraint { hMax <= 0.60 }
  }

  part def BouncingBallSystem {
    attribute e : RestitutionCoeff = 0.7;
    attribute hMax : Meter = 0.49;
    satisfy PassiveReboundRequirement by self;
    satisfy PeakAltitudeBound by self;
  }
}
```

Lint both files together and run the unified formal verifier to check all requirements and emit a **SARIF 2.1.0** report:

```bash
# Lint the polyglot workspace (Modelica + SysML v2)
msx lint BouncingBall.mo BouncingBallReq.sysml

# Formally verify requirements and contracts, emitting a SARIF proof report
msx verify BouncingBall BouncingBall.mo --format sarif --report results.sarif
```

---

## Step 3: Bind 3D CAD Geometry to Physical States

In ModelScript, physical states can directly drive 3D Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) or external STEP/glTF assets. Add a `CAD` annotation to `h` in `BouncingBall.mo`:

```modelica
model BouncingBall
  parameter Real e = 0.7 "Coefficient of restitution (0 < e < 1)";
  parameter Real g = 9.81 "Gravitational acceleration [m/s2]";
  parameter Real radius = 0.05 "Ball radius [m]";
  Real h(start = 1.0, fixed = true) "Center height above ground [m]" annotation(
    CAD(
      primitive = "sphere",
      radius = "radius",
      position = {0, 0, 0},
      dynamicPosition = "{0, h, 0}"
    )
  );
  Real v(start = 0.0, fixed = true) "Vertical velocity [m/s]";
equation
  der(h) = v;
  der(v) = -g;
  when h <= radius and v < 0 then
    reinit(v, -e * pre(v));
  end when;
end BouncingBall;
```

Extract and compile the 3D CSG topology from the command line, or open **ModelScript: Open 3D CAD Viewer** (`Ctrl+Shift+P`) in VS Code to watch the sphere rebound in 3D:

```bash
msx csg BouncingBall BouncingBall.mo
```

---

## Step 4: Simulate, Render Schematics & Export an FMI 3.0 FMU

Simulate the hybrid DAE over $3.0\text{ s}$, render an SVG schematic diagram, and package the model into a standards-compliant **FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation FMU** with an embedded WebAssembly binary:

```bash
# Flatten to the linear-memory DAE arena and simulate for 3.0 s
msx simulate BouncingBall BouncingBall.mo --stop-time 3.0 --interval 0.005 --format csv > trajectory.csv

# Render a publication-ready SVG schematic diagram
msx render BouncingBall BouncingBall.mo -o schematic.svg

# Export an FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation FMU with embedded C and WebAssembly binaries
msx fmu BouncingBall BouncingBall.mo --fmi-version 3 --type cs --wasm --output BouncingBall.fmu
```

---

## Step 5: Closed-Loop Calibration with an AI Agent (`@modelscript/mcp`)

Suppose experimental drop-test telemetry shows a lower rebound height than `e = 0.7` predicts. With `@modelscript/mcp` connected to your AI assistant (see [AI Agents & MCP Workflows](./ai-agents.md)), the agent can invoke **`modelica_diff_calibrate`** or **`modelscript_closed_loop_synthesize`** to automatically fit `e` against your CSV data and re-verify `BouncingBallReq.sysml`:

```json
{
  "tool": "modelica_diff_calibrate",
  "arguments": {
    "modelName": "BouncingBall",
    "sourceCode": "model BouncingBall ... end BouncingBall;",
    "parameters": [{ "name": "e", "initial": 0.7, "min": 0.1, "max": 0.99 }],
    "optimizer": "lbfgs",
    "maxIterations": 40
  }
}
```

# AI Agents & MCP Workflows

Large language models excel at generating structure and exploring design spaces, but when asked to write differential equations, power-grid topologies, or safety-critical requirements in free text, they frequently hallucinate mismatched units, structurally singular DAEs, or violated physical conservation laws.

ModelScript closes this loop through **`@modelscript/mcp`** — a deterministic **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server exposing **52 polyglot compilation, simulation, CAD, TGG, and formal verification tools** (plus **70+ domain-specific tool extensions**). Instead of guessing physics, an AI agent iteratively compiles, simulates, verifies, and calibrates models against mathematical solvers until every requirement proof passes.

---

## 1. Connecting Your AI Agent

`@modelscript/mcp` supports three transport topologies: local `stdio`, remote HTTP Server-Sent Events (`SSE`), and in-browser WebAssembly (`PolyglotMcpHost`).

### Claude Code (`stdio`)

Register the MCP server directly in your project or user scope:

```bash
claude mcp add modelscript -- npx -y @modelscript/mcp
```

### Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop & VS Code (`stdio`)

Add `@modelscript/mcp` to `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, or `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "modelscript": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelscript/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "MODELSCRIPT_API_URL": "http://localhost:3000"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Hosted Enterprise Hub (`SSE`)

For cloud agents, CI review bots, and multi-tenant teams, connect to the ModelScript Hub's authenticated SSE gateway (`/api/v1/mcp/sse`) using a user JWT or scoped `ms_bot_*` service token:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "modelscript-cloud": {
      "url": "https://hub.example.com/api/v1/mcp/sse",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ms_bot_live_9f8e7d6c5b4a..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Grounding Context Windows with `/llms.txt`

When prompting an LLM outside of MCP (or seeding system prompts for custom agents), point the model at **`https://modelscript.org/llms.txt`**. It is generated directly from the compiler's CLI definitions, language registry, and linter catalogs during every documentation build.

---

## 2. Core Agentic Engineering Workflows

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent as AI Agent (Claude / Cursor)
    participant MCP as @modelscript/mcp (52 Tools)
    participant Core as WASM GLR + Salsa + DAE Arena
    participant Verify as 13 Theory Oracles & Solvers

    Agent->>MCP: 1. modelica_lint / sysml2_check_constraints
    MCP->>Core: Parse CST & evaluate 794 static lint rules
    Core-->>Agent: Structured diagnostics (line, col, rule, fix)
    Agent->>MCP: 2. modelscript_closed_loop_synthesize
    MCP->>Verify: Flatten DAE -> Integrate -> Check STL robustness
    Verify-->>MCP: Counterexample trace (overshoot = 8.4% at t = 0.42s)
    MCP-->>Agent: Actionable gradient & counterexample feedback
    Agent->>MCP: 3. modelica_diff_calibrate (L-BFGS / Adam)
    MCP->>Verify: Optimize parameters & re-verify contracts
    Verify-->>Agent: Certified SAFE + SHA-256 Proof Manifest
```

### Workflow A: Autonomous Closed-Loop Physical Synthesis

Rather than writing a Modelica controller in one shot and hoping it stabilizes the plant, instruct the agent to call **`modelscript_closed_loop_synthesize`**. This single tool orchestrates a five-stage compiler/solver loop:

1. **GLR Parse & Semantic Lint** (`modelica_lint` across 307 Modelica rules)
2. **Arena DAE Flattening & Pantelides Index Reduction** (`modelica_flatten`)
3. **Time-Domain Integration** (`modelica_simulate` via SUNDIALS CVODE/IDA or Radau IIA)
4. **Signal Temporal Logic (STL) Verification** (`sysml2_falsify_requirements`)
5. **Counterexample & Sensitivity Tuning**: Evaluates STL robustness $\rho$ and tunes designated control gains (`tunableParameters`) via IMC-PID and sensitivity refinement until all five verification gates pass.

**Example MCP Tool Call:**

```json
{
  "name": "modelscript_closed_loop_synthesize",
  "arguments": {
    "modelName": "ActiveSuspension",
    "modelicaSource": "model ActiveSuspension\n  parameter Real k_s = 18000;\n  parameter Real c_d = 1450;\n  ...\nend ActiveSuspension;",
    "sysmlSource": "requirement def <'REQ-RIDE-01'> PeakAccelerationBound {\n  require constraint { maxVerticalAccel <= 1.8 }\n}",
    "tunableParameters": ["Kp", "Ki", "Kd"],
    "stopTime": 5.0,
    "maxRepairIterations": 5
  }
}
```

---

### Workflow B: Differentiable Parameter Calibration Against Test Data

When you have experimental bench data or field telemetry in CSV format, the agent can call **`modelica_diff_calibrate`** to fit unknown physical parameters (such as friction coefficients, thermal resistances, or battery internal impedances) using forward-mode Automatic Differentiation (`DualNumber`) paired with **L-BFGS** or **Adam**:

```json
{
  "name": "modelica_diff_calibrate",
  "arguments": {
    "modelName": "LithiumIonCell",
    "sourceCode": "model LithiumIonCell ... end LithiumIonCell;",
    "targetCsv": "time,v_terminal\n0.0,4.18\n10.0,4.09\n20.0,4.02\n...",
    "parameters": [
      { "name": "R_internal", "initial": 0.05, "min": 0.005, "max": 0.25 },
      { "name": "C_dl", "initial": 1200.0, "min": 100.0, "max": 5000.0 }
    ],
    "optimizer": "lbfgs",
    "maxIterations": 60,
    "tolerance": 1e-5
  }
}
```

After calibration converges, ask the agent to invoke **`modelica_sensitivity`** to inspect local identifiability and confidence intervals around the calibrated operating point.

---

### Workflow C: Bidirectional SysML v2 $\leftrightarrow$ Modelica TGG Synchronization

When a systems engineer adds a port or updates a mass budget in `.sysml` while a controls engineer edits equations in `.mo`, the digital thread can diverge. AI agents resolve cross-domain drift deterministically using three TGG & Theory Coordinator tools:

1. **`validate_system_consistency`**: Cross-checks `.sysml` and `.mo` models (or runs the 13 Nelson-Oppen Domain Theory Oracles) to detect port topology mismatches, unit conflicts, and divergent shared parameter slots.
2. **`tgg_diagnose_conflict`**: Runs static Critical Pair Analysis (CPA) and inspects concurrent edits on Triple Graph Grammar correspondence nodes.
3. **`tgg_reconcile_slot`**: Applies a formal resolution policy (`source-wins`, `target-wins`, `physics-simplex`, or `interval_intersection`) and rewrites both ASTs losslessly.

```json
{
  "name": "tgg_reconcile_slot",
  "arguments": {
    "correspondenceId": "corr_ThermalCoolantLoop_maxPressure",
    "strategy": "interval_intersection",
    "sysmlPath": "architecture/ThermalSystem.sysml",
    "modelicaPath": "models/ThermalCoolantLoop.mo"
  }
}
```

---

### Workflow D: Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) & Suspect Link Auditing

Before cutting a release or generating an FDA / ISO 26262 Design History File (`msx dhf export`), an AI agent can audit the workspace's Requirements Traceability Matrix:

1. **`rtm_query_matrix`**: Queries all requirements, satisfying architecture/physics elements, verification test cases, coverage percentages, and suspect links (where a downstream `.mo` equation or `.step` CAD solid changed after the requirement was last verified).
2. **`rtm_diagnose_suspect`**: Computes the structural CST/DAE delta across the suspect link and recommends whether to re-run verification (`sysml2_verify`) or update the requirement bound.
3. **`rtm_export_reqif`**: Exports the synchronized traceability matrix to OMG ReqIF 1.2 (`.reqif`) for enterprise ALM import.

---

### Workflow E: Cross-Domain CAD/FEA Sizing, Legacy B2B Certification & Formal Safety

Beyond 1D system dynamics, `@modelscript/mcp` provides five cross-domain certification tools:

- **`cad_fea_closed_loop_size`**: Couples parametric 3D OpenSCAD/STEP geometry with tetrahedral FEA von Mises stress analysis and 3D BVH collision clearance checks, iteratively sizing ribs, walls, and fillets until structural safety factors hold.
- **`polyglot_migrate_and_verify_b2b`**: Transpiles legacy Simulink (`.slx`), SPICE (`.cir`), or Adams (`.adm`) models into balanced Modelica and SysML v2, then executes an ISO 26262 Part 6 Back-to-Back (B2B) trajectory equivalence proof with C99 SHA-256 codegen parity.
- **`ssp_diagnose_cosim_stability`**: Detects direct-feedthrough algebraic loops across multi-FMU SSP topologies, computes the Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) spectral radius $\rho(J_{\mathrm{ZOH}})$, and synthesizes FMI directional-derivative Newton relaxation schedules.
- **`formal_verify_safety_and_mcdc`**: Proves unbounded safety invariants via IC3/PDR and Sum-of-Squares (SOS) barrier certificates, and synthesizes DO-178C / ISO 26262 MC/DC independence-pair test vectors.
- **`twin_discover_sindy_and_rom`**: Runs Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy STLSQ) over hardware telemetry residuals to discover unmodeled physics terms and calibrate a real-time Reduced-Order Model (ROM).

---

## 3. Recommended Prompt Patterns for Engineers

Use these prompt templates with Claude Code or Cursor when working in a ModelScript workspace:

> ** Synthesis & Verification Prompt:**
> _"Create a Modelica model `DC_BuckConverter.mo` and a companion `BuckConverterReq.sysml` specifying a $12\text{ V} \to 5\text{ V}$ step-down converter with output voltage ripple $\le 50\text{ mV}$ and settling time $\le 4\text{ ms}$. Run `modelica_lint`, simulate with `modelica_simulate`, and iterate using `modelscript_closed_loop_synthesize` until `sysml2_verify` proves both requirements SAFE."_

> ** Legacy Migration Prompt:**
> _"Import `legacy/PitchActuator.slx` into `models/PitchActuator.mo` using `polyglot_migrate_and_verify_b2b`, run `modelica_lint` to resolve any diagnostic warnings, and verify that the step response matches the Simulink reference trajectory within $10^{-4}$ relative error."_

> ** Grid Compliance Prompt:**
> _"Run `pscad_lint` and `pscad_verify_ieee2800` on `grid/WindFarm_300MW.pscx`. If Low-Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT) reactive current response time $T_{\text{resp}}$ exceeds $30\text{ ms}$, adjust the inverter inner current loop gains and re-run `pscad_verify_ieee2800` until all IEEE Std 2800-2022 clauses pass."\_

# CI/CD & GitHub Actions

Because every ModelScript artifact — from Modelica equations and SysML v2 requirements to PSCAD schematics and STEP geometry — is stored as text in Git, your entire cyber-physical digital thread can be linted, simulated, formally verified, and packaged inside standard CI/CD pipelines.

All `msx` CLI commands return strict POSIX exit codes (`0` = pass/proven safe, `1` = lint error/counterexample falsified, `2` = usage error) and respect `NO_COLOR=1` in non-interactive runners.

---

## 1. Continuous Verification Pipeline Overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    PR["Git Push / Pull Request"] --> Lint["1. Polyglot Static Lint<br/>(msx lint --format json)"]
    Lint --> Diff["2. Visual & Semantic PR Diff<br/>(msx pr-diff --format pr-comment)"]
    Diff --> Verify["3. Formal Contract & STL Proofs<br/>(msx verify --format sarif)"]
    Verify --> SARIF["GitHub Code Scanning<br/>(Upload results.sarif)"]
    Verify --> Artifacts["4. Release Artifacts<br/>(msx fmu / msx dhf export)"]
```

| Stage                      | Command                                        | Output Format                             | Purpose                                                                                                 |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Static Analysis**        | `msx lint ./models ./requirements`             | `json`, `text`                            | Enforces 794 static syntax, type, unit, and structural rules across 44 languages.                       |
| **Cross-Domain Alignment** | `msx polyglot verify .`                        | Terminal / Exit Code                      | Verifies `@satisfies` / `@verifies` bindings and cross-language port compatibility.                     |
| **Visual PR Review**       | `msx pr-diff --base origin/main`               | `pr-comment`, `visual-svg`, `visual-html` | Generates color-coded schematic diffs (added = green, modified = amber, deleted = red).                 |
| **Formal Verification**    | `msx verify <Class> <file> --format sarif`     | `sarif`, `junit`, `ctrf`, `html`, `dhf`   | Runs $\text{CDCL}(\mathcal{T})$ SMT, IC3/PDR, and flowpipe proofs; integrates with GitHub Security tab. |
| **STL Falsification**      | `msx falsify --modelica <file> --sysml <file>` | Counterexample trace JSON                 | Searches parameter and disturbance spaces via CMA-ES / Differential Evolution for safety violations.    |
| **Deliverables & DHF**     | `msx fmu` & `msx dhf export`                   | `.fmu`, `.md`, `.html`, `.json`           | Packages FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation FMUs and signed FDA 21 CFR Part 820 / ISO 26262 DHF dossiers.            |

---

## 2. Complete GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/modelscript-ci.yml`)

Copy the workflow below into `.github/workflows/modelscript-ci.yml` to run polyglot linting, upload **SARIF 2.1.0** formal verification proofs to **GitHub Code Scanning**, post automated **Visual PR Diff** summaries on pull requests, and archive **FMI 3.0 FMUs** and **Regulatory DHF Dossiers**:

```yaml
name: ModelScript Digital Thread CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  security-events: write

env:
  NO_COLOR: "1"

jobs:
  verify-digital-thread:
    name: Lint, Verify & Package Digital Thread
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository with full history for PR diffs
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Install @modelscript/cli and start warm compiler daemon
        run: |
          npm install -g @modelscript/cli
          msx daemon start

      - name: 1. Polyglot Static Linting
        run: |
          msx lint ./models ./architecture --daemon

      - name: 2. Verify Cross-Language Digital Thread Links
        run: |
          msx polyglot verify . --daemon

      - name: 3. Formal Contract Verification (SARIF + JUnit)
        run: |
          msx verify BrakingController models/BrakingController.mo \
            --format sarif \
            --report results.sarif \
            --daemon

      - name: Upload SARIF Proof Report to GitHub Code Scanning
        if: always()
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: results.sarif
          category: modelscript-formal-verification

      - name: 4. Generate Visual & Semantic Pull Request Diff
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: |
          msx pr-diff \
            --base origin/${{ github.base_ref }} \
            --format pr-comment \
            -o pr-diff-comment.md
          msx pr-diff \
            --base origin/${{ github.base_ref }} \
            --format visual-svg \
            -o visual-diff.svg

      - name: 5. Build FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation FMU & Regulatory DHF Dossier
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          msx fmu BrakingController models/BrakingController.mo \
            --fmi-version 3 \
            --type cs \
            --wasm \
            --output dist/BrakingController.fmu
          msx dhf export ./models ./architecture \
            --format html \
            -o dist/design-history-file.html
          msx dhf audit ./models ./architecture

      - name: Upload FMU, Visual Diff & DHF Artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: modelscript-release-bundle
          path: |
            dist/BrakingController.fmu
            dist/design-history-file.html
            results.sarif
            visual-diff.svg
```

---

## 3. Visual & Semantic Pull Request Diffs (`msx pr-diff`)

Traditional text diffs struggle to convey the engineering impact of rewired acausal connectors or altered SysML v2 internal block diagrams. `msx pr-diff` parses both the base revision (`--base`) and head revision (`--head`) into CSTs and flattened DAEs, computing:

- **Structural & Equation Delta**: Added, removed, or re-typed components, modified parameter bindings, and changed differential equations (ignoring whitespace or comment reformatting).
- **Breaking Interface Detection (`--breaking-only`)**: Flags removed public connectors, narrowed requirement constraint intervals, or altered causal input/output signatures with exit code `1`.
- **Color-Coded Visual Schematics (`--format visual-svg` / `visual-html`)**: Renders an overlay schematic highlighting added blocks in green, modified parameters in amber, and deleted connections in red.

```bash
# Generate a Markdown summary table for GitHub / GitLab PR comments
msx pr-diff --base origin/main --format pr-comment -o pr-summary.md

# Render a standalone interactive HTML schematic comparison
msx pr-diff models/Powertrain.mo --base HEAD~1 --format visual-html -o diff.html

# Fail CI if a pull request introduces breaking port or contract changes
msx pr-diff --base origin/main --breaking-only
```

---

## 4. Domain-Specific Compliance Gates

In addition to general Modelica and SysML v2 verification, you can gate pull requests on industry-specific homologation standards:

### Power Grid Interconnection (IEEE Std 2800-2022)

```bash
# Lint PSCAD EMT schematics and verify LVRT/HVRT ride-through compliance
msx pscad lint grid/SolarPlant_250MW.pscx
msx pscad verify-ieee2800 grid/SolarPlant_250MW.pscx --tstop 3.0 --step 20us -o ieee2800.json
```

### Railway Vehicle Running Safety (EN 14363 / UIC 518)

```bash
# Lint GENSYS railway vehicle model and emit a SARIF homologation report
msx gensys lint rail/HighSpeedBogie.calc
msx gensys report rail/HighSpeedBogie.calc --format sarif --out en14363.sarif
```

### Subsea Flow Assurance (OLGA Severe Slugging & Hydrate Margins)

```bash
# Lint and verify MAOP, hydrate subcooling margin, and erosional velocity limits
msx olga lint subsea/Tieback.opi
msx olga verify subsea/Tieback.opi
```

## 5. Offloading Heavy Campaigns to Cloud HPC (`msx cloud`)

When a CI pipeline needs to run a 10,000-shot Monte Carlo uncertainty study or a multi-hour 3D CFD/FEA co-simulation, dispatch the job to a remote Slurm HPC cluster using `MODELSCRIPT_API_URL` and `MODELSCRIPT_TOKEN`:

```bash
# Dispatch a high-CPU simulation job to the ModelScript Cloud Slurm cluster
msx simulate ThermalGrid models/ThermalGrid.mo \
  --cloud \
  --profile high-cpu \
  --stop-time 3600 \
  --output-dir ./artifacts/thermal

# Or inspect and download artifacts from an asynchronous cloud job
msx cloud status job_01j8x9k2m
msx cloud download job_01j8x9k2m ./artifacts
```

# Embedding Artifacts & Models

The **ModelScript Embed Service** allows you to embed interactive 2D schematics, 3D CAD/STEP models, simulation trajectory charts, and editable playgrounds directly into external websites, blogs, Notion, and documentation portals.

---

## 1. Quick Start: Web Component (`<modelscript-viewer>`)

The simplest and cleanest way to embed a ModelScript model in any modern web page or documentation framework is using the custom Web Component:

```html
<script type="module" src="https://modelscript.org/static/embed.js"></script>

<modelscript-viewer
  dialect="modelica"
  view="diagram"
  anchor="R1"
  code="model RLC
  Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Basic.Resistor R1(R=100);
  Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Basic.Capacitor C1(C=1e-6);
equation
  connect(R1.p, C1.n);
end RLC;"
>
</modelscript-viewer>
```

### Supported Attributes

| Attribute     | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                    |
| :------------ | :------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dialect`     | `"modelica"`   | Language dialect: `"modelica"`, `"sysml2"`, `"step"`, `"scad"`, `"pscad"`, `"olga"`, `"csv"`.                                                  |
| `view`        | `"diagram"`    | Initial visual mode: `"diagram"`, `"cad"`, `"plot"`, `"code"`, `"split-columns"`.                                                              |
| `anchor`      | `undefined`    | Target component element ID to visually highlight and auto-center (e.g. `"R1"` or `"chassis"`).                                                |
| `controls`    | `"none"`       | Set to `"parameters"` to display an interactive live parameter slider ribbon below the model.                                                  |
| `zoom-mode`   | `"ctrl-wheel"` | Scroll protection mode: `"ctrl-wheel"` (requires Ctrl/⌘ to zoom, preventing iframe page wheel-trapping), `"always"`, or `"click-to-interact"`. |
| `multi-file`  | `false`        | If set, the watermark pill routes the user to the **ModelScript IDE** instead of the Playground.                                               |
| `artifact-id` | `undefined`    | Numerical ID of a published artifact on the ModelScript Hub.                                                                                   |

---

## 2. Zero-Config `<iframe>` Embed

For Markdown documents, Notion, or environments where custom scripts are restricted, use an `<iframe>` with a compressed `#m=...` permalink hash:

```html
<iframe
  src="https://embed.modelscript.org/?view=diagram&theme=dark#m=<compressed-token>"
  width="100%"
  height="500"
  frameborder="0"
  allow="clipboard-write"
>
</iframe>
```

---

## 3. Programmatic JavaScript SDK (`@modelscript/embed`)

For full programmatic control in React, Vue, Svelte, or vanilla TypeScript applications, install the client package:

```bash
npm install @modelscript/embed
```

```typescript
import { ModelScriptEmbed } from "@modelscript/embed";

const embed = new ModelScriptEmbed({
  container: "#viewer-container",
  dialect: "modelica",
  view: "diagram",
  anchor: { elementId: "R1" },
  code: `model Example ... end Example;`,
});

// React to user interactions inside the embed
embed.on("ANCHOR_CLICKED", ({ anchor }) => {
  console.log("User focused element:", anchor.elementId);
});

// Update model code or trigger simulation dynamically
embed.setCode(`model Updated ... end Updated;`);
embed.triggerSimulate({ stopTime: 10.0 });
```

---

## 4. React Component SDK (`@modelscript/react`)

For native React applications, `@modelscript/react` provides first-class components and hooks for engineering inspection:

```bash
npm install @modelscript/react
```

```tsx
import { BlackboxInspector, StepResponseTestbench, useCWasmCompiler } from "@modelscript/react";

export function SimulationDashboard({ fmuBuffer }: { fmuBuffer: ArrayBuffer }) {
  const { compile, isCompiling } = useCWasmCompiler();

  return (
    <div className="dashboard-grid">
      {/* Live inspection of FMU variables, inputs, and outputs */}
      <BlackboxInspector
        buffer={fmuBuffer}
        onVariableChange={(name, val) => console.log(`Param ${name} updated to ${val}`)}
      />

      {/* Dynamic step response testbench with automatic settling time & overshoot metrics */}
      <StepResponseTestbench
        buffer={fmuBuffer}
        inputVariable="voltage_in"
        outputVariable="speed_out"
        stepMagnitude={10.0}
        stopTime={5.0}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

---

## 5. Accelerated Rehydration (`IndexedDB`)

When loading models that depend on standard libraries (such as the Modelica Standard Library or KerML), `@modelscript/embed` utilizes pre-baked binary symbol tables (`.sym.bin`):

```typescript
import { PackageRehydrationCache } from "@modelscript/embed";

// Retrieves from local IndexedDB in <15ms or streams from CDN on cache miss
const symbolBuffer = await PackageRehydrationCache.loadOrFetch("Modelica", "4.0.0");
```

This bypasses parsing thousands of library classes on every page load, which substantially reduces startup time.

---

## 6. Live Parameter Slider Ribbon

Embeds can be made dynamically interactive without opening full code editors. Pass `controls="parameters"` or append `?controls=parameters` to any embed URL:

```html
<modelscript-viewer
  dialect="modelica"
  view="plot"
  controls="parameters"
  code="model RC
  parameter Real R = 100 \"Resistance\";
  parameter Real C = 1e-4 \"Capacitance\";
  Real v(start=5.0);
equation
  der(v) = -v / (R * C);
end RC;">
</modelscript-viewer>
```

The viewer automatically extracts top-level parameters from the model code, renders sleek glassmorphic range sliders with real-time numeric inputs, and re-executes simulations upon user adjustments with built-in 300ms debouncing.

---

## 7. Universal oEmbed API & Rich Social Cards

ModelScript embeds implement the standard [oEmbed specification](https://oembed.com/) (`GET /api/v1/oembed`), enabling drop-in interactive previews in Notion, Discord, Slack, and WordPress.

### Auto-Discovery

Every ModelScript post (`https://modelscript.org/p/:id`) includes standard auto-discovery `<link>` tags in the HTML header:

```html
<link
  rel="alternate"
  type="application/json+oembed"
  href="https://api.modelscript.org/api/v1/oembed?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmodelscript.org%2Fp%2F123&format=json"
  title="ModelScript Interactive Model"
/>
```

### Direct oEmbed Query

Clients can query the oEmbed endpoint directly using either a post URL or a playground permalink hash (`#m=...`):

```bash
curl "https://api.modelscript.org/api/v1/oembed?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmodelscript.org%2F%23m%3DeJy...&maxwidth=800&format=json"
```

Response:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "type": "rich",
  "provider_name": "ModelScript",
  "provider_url": "https://modelscript.org",
  "title": "Interactive Model Simulation",
  "width": 800,
  "height": 500,
  "html": "<iframe src=\"https://embed.modelscript.org/?embed=true#m=eJy...\" width=\"100%\" height=\"500\" frameborder=\"0\" loading=\"lazy\" allow=\"clipboard-write\" style=\"border-radius:12px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1);max-width:800px;\"></iframe>"
}
```

---

## 8. WebGL Context Management & Mobile Scroll Protection

To guarantee rock-solid stability when multiple 3D CAD or WebGPU viewers exist on the same page:

- **Context Pooling (`CanvasContextPool`):** Restricts active WebGL contexts to 6 on mobile/Safari and 8 on desktop. Inactive canvases automatically sleep and display an ultra-crisp WebP raster snapshot with a glassmorphic `🧊 Click to re-activate 3D` overlay pill.
- **Scroll Hijacking Protection:** Embeds intercept wheel events and require holding `Ctrl` (Windows/Linux) or `⌘` (macOS) to zoom, displaying a non-intrusive badge hint if scrolling is attempted without the key.
- **Mobile Touch Passthrough:** Single-finger dragging vertically passes straight through to scroll the host webpage; two-finger pinch and drag gestures control 3D orbit and dolly zoom.

# Platform Administration & Enterprise Hub Guide

The **ModelScript Enterprise Hub** (`@modelscript/api`, `@modelscript/web`, and `@modelscript/ee`) provides a self-hostable or cloud-managed control plane for polyglot package management, Git Smart HTTP hosting, OMG SysML v2 / Semantic Web APIs, Slurm HPC simulation offload, operational digital twins, and cryptographically verifiable regulatory compliance.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Community (`MSX_EDITION=ce`) vs. Enterprise Edition (`MSX_EDITION=ee`)**:
> The core package registry, Git server, GraphQL/SPARQL endpoints, and local simulation runtime are licensed under **AGPL-3.0-or-later**. Enterprise subsystems located in `ee/` (`@modelscript/ee`) — including Corporate SAML/OIDC SSO & Org RBAC (`saml_oidc_sso`), Air-Gap NERC CIP / FERC CEII & ITAR/EAR Compliance (`airgap_compliance`), FDA 21 CFR Part 11 DHF Attestations (`dhf_attestation`), Slurm HPC & Compute Billing (`slurm_hpc`), Operational Digital Twins & Historian (`digital_twins`), Digital Thread Governance (`digital_thread_governance`), OMG SysML v2 REST (`sysml2_omg_api`), Hosted MCP SSE Gateway (`mcp_sse_gateway`), Real-Time HIL Codegen (`hil_codegen`), and Enterprise PLM/CAE Connectors (`plm_connectors`) — are licensed under `LicenseRef-ModelScript-Enterprise` and verified offline via an Ed25519-signed `MSX_LICENSE_KEY`.

---

## 1. First-Run Install Wizard (`/setup`), Console & Staff RBAC

### First-Run Install Wizard (`/setup`) & Headless Bootstrap

When a new ModelScript instance is deployed without an existing administrator account (`needsSetup: true` on `GET /api/v1/instance/banner` and `GET /api/v1/setup/status`), the web UI displays a `[FIRST-BOOT SETUP]` banner and provides a guided 4-step **First-Run Install Wizard** at `/setup`:

1. **Deployment Architecture Profile & Migration Restore**:
   - **Tier 1: Independent Federated Node** (`invite_only` registration, `open` ActivityPub S2S federation, `3` report auto-quarantine threshold).
   - **Tier 2: Corporate Intranet / Air-Gapped Appliance** (`domain_allowlist` registration, `disabled` outbound federation, `14` hot backup retention).
   - **Tier 3: Public Flagship Hub** (`open` registration with anti-Sybil verification, `open` federation, `30` hot backup retention).
   - **Optional Migration Restore**: Upload a Portable Instance Migration Bundle (`.json`) directly in Step 1 to clone settings, federation policies, feature flags, and quarantines from a prior instance.
2. **Founding Administrator Account**: Creates the initial `admin` user (`1,000` initial compute credits) and provisions Ed25519 instance keys plus RSA-2048 ActivityPub actor keys.
3. **Instance Identity, Registration & Federation Policy**: Configures NodeInfo 2.0/2.1 metadata, email domain allowlists, and moderation auto-quarantine thresholds.
4. **Starter Invites & Baseline Snapshot**: Generates initial invitation codes, records a `first-boot-baseline` SQLite hot backup (`VACUUM INTO` + SHA-256), signs the founding admin in, and **permanently locks** `POST /api/v1/setup/complete` (`403 Forbidden` on any subsequent calls).

For automated GitOps / Helm / Ansible / Docker Compose deployments, setting `ADMIN_INIT_USERNAME` and `ADMIN_INIT_PASSWORD` (or `AUTO_SEED_ADMIN=true`) alongside `DEPLOYMENT_PRESET` (`tier3_flagship`, `tier2_corporate`, or `tier1_federated`) bootstraps the founding administrator headlessly on boot, applies the tier branding and federation policies, provisions cryptographic keys, and permanently locks the setup wizard without requiring any manual interaction.

### Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

Access to the Platform Administration Console (`/admin`) and `/api/v1/admin/*` endpoints is enforced via JWT authentication and tiered staff RBAC (`requireStaffRole`):

- **`admin`**: Full platform superuser privileges across all 9 Admin Console tabs (Moderation, Users & Credits, Analytics, Federation, DMCA & Quarantine, Audit Logs, Database & Backups, Feature Flags, Instance Settings & Invites, and System & License Posture).
- **`moderator`**: Trust & Safety access to the **Moderation Queue** (`/api/v1/admin/moderation/*`) and **Users & Governance** (`/api/v1/admin/users`, including User Forensic Dossiers). Cannot promote accounts to `admin`/`auditor` or mutate database/system settings.
- **`auditor`**: Read-only compliance inspector access to **Security & Audit Logs** (`/api/v1/admin/audit-logs`, hash-chain verification), **Analytics & Traffic** (`/api/v1/admin/analytics`), **System Health** (`/api/v1/admin/system`), and **Enterprise Compliance Posture** (`/api/v1/admin/ee/posture`).
- **`user` / Organization Roles (`owner`, `admin`, `member`, `billing`, `viewer`)**: Scoped access within `/api/v1/organizations/:org` namespaces.

### Instance Admin Console Tabs (`/admin`)

1. **Moderation Queue**: Enriched forensic snapshots, keyboard-driven triage (`j`/`k` navigate, `x` select, `r` resolve, `d` dismiss), bulk resolution, content warnings (`mark_sensitive`), ActivityPub `Delete` tombstone broadcast, outbound `Flag` forwarding, and automated report-threshold quarantine (`autoQuarantineReportThreshold`).
2. **Users & Governance**: Global status breakdown (`active`, `frozen`, `suspended`, `admins`, `moderators`, `auditors`), role promotion (`user` | `moderator` | `auditor` | `admin`), session token revocation, HPC compute credit grants/deductions (`POST /api/v1/admin/users/:id/credits`), and slide-over **User Forensic Dossiers** (`GET /api/v1/admin/users/:id/forensics`).
3. **Analytics & Traffic**: First-party privacy-preserving pageview rollups across `web` and `docs` surfaces, bot filtering, geographic heatmaps, and retention pruning.
4. **Federation Domains & S2S Queue**: Domain policy tiers (`allow`, `silence`, `suspend`), consortium `allowlist` mode, Mastodon/Oliphant CSV & JSON blocklist import/export, live WebFinger + NodeInfo peer connectivity tester, S2S JSON payload inspector, and ActivityPub `Move` (`alsoKnownAs`) migration broadcast.
5. **DMCA & Universal Resource Quarantine**: Public statutory takedown intake (`POST /api/v1/admin/dmca/notices`), universal resource quarantine across `post`, `package`, `repository`, and `artifact` targets, 17 U.S.C. § 512(g) counter-notice filing (14-day statutory window), and one-click restoration.
6. **Security & Audit Logs**: Cryptographic SHA-256 hash-chained audit ledger (`GET /api/v1/admin/audit-logs/verify`) with hash-preserving GDPR IP redaction (`POST /api/v1/admin/audit-logs/redact-expired`, replacing expired raw IPs with `REDACTED:<ipToken>` without breaking chain verification).
7. **Database, Backups & Migration**: Live schema migration dry-run/upgrade, `PRAGMA` relational & physical integrity checks, online SQLite WAL `VACUUM INTO` snapshots with SHA-256 checksums, `.db` snapshot download, point-in-time online restore (with automatic `pre-restore` safety snapshot), retention pruning, and portable instance migration bundles (`/api/v1/admin/bundle/export` & `/import`).
8. **Instance Settings & Registration Invites**: Dynamic NodeInfo 2.0/2.1 branding (`instanceName`, `instanceDescription`, `contactEmail`), registration policy (`open`, `invite_only`, `domain_allowlist`, `closed`), multi-use registration invite codes with initial compute credit and role grants, and a live global announcement / multi-tiered maintenance mode banner (`/api/v1/instance/banner`).
9. **System Health & Enterprise Posture**: Live storage & SQLite WAL telemetry, HPC job queue counters, GeoIP/Mailer readiness, and (in Enterprise Edition) Air-Gap / FERC CEII / ITAR compliance posture.

### Multi-Tiered Maintenance Mode, Step-Up Sudo & Prometheus Metrics

- **Multi-Tiered Maintenance Mode (`off` | `scheduled` | `read_only` | `lockdown`)**:
  - Configurable dynamically via `PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings` (`maintenanceMode` and `maintenanceEta`) or via environment variables (`MSX_MAINTENANCE_MODE`, `MSX_MAINTENANCE_ETA`).
  - `scheduled` surfaces a countdown banner on `/api/v1/instance/banner`; `read_only` blocks non-admin `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` requests with `503 Service Unavailable` and `Retry-After` headers while keeping read/download routes online; `lockdown` restricts all non-admin traffic during major maintenance windows.
- **Step-Up Sudo Mode (`POST /api/v1/admin/sudo` & `REQUIRE_ADMIN_SUDO=true`)**:
  - Re-verifies the administrator's password or TOTP code and mints a 15-minute `admin_sudo` JWT token (`X-Admin-Sudo-Token`) required when `REQUIRE_ADMIN_SUDO=true` for high-impact mutations (role changes, database restores, bundle imports, and DMCA restorations).
- **Prometheus & OpenMetrics Telemetry (`GET /api/v1/admin/metrics`)**:
  - Exposes real-time instance metrics in standard Prometheus `text/plain; version=0.0.4` format (`modelscript_process_memory_bytes`, `modelscript_db_size_bytes`, `modelscript_users_total`, `modelscript_packages_total`, `modelscript_federation_activities_total`, `modelscript_hpc_jobs_total`, `modelscript_moderation_open_reports`).

### Headless CLI Database, Diagnostics & Backup Management (`msx db`)

```bash
msx db status                                  # View current schema version and pending migrations
msx db upgrade [--dry-run]                     # Apply pending migrations with automatic pre-flight snapshot
msx db verify                                  # Run PRAGMA foreign_key_check & integrity_check
msx db doctor                                  # Deep health check (SQLite, audit hash-chain, disk headroom)
msx db support-bundle --file support.json      # Export redacted diagnostic support bundle (zero secrets)
msx db backup [--label pre-release]            # Create online SQLite WAL snapshot with SHA-256 digest
msx db backups                                 # List available snapshots, sizes, and SHA-256 digests
msx db restore --file modelscript-backup-..db  # Verify integrity & perform online point-in-time restore
msx db prune [--keep 7]                        # Prune older snapshots while retaining latest N
msx db export-bundle --file bundle.json        # Export portable instance migration bundle + snapshot
msx db import-bundle --file bundle.json        # Import settings, federation rules, flags & quarantines
```

## 2. Runtime Feature Flags & Progressive Rollouts

ModelScript includes an in-memory and database-backed **Feature Flag Engine** (`apps/api/src/services/feature-flag-service.ts`) that allows operators to toggle experimental compilers, cloud solvers, or UI capabilities at runtime without redeploying containers.

### Flag Evaluation Precedence

1. **Environment Variable Override**: Setting `FEATURE_FLAG_<UPPER_SNAKE_KEY>=true|false` (for example, `FEATURE_FLAG_WEBGPU_CLOUD_SOLVER=true`) overrides database state for deterministic staging/CI configuration.
2. **Role Gate (`allowedRoles`)**: If a flag specifies `allowedRoles` (e.g., `["admin", "moderator"]`), only authenticated users holding one of those roles receive `true`.
3. **Deterministic Percentage Rollout (`rolloutPercentage`)**: When `0 < rolloutPercentage < 100`, the service computes a deterministic hash over `(flagKey, userId)` so a given user receives a consistent cohort experience across sessions.

### Administrative Flag Endpoints

| Method & Endpoint                | Access        | Description                                                                                                                                                          |
| :------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/v1/flags`              | Public / User | Evaluate all feature flags for the current caller's `userId` and `role`.                                                                                             |
| `GET /api/v1/admin/flags`        | `admin`       | List all registered feature flags with full rollout metadata, role gates, and environment override states.                                                           |
| `PATCH /api/v1/admin/flags/:key` | `admin`       | Dynamically update `enabled` (`boolean`), `rolloutPercentage` (`0`–`100`), `allowedRoles` (`string[]`), or `description`, and record an immutable admin audit event. |

## 3. Enterprise Authentication, SSO, 2FA & Bot Accounts

The authentication subsystem (`/api/v1/auth`, `/api/v1/auth/sso`, `/api/v1/auth/2fa`, `/api/v1/bots`) supports defense-in-depth enterprise identity requirements:

- **OpenID Connect (OIDC) & SAML Enterprise SSO (`/api/v1/auth/sso`)**: Connect Okta, Azure AD / Entra ID, Keycloak, or Google Workspace identity providers with automatic Just-in-Time (JIT) organization provisioning and group-to-role mapping.
- **TOTP Two-Factor Authentication (`/api/v1/auth/2fa`)**: RFC 6238 Time-Based One-Time Password enrollment (QR code provisioning, backup recovery codes, and mandatory 2FA enforcement policies per organization).
- **Machine & CI/CD Bot Accounts (`/api/v1/bots`)**: Provision scoped, non-interactive service accounts bearing `ms_bot_*` API tokens with granular permissions (`package:read`, `package:publish`, `cloud:dispatch`, `mcp:invoke`, `dhf:export`) and automatic token rotation schedules.
- **Signed Outbound Webhooks (`/api/v1/webhooks`)**: Subscribe external CI/CD pipelines to workspace events (`package.published`, `simulation.completed`, `verification.failed`, `twin.anomaly_detected`) signed with HMAC-SHA256 (`X-ModelScript-Signature-256`).

## 4. Native Git Smart HTTP Server & Content-Addressable Registry

The Hub integrates both a **Git Smart HTTP Backend** and a **Signed Content-Addressable Package Registry**:

### Native Git Smart HTTP Server (`/git/:namespace/:project` & `/api/v1/git-server`)

Engineers can clone, fetch, branch, and push polyglot model repositories using standard `git` clients over HTTPS:

```bash
git clone https://hub.example.com/git/aerospace/flight-control.git
```

- Supports `git-upload-pack` (`GET /info/refs?service=git-upload-pack`) and `git-receive-pack` (`POST /git-receive-pack`) authenticated via Basic Auth (`username` + PAT or `ms_bot_*` token).
- Pre-receive hooks optionally enforce zero-error `msx lint` checks and Digital Thread correspondence verification before accepting pushes to protected branches.

### Cryptographic Package Signing & Multi-Lens Manifests (`/api/v1/packages`)

Every package published via `msx publish` is stored in a SHA-256 Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) blob store and signed with the publisher's **Ed25519** private key:

- **Integrity & Provenance**: `msx install --verify-signatures` validates both the SHA-256 tarball digest against `modelscript.lock` and the Ed25519 signature against the registry's public keyring.
- **Multi-Lens Manifest Projection (`GET /api/v1/packages/:name/:version?lens=<lens>`)**: The registry dynamically projects any `modelscript.json` package manifest into three industry interoperability schemas on the fly:
  - `?lens=npm`: Standard Node/NPM-compatible package metadata for JavaScript/TypeScript tooling.
  - `?lens=aas`: **IDTA Asset Administration Shell (AAS v3.0)** JSON submodel descriptor containing `TechnicalData` and `SimulationModels` (FMU) references.
  - `?lens=okh`: **DIN SPEC 3105 / OSHWA Open Know-How (OKH v1.0)** hardware manifest exposing CAD/ECAD bill-of-materials, manufacturing files, and SPDX license metadata.

## 5. Standards-Compliant Systems & Semantic Web APIs

The Hub natively implements open MBSE and Semantic Web specifications so external enterprise tools can query models without proprietary adapters:

| API Surface                 | Base Path                             | Standard / Capabilities                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| :-------------------------- | :------------------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **OMG SysML v2 REST API**   | `/api/v1/sysml2` (and root `/` alias) | Implements the **OMG Systems Modeling API and Services v2.0** specification: `/projects`, `/projects/{id}/commits`, `/projects/{id}/branches`, `/projects/{id}/tags`, `/projects/{id}/commits/{cid}/elements`, and `/relationships`. |
| **GraphQL Library API**     | `/api/v1/libraries/graphql`           | Strongly typed GraphQL schema for querying packages, Modelica classes, ports, equations, physical units, and dependency graphs in a single round-trip.                                                                               |
| **W3C RDF Serialization**   | `/api/v1/libraries/rdf`               | Exports package and workspace ontologies as `text/turtle`, `application/ld+json`, or `application/n-triples`.                                                                                                                        |
| **W3C SPARQL 1.1 Endpoint** | `/api/v1/libraries/sparql`            | Executes SPARQL 1.1 `SELECT`, `CONSTRUCT`, and `ASK` queries with optional OWL 2 RL entailment reasoning over indexed engineering libraries.                                                                                         |
| **OSLC 3.0 & TRS 3.0**      | `msx oslc serve` / `/api/v1/threads`  | Exposes OASIS OSLC Requirements (`oslc_rm`) and Architecture (`oslc_am`) catalogs with Tracked Resource Set (TRS 3.0) incremental change logs for IBM DOORS Next and Polarion synchronization.                                       |

## 6. Cloud Slurm HPC Offload, CAE Sweeps & Compute Credit Billing

When engineers run `msx simulate --cloud` or `msx cloud dispatch`, the Hub orchestrates containerized batch execution across Slurm HPC clusters or Kubernetes GPU pools:

- **Cloud Simulation & CAE Endpoints (`/api/v1/cloud` & `/api/v1/cae`)**:
  - Dispatches single-run stiff DAE simulations, multi-thousand-run Monte Carlo ensembles, SU2 CFD runs, and CalculiX FEA jobs to isolated worker nodes.
  - Streams live progress events and solver logs via WebSockets (`/ws`) and persists output trajectories (`CSV`, `Parquet`, `VTK`, `FRD`) to S3-compatible object storage.
- **Compute Credit Wallet & Stripe Billing (`/api/v1/billing`)**:
  - Each user or organization maintains an ACID transactional **Compute Credit Wallet**.
  - Job submission places a pre-authorization hold (`reserveCredits`) based on the requested hardware profile (`standard`, `high-cpu`, `gpu-a100`, `slurm-mpi`); upon completion or cancellation (`msx cloud cancel`), exact wall-clock consumption is settled and unused credits are refunded.
  - Supports self-service credit top-ups via Stripe Checkout webhooks (`/api/v1/billing/webhook`) or manual enterprise quota allocation by platform admins.

## 7. Digital Thread Hash-Chained Audit Ledger & Operational Digital Twins

For safety-critical industries (aerospace DO-178C, automotive ISO 26262, medical FDA 21 CFR Part 11 / 820, and nuclear IEC 61513), the Hub maintains a tamper-evident digital thread and live twin telemetry pipeline:

### Cryptographic Hash-Chained Audit Ledger (`/api/v1/threads/audit-log`)

Every mutation to a requirement, model equation, TGG alignment link, verification proof, or administrative setting is appended to a PostgreSQL audit ledger where each record $k$ stores:

$$H_k = \text{SHA256}\bigl(H_{k-1} \;\|\; \text{timestamp}_k \;\|\; \text{actorId}_k \;\|\; \text{action}_k \;\|\; \text{payloadHash}_k\bigr)$$

Operators and external auditors can verify the unbroken integrity of the entire historical chain at any time via the CLI or REST API:

```bash
# Verify cryptographic hash-chain integrity across the PostgreSQL audit ledger
msx db verify

# Export and verify a signed Design History File (DHF) compliance archive
msx dhf export ./workspace -o release_v1.dhf.md
msx dhf audit release_v1.dhf.md
```

### Operational Digital Twins (`/api/v1/twins` & `/api/v1/instances`)

- **Asset Instance Registry (`/api/v1/instances`)**: Tracks serialized physical assets in the field (e.g., tail numbers, inverter serial IDs, or battery packs) bound to specific immutable commits of their ModelScript digital twin.
- **Live Telemetry & Drift Detection (`/api/v1/twins`)**: Ingests time-series sensor telemetry via REST/WebSockets, executes an online Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) / moving-horizon observer against the compiled WASM DAE arena, and triggers automated alerts when physical parameter drift or residual anomalies exceed safety thresholds.

## 8. Hosted MCP SSE Gateway (`/api/v1/mcp`)

Enterprise teams can connect cloud AI agents and internal copilot orchestrators directly to the Hub's **Hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) Gateway**:

- **`GET /api/v1/mcp/sse`**: Authenticates via Bearer token (`JWT` or `ms_bot_*`) and opens a server-sent events transport session.
- **`POST /api/v1/mcp/messages`**: Dispatches any of the [31 MCP engineering tools](../reference/mcp-and-ide.md) inside sandboxed worker isolates with automatic compute credit metering and full audit-ledger logging of every AI tool invocation.

## 9. Deployment & Self-Hosting Runbook

ModelScript publishes distinct **Community Edition (`-ce`)** and **Enterprise Edition (`ee`)** container images to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io/modelscript/*`). Choose the deployment scenario below that matches your environment.

| Container Image                 |                   Edition                    |      `/app/ee` Included?      | Default Environment                                                                               | Target Scenario                                          |
| :------------------------------ | :------------------------------------------: | :---------------------------: | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ghcr.io/modelscript/api-ce`    |         **CE** (`AGPL-3.0-or-later`)         | **No** _(physically omitted)_ | `MSX_EDITION=ce`                                                                                  | Self-Hosted Community Edition                            |
| `ghcr.io/modelscript/cli-ce`    |         **CE** (`AGPL-3.0-or-later`)         | **No** _(physically omitted)_ | `MSX_EDITION=ce`                                                                                  | Open-core CI/CD runner                                   |
| `ghcr.io/modelscript/api`       | **EE** (`LicenseRef-ModelScript-Enterprise`) |            **Yes**            | `MSX_EDITION=ee`, `MSX_LICENSE_ENFORCE=true`                                                      | Corporate EE Cluster & `modelscript.org` Cloud           |
| `ghcr.io/modelscript/cli`       | **EE** (`LicenseRef-ModelScript-Enterprise`) |            **Yes**            | `MSX_EDITION=ee`, `MSX_LICENSE_ENFORCE=true`                                                      | Licensed Enterprise CI/CD & HIL codegen runner           |
| `ghcr.io/modelscript/appliance` | **EE** (`LicenseRef-ModelScript-Enterprise`) |            **Yes**            | `MSX_EDITION=ee`, `MSX_LICENSE_ENFORCE=true`, `ENTERPRISE_APPLIANCE=true`, `AIRGAP_ENFORCED=true` | Single-container Air-Gapped Intranet Appliance (`:8080`) |
| `ghcr.io/modelscript/web`       |                    Shared                    |              N/A              | Nginx SPA (`/`) + VitePress Docs (`/docs`) + IDE (`/ide`)                                         | Web UI, IDE Launcher & Unified Documentation Portal      |

---

### Scenario A: Self-Hosted Community Edition (`MSX_EDITION=ce`)

For individual engineers, universities, and open-source teams running under **GNU AGPLv3** without a commercial license key:

- Uses `ghcr.io/modelscript/api-ce:latest` (which physically excludes `/app/ee`) or sets `MSX_EDITION=ce`.
- Includes the full 44-language compiler, DAE simulation engine, local package registry, public repositories, GraphQL/RDF queries, Web IDE, and the core **Instance Admin Console** (`/admin` and `/api/v1/admin/*` for content moderation, federation domain governance, DMCA takedowns, audit logs, and online SQLite backups).
- Enterprise-only endpoints (`/api/v1/ee/*`, `/api/v1/admin/stats`, `/api/v1/admin/ee/*`, `/api/v1/organizations`, `/api/v1/cae`, `/api/v1/cloud`, `/api/v1/twins`, `/api/v1/cosim`, `/api/v1/threads`, `/api/v1/sysml2`, `/api/v1/mcp`, `/api/v1/webhooks`, etc.) return `501 Not Implemented`.

```bash
# Option 1: Run the physically isolated Community Edition API container directly
docker run -d \
  --name modelscript-api-ce \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -e JWT_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  -v modelscript-data:/app/apps/api/data \
  ghcr.io/modelscript/api-ce:latest

# Option 2: Run the full multi-container stack (Caddy + API + Web) in Community Edition mode
export MSX_EDITION=ce
export JWT_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
export PUBLIC_DOMAIN=localhost
docker compose --profile standalone up -d
```

---

### Scenario B: Corporate Self-Hosted Enterprise Edition (`MSX_EDITION=ee`)

For regulated utilities, civil aerospace manufacturers, medical device companies, and enterprise engineering organizations holding a signed `msx_lic_<payloadBase64Url>.<ed25519SigBase64Url>` license key.

#### B.1 Single-Container Air-Gapped Intranet Appliance (Recommended for Isolated Enclaves / NERC CIP / Cleanrooms)

Bundles the API server, `@modelscript/ee`, Web SPA, Unified Documentation Portal (`/docs`), and Web IDE into a single hardened container on port `8080` with zero outbound network dependencies:

```bash
# 1. On an internet-connected bastion, pull and export the appliance image for offline transfer
docker pull ghcr.io/modelscript/appliance:latest
docker save ghcr.io/modelscript/appliance:latest | gzip > modelscript-appliance.tar.gz

# 2. Inside the air-gapped enclave, load and start the appliance with your offline license token
docker load < modelscript-appliance.tar.gz

docker run -d \
  --name modelscript-appliance \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  -e MSX_EDITION=ee \
  -e MSX_LICENSE_ENFORCE=true \
  -e MSX_LICENSE_KEY="msx_lic_<PAYLOAD>.<SIGNATURE>" \
  -e JWT_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  -v modelscript-data:/app/apps/api/data \
  -v modelscript-uploads:/app/apps/api/uploads \
  ghcr.io/modelscript/appliance:latest
```

Or via Docker Compose using [`ee/deploy/docker-compose.yml`](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/blob/main/ee/deploy/docker-compose.yml) or the root `appliance` profile:

```bash
export MSX_LICENSE_KEY="msx_lic_<PAYLOAD>.<SIGNATURE>"
export JWT_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
docker compose --profile appliance up -d
```

#### B.2 Corporate Multi-Container Stack (with Caddy TLS, MQTT Unified Namespace & TimescaleDB Historian)

For corporate intranet clusters running live Operational Digital Twins, distributed FMI/MQTT co-simulation, and TimescaleDB telemetry historians:

```bash
cp .env.production.example .env.enterprise
# Edit .env.enterprise:
#   PUBLIC_DOMAIN=modelscript.corp.internal
#   PUBLIC_URL=https://modelscript.corp.internal
#   MSX_EDITION=ee
#   MSX_LICENSE_ENFORCE=true
#   MSX_LICENSE_KEY=msx_lic_<PAYLOAD>.<SIGNATURE>
#   JWT_SECRET=<64-hex-secret>

docker compose --env-file .env.enterprise --profile federated up -d
```

#### B.3 Kubernetes StatefulSet Deployment

Apply the hardened Kubernetes manifest at [`ee/deploy/kubernetes-appliance.yaml`](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/blob/main/ee/deploy/kubernetes-appliance.yaml) (pre-configured as a single-writer `StatefulSet` (`replicas: 1`) with `runAsNonRoot: true`, `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault`, RFC 1918 `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS`, and a strict zero-egress `NetworkPolicy`):

```bash
kubectl create namespace modelscript-system
kubectl -n modelscript-system create secret generic modelscript-enterprise-secrets \
  --from-literal=license-key="msx_lic_<PAYLOAD>.<SIGNATURE>" \
  --from-literal=jwt-secret="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
kubectl apply -f ee/deploy/kubernetes-appliance.yaml
```

#### B.4 Verifying Enterprise License & Compliance Readiness

```bash
# Verify Ed25519 license status and enabled feature entitlements
curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ee/license/status | jq .

# Verify NERC CIP / FERC CEII air-gap compliance posture
curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/v1/compliance/airgap | jq .
```

### Scenario C: Official `modelscript.org` & `ansatz.social` Cloud Production Deployment

`modelscript.org` and `ansatz.social` run on a shared multi-container **Enterprise Edition** stack via [`docker-compose.yml`](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/blob/main/docker-compose.yml) + [`docker-compose.prod.yml`](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/blob/main/docker-compose.prod.yml) (`--profile flagship` or `--profile federated`) behind Caddy automatic multi-domain TLS (`PUBLIC_DOMAIN=ansatz.social`, `DOCS_DOMAIN=modelscript.org`). Host-based routing in Nginx serves the **Unified VitePress Documentation & PDF Manual** (`/` and `/docs`, `/guide/*`, `/ansatz/*`, `/languages/*`, `/pricing`) on `modelscript.org` and the **Ansatz Federated Web SPA** (`/`, `/home`, `/explore`, `/packages`, `/repos`, `/playground`) on `ansatz.social`, alongside the WebGPU IDE (`/ide`, `/vscode`) and Enterprise API (`/api/*`, `/git/*`).

#### C.1 Initial Server Provisioning (`/opt/modelscript`)

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /opt/modelscript/config
cd /opt/modelscript

# Copy docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.prod.yml, config/Caddyfile, config/mosquitto.conf, config/init-timescaledb.sql
cp .env.production.example .env.production
chmod 600 .env.production

# Edit .env.production to set production secrets:
#   PUBLIC_DOMAIN=ansatz.social
#   DOCS_DOMAIN=modelscript.org
#   PUBLIC_URL=https://ansatz.social
#   CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://ansatz.social,https://modelscript.org,https://ide.ansatz.social,https://ide.modelscript.org
#   MSX_EDITION=ee
#   MSX_LICENSE_ENFORCE=true
#   MSX_LICENSE_KEY=<pre-minted modelscript-cloud-prod Ed25519 token>
#   JWT_SECRET=<production-64-char-hex-secret>
#   TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<production-64-char-hex-key>
#   STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_...
#   STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...

# Pull prebuilt GHCR images and launch the production stack
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml \
  --env-file .env.production --profile flagship pull

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml \
  --env-file .env.production --profile flagship up -d --wait --remove-orphans
```

#### C.2 Automated CI/CD Rollouts (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` & `.github/workflows/release.yml`)

Every push to `main` and every tagged release in GitHub Actions builds and pushes all 6 Docker images (`api`, `api-ce`, `web`, `cli`, `cli-ce`, `appliance`) to `ghcr.io/modelscript/*` (tagged with both `:sha-<commit>` / `:<version>` and `:latest`) and triggers the `deploy_production` rollout job under a shared `production-deploy` concurrency lock. Before rolling out new containers, the deployment job executes an online SQLite `VACUUM INTO` snapshot inside the running `api` container (`/app/apps/api/data/backups/pre-deploy-<timestamp>.db`). Configure either SSH or Webhook secrets in GitHub repository settings:

| GitHub Secret                          | Description                                                                                  |
| :------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PROD_SSH_HOST`                        | Hostname or IP of the shared `modelscript.org` / `ansatz.social` production server           |
| `PROD_SSH_USER`                        | Deployment SSH user (with `docker` group permissions)                                        |
| `PROD_SSH_KEY`                         | Ed25519 private SSH key for `PROD_SSH_USER`                                                  |
| `PROD_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS` _(optional)_    | Pinned SSH host key entry for `PROD_SSH_HOST` (falls back to `ssh-keyscan` if omitted)       |
| `PROD_DEPLOY_PATH`                     | Directory on the production host (defaults to `/opt/modelscript`)                            |
| `PROD_ENV_FILE` _(optional)_           | Complete content of `.env.production` to automatically write and secure on the host          |
| `PROD_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL` _(optional)_ | Webhook URL if triggering rollouts via an external orchestrator (Portainer / Coolify / Argo) |
| `PROD_DEPLOY_TOKEN` _(optional)_       | Bearer token for `PROD_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL`                                                   |

#### C.3 Issuing & Verifying Customer License Keys (Maintainer Runbook)

The offline Ed25519 license keypair generator and token signer lives in `ee/src/cli/license-cli.ts`:

```bash
# 1. Generate a new Ed25519 keypair (stored in .keys/, which is gitignored)
npm run ee:keygen -- --out-dir=.keys

# 2. Mint a signed offline customer license token
npm run ee:sign-license -- \
  --private-key=.keys/msx-license-private.pem \
  --org="Acme Aerospace Corp" \
  --tier=appliance \
  --seats=100 \
  --days=365 \
  --out=.keys/acme-aerospace.license.json

# 3. Verify any license token offline against the embedded production public key
npm run ee:verify-license -- msx_lic_<PAYLOAD>.<SIGNATURE>
```
