# Cellier-Elmqvist Algebraic Loop Tearing

**Implementation**: `TornBlock` in [`packages/runtime/src/wasm/structural/tearing.ts`](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/tree/main/packages/runtime/src/wasm/structural/tearing.ts)

---

## Academic Citations

- **Cellier, F. E. (1979)**. _Combined Continuous/Discrete System Simulation by Use of Digital Computers: Techniques and Tools_.  
  **PhD thesis, ETH Zurich**.  
  DOI: [10.3929/ethz-a-000179979](https://doi.org/10.3929/ethz-a-000179979)
- **Elmqvist, H., & Otter, M. (1994)**. _"Methods for Tearing Systems of Equations in Object-Oriented Modeling."_  
  **Proceedings of the European Simulation Multiconference (ESM'94)**, pp. 326–332.
- **Mahana, P. N., & Eagan, J. P. (1975)**. _"A tearing algorithm for large systems of equations."_  
  **IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems**.

---

## ModelScript Architectural Rationale

Even after BLT partitioning, physical systems containing closed kinematic loops, electrical bridge circuits, or multi-phase fluid balances yield coupled Strongly Connected Components of size $N > 1$.

Solving an $N$-dimensional non-linear system via Newton-Raphson requires inverting an $N \times N$ Jacobian matrix at every iteration:

$$\mathcal{O}(N^3)$$

The Cellier-Elmqvist Minimum Degree Tearing algorithm identifies a minimal set of $k$ **tearing variables** ($k \ll N$) such that assuming known values for these $k$ variables breaks all cyclic dependencies in the block. The remaining $N - k$ inner variables can then be evaluated sequentially via a causal explicit forward substitution chain:

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{\text{inner}} &= g(x_{\text{tear}}, u) \quad \text{(explicit chain)} \\
R(x_{\text{tear}}) &= f_{\text{residual}}(x_{\text{tear}}, x_{\text{inner}}) = 0 \quad \text{(small $k \times k$ solve)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The non-linear iterative solver is restricted to the tiny $k \times k$ residual system, accelerating simulation speed by orders of magnitude.

---

## ModelScript Modifications & WASM Architecture

1. **Unmanaged WebAssembly Kernel**: Implemented as `@unmanaged` classes directly in linear memory with zero garbage collection pauses.
2. **Dynamic Minimum Degree Heuristic**: Evaluates vertex degrees in the block incidence graph in memory, prioritizing linear tearing variables over non-linear variables to avoid non-linear solving where possible.
3. **Partitioned In-Memory Structures**: Splits the block into:
   - $k$ tearing variables (`tearVarIndices`)
   - $N - k$ explicit causal equations (`innerEqIndices`)
   - $k$ residual constraint equations (`residualEqIndices`)
4. **Direct Matrix Integration**: Emits residual Jacobians directly to the in-WASM LU factorizer (`luFactor`, `luSolve`).

---

## Algorithm Steps

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SCC["Coupled SCC Block (Size N > 1)"] --> DEG["1. Calculate Incidence Degrees<br/>Count variable occurrences across block equations"]
    DEG --> SELECT["2. Minimum Degree Variable Selection<br/>Select variable v_tear with lowest degree (preferring linear)"]
    SELECT --> TEAR["3. Tear Variable v_tear<br/>Add to k tearing set; remove from active incidence graph"]
    TEAR --> CAUSAL{"Are any equations now solvable with degree 1?"}
    CAUSAL -->|Yes| PROPAGATE["4. Causal Forward Substitution<br/>Solve explicit variable and back-substitute into remaining equations"]
    PROPAGATE --> CAUSAL
    CAUSAL -->|No, but equations remain| SELECT
    CAUSAL -->|No, all N-k variables resolved| RESID["5. Formulate Residual System R(x_tear) = 0<br/>k equations become residual constraints"]
```

---

## Upstream & Downstream Pipeline Connections

- **Upstream Inputs**:
  - Receives coupled SCC blocks of size $> 1$ from [`BltEngine`](./blt.md).
- **Downstream Consumers**:
  - Feeds explicit forward chains and $k \times k$ residual systems to the in-WASM Newton-Raphson solver and [`Sparse LU Solver`](./surrogates-linear-algebra.md).
  - Evaluated inside simulation step loops ([`SUNDIALS`](./solvers-ode-dae.md), [`TR-BDF2`](./solvers-ode-dae.md), [`Tsit5`](./solvers-ode-dae.md)).

## 1. Tsitouras 5(4) Adaptive Runge-Kutta (Tsit5)

### Academic Citations

- **Tsitouras, Ch. (2011)**. _"Runge-Kutta pairs of order 5 (4) satisfying only the first column simplifying assumption."_  
  **Computers & Mathematics with Applications**, 62(2), pp. 770–775.  
  DOI: [10.1016/j.camwa.2011.06.002](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.camwa.2011.06.002)
- **Rackauckas, C., & Nie, Q. (2017)**. _"DifferentialEquations.jl – A Performant and Feature-Rich Ecosystem for Solving Differential Equations in Julia."_  
  **Journal of Open Research Software**, 5(1), 15. DOI: [10.5334/jors.151](https://doi.org/10.5334/jors.151)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

For non-stiff systems (e.g. mechanical multi-body dynamics, kinematics, flight control), high-order adaptive explicit Runge-Kutta pairs offer peak throughput without Newton-Raphson linear algebra costs. Tsit5 demonstrates significantly lower error coefficients and wider stability regions than classical Dormand-Prince (DOPRI5).

- **Modifications**: Employs the First-Same-As-Last (FSAL) optimization eliminating stage 1 evaluation in successive steps; embeds a 5th-order continuous dense output polynomial for sub-interval event zero-crossing localization.

## 2. TR-BDF2 Composite Stiff Solver

### Academic Citations

- **Bank, R. E., Coughran, W. M., et al. (1985)**. _"Transient simulation of silicon devices and circuits."_  
  **IEEE Transactions on CAD of Integrated Circuits**, 4(4), pp. 436–446.  
  DOI: [10.1109/TCAD.1985.1270142](https://doi.org/10.1109/TCAD.1985.1270142)
- **Hosea, M. E., & Shampine, L. F. (1996)**. _"Analysis and implementation of TR-BDF2."_  
  **Applied Numerical Mathematics**, 20(1-2), pp. 21–37.  
  DOI: [10.1016/0168-9274(95)00115-8](<https://doi.org/10.1016/0168-9274(95)00115-8>)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Cyber-physical models featuring frequent hybrid discrete events (switches, impacts, hysteresis) severely penalize multistep BDF solvers (which must drop to order 1 after every event). TR-BDF2 is an L-stable one-step composite method pairing a trapezoidal half-step with a BDF2 completion step:

- **Modifications**: Shares the diagonal Jacobian coefficient $d = 1 - 1/\sqrt{2}$ across both internal stages, requiring only **one** sparse LU factorization per time step; connects directly with ModelScript's in-WASM sparse matrix kernel (`sparse_lu.ts`).

## 3. RODAS-4P Linearly Implicit Rosenbrock Solver

### Academic Citations

- **Steinebach, G. (1995)**. _"Order-reduction of ROW-methods for DAEs and method of lines applications."_

- **Hairer, E., & Wanner, G. (1996)**. _Solving Ordinary Differential Equations II: Stiff and Differential-Algebraic Problems_.  
  **Springer-Verlag**. Section IV.8.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Solves stiff index-1 DAEs and method-of-lines continuum discretizations without iterative non-linear Newton solves. It solves only a sequence of linear systems sharing the same system matrix $I - \gamma h J$.

- **Modifications**: Optimized for in-WASM sparse Jacobian caching; utilizes automatic differentiation coloring (`coloring.ts`) for fast Jacobian updates.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Physical systems operate under thermal noise, turbulence, and sensor fluctuations:
$$dx = f(t, x) \, dt + g(t, x) \, dW_t$$

- **Modifications**: Employs an in-WASM `Xoshiro256pp` PRNG with Box-Muller transformation; provides both fixed-step Euler-Maruyama (strong order 0.5) and adaptive Rößler SRIW1 (strong order 1.5) integrators for Monte Carlo uncertainty rollouts.

## 6. Dommel Companion-Circuit EMT & Bergeron Traveling-Wave Solver

### Academic Citations

- **Dommel, H. W. (1969)**. _"Digital Computer Solution of Electromagnetic Transients in Single- and Multiphase Networks."_  
  **IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems**, PAS-88(4), pp. 388–399.  
  DOI: [10.1109/TPAS.1969.292459](https://doi.org/10.1109/TPAS.1969.292459)
- **Marti, J. R. (1982)**. _"Accurate Modelling of Frequency-Dependent Transmission Lines in Electromagnetic Transient Simulations."_  
  **IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems**, PAS-101(1), pp. 147–157.  
  DOI: [10.1109/TPAS.1982.317332](https://doi.org/10.1109/TPAS.1982.317332)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Implemented in `EmtSolver` (`packages/simulate/src/solvers/emt/emt-solver.ts`), this solver targets microsecond-scale electromagnetic transients, power electronics switching (IGBTs/breakers), and distributed transmission lines imported from `@modelscript/pscad`:

- **Trapezoidal Companion Models & Constant Nodal Matrix**: Inductors ($G_L = \frac{\Delta t}{2L}$) and capacitors ($G_C = \frac{2C}{\Delta t}$) are discretized into Norton companion equivalents $\mathbf{G}\mathbf{v}(t) = \mathbf{i}_{\text{hist}}(t - \Delta t) + \mathbf{i}_{\text{src}}(t)$, allowing $\mathbf{G}$ to remain constant between switching events.
- **Critical Damping Adjustment (CDA)**: Automatically transitions from Trapezoidal to Backward Euler integration ($G_L = \frac{\Delta t}{L}, G_C = \frac{C}{\Delta t}$) for two half-steps ($\Delta t / 2$) immediately after any breaker or semiconductor switching discontinuity to suppress artificial $dv/dt$ numerical oscillations.
- **Bergeron Traveling-Wave Line Decoupling & Norton FMU Interface**: Distributed transmission lines with propagation delay $\tau = \ell / v \ge \Delta t$ decouple the nodal admittance matrix into independent sub-grids using interpolated history ring buffers, and expose `getNortonEquivalent(portNode)` ($I_{\text{eq}}, G_{\text{eq}}$) for zero-delay FMI Co-Simulation coupling.

## 7. High-Order Taylor Model Flowpipe Integration

### Academic Citations

- **Makino, K., & Berz, M. (2003)**. _"Taylor Models and Other Validated Functional Inclusion Methods."_  
  **International Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics**, 4(4), pp. 379–456.
- **Chen, X., Ábrahám, E., & Sankaranarayanan, S. (2013)**. _"Flow\*: An Analyzer for Non-Linear Hybrid Systems."_  
  **Computer Aided Verification (CAV 2013)**, LNCS vol. 8044, pp. 258–263.  
  DOI: [10.1007/978-3-642-39799-8_18](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-39799-8_18)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Implemented in `TaylorModel` (`packages/runtime/src/analysis/wasm_taylor_model.ts`), validated Taylor Model arithmetic bounds all trajectories of a non-linear ODE/DAE system subject to uncertain initial sets $x(0) \in X_0$ and parameter intervals without wrapping-effect blowup:

- **Polynomial + Interval Remainder Representation**: Represents each state reachable tube over normalized domain $\mathbf{z} \in [-1, 1]^d$ as a multivariate polynomial $P_k(\mathbf{z})$ of order $k$ plus a sound interval remainder $I = [\underline{r}, \overline{r}]$, where truncated higher-order terms ($> k$) are conservatively swept into $I$.
- **Picard-Lindelöf Validated Operator**: Evaluates the contractive Picard integral operator $\mathcal{P}(X)(t) = X_0 + \int_0^t f(s, X(s))\,ds$ directly on Taylor models to construct guaranteed continuous-time flowpipes consumed by `ContinuousSafetyOracle` and SysML v2 hybrid state-machine reachability (`hybrid-flowpipe-bridge.ts`).

## ModelScript Architectural Rationale

Numerical finite-difference approximations ($\frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}$) suffer from a fundamental trade-off: large step sizes $h$ cause truncation errors, while small step sizes cause catastrophic floating-point cancellation.

ModelScript implements an integrated suite of **exact differentiation and continuous bounding engines** inside WebAssembly linear memory:

1. **Forward-Mode Dual Numbers**: Computes exact machine-precision directional derivatives $\nabla f(x) \cdot v$ concurrently with primal function evaluation for Newton steps in algebraic loops and stiff ODE/DAE integrators without allocating expression trees.
2. **Reverse-Mode Computational Tape**: Evaluates scalar objective gradients $\nabla f(x) \in \mathbb{R}^N$ with cost proportional to $O(1)$ evaluations of $f$, enabling gradient-based parameter estimation and surrogate neural network training.
3. **CPR Distance-2 Graph Coloring**: For large-scale DAE systems ($N = 10{,}000+$ equations), evaluating the full $N \times N$ Jacobian naively requires $N$ forward passes. CPR distance-2 coloring partitions structural columns into $p \ll N$ non-interfering groups (typically $p \le 15$ for sparse physical networks), reducing Jacobian assembly time by orders of magnitude.
4. **McCormick Envelopes & Affine Arithmetic**: Classical interval arithmetic suffers from the **dependency problem**: evaluating $x - x$ for $x \in [0, 1]$ yields $[-1, 1]$ instead of $0$, causing rapid exponential bounding blowup. Affine arithmetic tracks first-order noise symbols ($\epsilon_i \in [-1, 1]$) across state equations, while McCormick relaxations compute rigorous convex lower bounds ($f^R$) and concave upper bounds ($f^{AR}$) for non-convex global optimization.
5. **Hybrid Adjoint Sensitivity with Saltation Matrices**: Standard continuous adjoint solvers break down across Modelica `when`/`reinit` events, impact mechanics, or switching surfaces because Dirac delta impulses arise at event-crossing times $t^*$. ModelScript propagates reverse-mode adjoints across non-smooth mode transitions using exact saltation matrix jump conditions alongside optional sigmoidal equation smoothing (`DAEEventRelaxer`).
6. **Aitken Dynamic $\Delta$-Relaxation**: Partitioned co-simulation of strongly coupled multi-physics domains (such as lightweight aerodynamic structures coupled to dense fluids or algebraic FMU loops) diverges under explicit Gauss-Seidel macro-steps due to the artificial added-mass effect. Dynamic vector Aitken acceleration stabilizes fixed-point iterations without requiring monolithic cross-FMU Jacobians.

---

## ModelScript Modifications & WASM Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    DAE["DAE Linear Arena Expressions"] --> FORWARD["Dual Numbers (16-byte Unmanaged)"]
    DAE --> TAPE["Reverse Adjoint Tape (32-byte Nodes)"]
    DAE --> SPARSITY["Bipartite Sparsity Graph"]
    SPARSITY --> COLORING["CPR Distance-2 Column Coloring"]
    COLORING --> COMPRESSED_JAC["Compressed Jacobian Seeds<br/>p << N Directional Passes"]
    FORWARD --> COMPRESSED_JAC
    COMPRESSED_JAC --> NEWTON["WASM Newton-Raphson Solver<br/>(TR-BDF2, Rodas-4P, Tearing)"]
    DAE --> RELAX["McCormick Envelopes & Affine Noise Form"]
    RELAX --> GLOBAL["Global Branch-and-Bound & HC4 Contractor"]
    DAE --> HYBRID_ADJ["HybridAdjointSolver<br/>Hermite Checkpoint Tape & Saltation Jumps"]
    DAE --> AITKEN["VectorAitkenRelaxation<br/>Coupled FSI & FMU Macro-Step Convergence"]
```

### 1. Zero-GC Dual Number Arithmetic

Represented as a 16-byte unmanaged struct (`@unmanaged`) in WASM memory:

```typescript
@unmanaged
export class Dual {
  val: f64; // Primal evaluation f(x)
  dot: f64; // Directional derivative f'(x) * v
}
```

All elementary operators ($+, -, \times, /$) and transcendental functions ($\sin, \cos, \exp, \log, \text{pow}$) are inlined without intermediate object allocation.

### 2. Linear Memory Computational Tape

The reverse-mode tape records operations into a flat 32-byte stride unmanaged array:
$$\text{Stride: } [\text{op: u32}, \text{left: u32}, \text{right: u32}, \text{aux: u32}, \text{valLo: u32}, \text{valHi: u32}, \text{gradLo: u32}, \text{gradHi: u32}]$$
During the reverse pass, adjoints are accumulated in topological order directly in linear memory:
$$\bar{x}_j \leftarrow \bar{x}_j + \bar{x}_i \cdot \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}$$

### 3. CPR Distance-2 Coloring Algorithm

Two columns $j$ and $k$ in the Jacobian $J$ are **structurally orthogonal** if they do not share any non-zero row entry:
$$\text{Row}(j) \cap \text{Row}(k) = \emptyset$$
The graph coloring algorithm:

1. Constructs the bipartite graph $B = (V_R, V_C, E)$ where edge $(i, j) \in E \iff \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j} \neq 0$.
2. Colors columns $V_C$ such that any pair of columns connected by a path of length 2 receives different colors.
3. Groups columns of color $c \in \{1, \dots, p\}$ into a perturbation vector $d^{(c)} = \sum_{j \in \text{Color}(c)} e_j$.
4. Computes the entire compressed Jacobian in exactly $p$ directional forward-mode passes:
   $$J \cdot d^{(c)} = \sum_{j \in \text{Color}(c)} J_{*, j}$$

### 4. McCormick Relaxations

For factorable bilinear products $z = x \cdot y$ over bounds $x \in [x^L, x^U]$ and $y \in [y^L, y^U]$, the convex underestimator $z^{cv}$ and concave overestimator $z^{cc}$ are:
$$z^{cv} = \max\left(x^L y + x y^L - x^L y^L, \; x^U y + x y^U - x^U y^U\right)$$
$$z^{cc} = \min\left(x^U y + x y^L - x^U y^L, \; x^L y + x y^U - x^L y^U\right)$$
ModelScript evaluates McCormick tuples $[z^{cv}, z^{cc}, \nabla z^{cv}, \nabla z^{cc}]$ directly on WASM arrays.

### 5. Hybrid Adjoint Sensitivity with Saltation Matrices (`hybrid-adjoint.ts`)

When a hybrid DAE trajectory crosses a discrete event surface $g(x(t^*), p) = 0$ with state reset map $x(t^{*+}) = h(x(t^{*-}), p)$ (such as Modelica `when` clauses, `reinit(x, expr)` impulses, or mechanical contact restitution), the forward sensitivity transition matrix undergoes a discontinuous rank-1 update governed by the **saltation matrix**:
$$\Xi = I + \frac{\left(f^+ - f^- - \frac{\partial h}{\partial t}\right) (\nabla_x g)^T}{(\nabla_x g)^T f^- + \frac{\partial g}{\partial t}}$$

`HybridAdjointSolver` (`solveHybridAdjoint` in `packages/simulate/src/core/hybrid-adjoint.ts`) implements a three-phase hybrid sensitivity pipeline:

1. **Forward Integration & Event Localization**: Integrates the primal DAE arena while streaming cubic Hermite segments into `DenseHermiteCheckpointTape`. Whenever an event indicator $h(t, x, p)$ changes sign across a step, a 20-iteration bisection root-finder isolates the exact crossing time $t_e$, records pre-event limits $(x^-, \dot{x}^-)$, applies the discrete reset map $x^+ = \Delta(x^-, p)$, and re-evaluates post-event derivatives $(x^+, \dot{x}^+)$.
2. **Adjoint Jump across Event Surfaces**: During backward Heun integration of the co-state $\lambda(t)$, crossing $t_e$ in reverse applies the transposed saltation jump condition to $\lambda(t_e^-)$ and accumulates the discrete event timing contribution into the parameter gradient $\frac{d\mathcal{L}}{dp}$:
   $$\lambda(t_e^-) = \left[\frac{\partial \Delta}{\partial x}\right]^T \lambda(t_e^+) + \frac{\left(\frac{d\Delta}{dt}\right)^- - \dot{x}^+}{\dot{h}^-} \nabla_x h(t_e^-)$$
   $$\Delta\left(\frac{d\mathcal{L}}{dp}\right) = \left[\frac{\partial \Delta}{\partial p}\right]^T \lambda(t_e^+) + \frac{\left(\frac{d\Delta}{dt}\right)^- - \dot{x}^+}{\dot{h}^-} \nabla_p h(t_e^-)$$
3. **Optional Sigmoidal Event Relaxation**: For models with dense chattering or non-smooth algebraic switches (`if`, `abs`, `min`, `max`), `HybridAdjointSolver` optionally invokes `DAEEventRelaxer` to smooth C0 discontinuities into $C^\infty$ sigmoidal transitions prior to adjoint integration.

### 6. Aitken Dynamic $\Delta$-Relaxation for Coupled Co-Simulation (`fsi-relaxation.ts`)

In partitioned Fluid-Structure Interaction (FSI) and multi-FMU co-simulation macro-steps, exchanging boundary loads and displacements via unrelaxed fixed-point iteration $x_{k+1} = \tilde{x}(x_k)$ often diverges due to artificial added-mass instability.

`VectorAitkenRelaxation` (`packages/simulate/src/core/fsi-relaxation.ts`) accelerates and stabilizes convergence over scalar variables, multi-DOF nodal displacement vectors, or 3D boundary traction maps (`relaxBoundaryLoads`):

1. **Fixed-Point Residual**: At macro-step sub-iteration $k$, computes the interface residual $r_k = \tilde{x}_k - x_{k-1}$ and residual difference $\Delta r_k = r_k - r_{k-1}$.
2. **Secant Aitken Factor Update**: Updates the dynamic relaxation factor $\omega_k$ via the multidimensional Aitken $\Delta^2$ projection:
   $$\omega_k = -\omega_{k-1} \frac{r_{k-1}^T (r_k - r_{k-1})}{\|r_k - r_{k-1}\|_2^2}$$
   clamped to a safe stability interval $\omega_k \in [\omega_{\min}, \omega_{\max}]$ (default $[0.02, 1.0]$).
3. **Relaxed State Update**: Advances the interface state via under-relaxation:
   $$x_{k+1} = x_k + \omega_k r_k$$
   terminating when the relative residual norm $\|r_k\|_2 / (\|x_k\|_2 + \epsilon) < \text{tol}$.
4. **Multi-Rate Sub-Cycling (`MultiRateSubCycleScheduler`)**: Synchronizes fast acoustic CFD steps ($\Delta t_{\text{CFD}} \sim 10^{-4}\text{ s}$), intermediate elastodynamic FEA steps ($\Delta t_{\text{FEA}} \sim 10^{-3}\text{ s}$), and macro 1D DAE steps ($\Delta t_{\text{macro}} \sim 10^{-2}\text{ s}$) using linear sub-step boundary interpolation $\mathbf{u}(\tau) = (1 - \tau)\mathbf{u}_{\text{prev}} + \tau \mathbf{u}_{\text{target}}$.

# Mathematical Optimization & Calibration Solvers

**Implementation**: [`packages/simulate/src/optimizer/solvers/`](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/tree/main/packages/simulate/src/optimizer/solvers/)

---

## 1. Limited-Memory BFGS with Bounds (L-BFGS-B)

### Academic Citations

- **Byrd, R. H., Lu, P., Nocedal, J., & Zhu, C. (1995)**. _"A limited memory algorithm for bound constrained optimization."_  
  **SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing**, 16(5), pp. 1190–1208. DOI: [10.1137/0916069](https://doi.org/10.1137/0916069)
- **Zhu, C., Byrd, R. H., Lu, P., & Nocedal, J. (1997)**. _"Algorithm 778: L-BFGS-B: Fortran subroutines for large-scale bound-constrained optimization."_  
  **ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software**, 23(4), pp. 550–560. DOI: [10.1145/279232.279236](https://doi.org/10.1145/279232.279236)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Solves large-scale bound-constrained non-linear minimization:
$$\min_{x \in \mathbb{R}^n} f(x) \quad \text{subject to } l \le x \le u$$
Crucial for parameter identification and direct collocation optimal control where thousands of discretized states and control bounds must be optimized.

- **Modifications**: Employs compact representation of the inverse Hessian approximation $H_k$ using history buffers $m \in [5, 20]$ in typed arrays; Cauchy point computation with piecewise linear path search; exact line search with strong Wolfe conditions.

---

## 2. Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES)

### Academic Citations

- **Hansen, N., & Ostermeier, A. (2001)**. _"Completely derandomized self-adaptation in evolution strategies."_  
  **Evolutionary Computation**, 9(2), pp. 159–195. DOI: [10.1162/106365601750190398](https://doi.org/10.1162/106365601750190398)
- **Hansen, N. (2016)**. _"The CMA Evolution Strategy: A Tutorial."_  
  **arXiv preprint**: [arXiv:1604.00772](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.00772).

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Derivative-free black-box optimization on rugged, non-convex, non-separable objective functions (e.g. tuning PID controller gains over simulations with discontinuous switching events).

- **Modifications**: Tracks full covariance matrix $C \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ updates with rank-$\mu$ and rank-one update mechanisms; vectorized population sampling using WebAssembly-accelerated Cholesky decomposition; step-size control using cumulative path lengths (CSA).

---

## 3. Differential Evolution (DE)

### Academic Citations

- **Storn, R., & Price, K. (1997)**. _"Differential Evolution – A Simple and Efficient Heuristic for global Optimization over Continuous Spaces."_  
  **Journal of Global Optimization**, 11(4), pp. 341–359. DOI: [10.1023/A:1008202821328](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1008202821328)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Stochastic population-based global search algorithm utilizing vector differences for directional perturbations. Highly effective for parameter estimation against experimental CSV test bench data.

- **Modifications**: Supports `rand/1/bin`, `best/1/bin`, and `current-to-best/1` mutation strategies with adaptive crossover probability ($CR$) and scaling factor ($F$).

---

## 4. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)

### Academic Citations

- **Kennedy, J., & Eberhart, R. (1995)**. _"Particle swarm optimization."_  
  **Proceedings of IEEE ICNN'95**, Vol. 4, pp. 1942–1948. DOI: [10.1109/ICNN.1995.488968](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICNN.1995.488968)
- **Shi, Y., & Eberhart, R. C. (1998)**. _"A modified particle swarm optimizer."_  
  **IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation**, pp. 69–73.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Simulates social swarm dynamics for continuous global search:
$$v_i(t+1) = w v_i(t) + c_1 r_1 (p_i - x_i) + c_2 r_2 (g - x_i)$$

- **Modifications**: Implements constriction factors and dynamically declining inertia weights $w(t)$ to transition smoothly from global exploration to local exploitation.

---

## 5. Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II)

### Academic Citations

- **Deb, K., Pratap, A., Agarwal, S., & Meyarivan, T. (2002)**. _"A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II."_  
  **IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation**, 6(2), pp. 182–197. DOI: [10.1109/4235.996017](https://doi.org/10.1109/4235.996017)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Solves multi-objective engineering trade-offs (e.g. simultaneously minimizing electric vehicle energy consumption while maximizing battery longevity and top speed).

- **Modifications**: Fast non-dominated sorting ($\mathcal{O}(M N^2)$ complexity) paired with crowding-distance assignment in continuous parameter spaces; outputs full Pareto fronts directly.

- **Downstream Consumers**:

  - Powers `msx cosim optimize` for black-box multi-FMU tuning across SSP boundaries.
  - Powers `ModelicaCalibrator` with `hybrid-cmaes-lm` (CMA-ES global exploration + Levenberg-Marquardt quadratic polishing).
  - Powers `TradeStudyEngine.evolve` for generative multi-objective Pareto design trade studies.

## Programmatic TypeScript API

```typescript
import { cmaesSolve, deSolve, psoSolve, nsga2Solve, type BlackBoxProblem } from "@modelscript/simulate/optimizer";

// 1. Single-Objective Black-Box Optimization (CMA-ES, DE, PSO)
const problem: BlackBoxProblem = {
  dimension: 2,
  bounds: {
    min: new Float64Array([-5, -5]),
    max: new Float64Array([5, 5]),
  },
  fitness: (x) => Math.pow(1 - x[0]!, 2) + 100 * Math.pow(x[1]! - x[0]! * x[0]!, 2),
};

const result = await cmaesSolve(problem, { maxGenerations: 100 });
console.log("Optimum:", result.bestSolution, "Cost:", result.bestFitness);

// 2. Hybrid Global-Local Model Calibration
import { ModelicaCalibrator } from "@modelscript/simulate/optimizer";

const calibrator = new ModelicaCalibrator(arena, sim, {
  parameters: ["k", "c"],
  parameterBounds: new Map([
    ["k", { min: 1, max: 30 }],
    ["c", { min: 0.1, max: 10 }],
  ]),
  measurements,
  method: "hybrid-cmaes-lm", // Global CMA-ES basin exploration + Levenberg-Marquardt refinement
});
const calResult = calibrator.calibrate();
```

## 1. Davis SuiteSparse Left-Looking Cholesky ($LL^T$)

### Academic Citations

- **Davis, T. A. (2006)**. _Direct Methods for Sparse Linear Systems_.  
  **SIAM**. DOI: [10.1137/1.9780898718881](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718881)
- **Chen, Y., Davis, T. A., Hager, W. W., & Rajamanickam, S. (2008)**. _"Algorithm 887: CHOLMOD, supernodal sparse Cholesky factorization and update/downdate."_  
  **ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software**, 35(3), pp. 22:1–22:14. DOI: [10.1145/1462166.1462176](https://doi.org/10.1145/1462166.1462176)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Solves symmetric positive-definite sparse systems $A x = b$ arising in finite element analysis, electrical mesh equations, and quadratic programming subproblems.

- **Modifications**: Left-looking column-by-column factorization computing non-zero patterns dynamically via elimination trees; operates inside unmanaged WebAssembly linear memory with zero heap fragmentation.

## 2. Gilbert-Peierls Left-Looking Sparse LU ($P A Q = L U$)

### Academic Citations

- **Gilbert, J. R., & Peierls, T. (1988)**. _"An approach to sparse LU factorization based on graph coloring and topological sort."_  
  **International Conference on Supercomputing**.
- **Davis, T. A. (2006)**. _Direct Methods for Sparse Linear Systems_. **SIAM**. Chapter 5.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Factorizes unsymmetric, highly irregular sparse Jacobians generated by torn physical DAE systems.

- **Modifications**: Depth-first search (DFS) topological ordering to find the exact non-zero structure of each column in $L$ and $U$ in time proportional to arithmetic operations; threshold partial pivoting with diagonal preference to preserve physical sparsity.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Computes numerically stable orthogonal factorizations $A P = Q R$ for rank-deficient least-squares calibration and parameter sensitivity studies.

## 4. Buchberger's Gröbner Basis Engine with Gebauer-Möller Criteria

### Academic Citations

- **Buchberger, B. (1965)**. _An Algorithm for Finding the Basis Elements of the Residue Class Ring of a Zero Dimensional Polynomial Ideal_.  
  **PhD thesis, University of Innsbruck**.
- **Gebauer, R., & Möller, H. M. (1988)**. _"On an installation of Buchberger's algorithm."_  
  **Journal of Symbolic Computation**, 6(2-3), pp. 275–286. DOI: [10.1016/S0747-7171(88)80048-8](<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0747-7171(88)80048-8>)
- **Cox, D., Little, J., & O'Shea, D. (2015)**. _Ideals, Varieties, and Algorithms_ (4th ed.).  
  **Springer**. DOI: [10.1007/978-3-319-16721-3](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-16721-3)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Solves small non-linear algebraic loops analytically to avoid numerical Newton iterations entirely. Computes the Gröbner basis under lexicographic monomial ordering ($\text{Lex}$) to triangularize polynomial systems into univariate root problems.

- **Modifications**: Implements the Gebauer-Möller criteria ($B_{\text{new}}$ and $M_{\text{new}}$ sets) to eliminate over 90% of redundant $S$-polynomial reduction checks; operates over exact rational coefficients $\mathbb{Q}$.

## 5. Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) / Snapshot SVD

### Academic Citations

- **Sirovich, L. (1987)**. _"Turbulence and coherence in Catherine's wheel: Method of snapshots."_  
  **Quarterly of Applied Mathematics**, 45(3), pp. 561–571. DOI: [10.1090/qam/910462](https://doi.org/10.1090/qam/910462)
- **Berkooz, G., Holmes, P., & Lumley, J. L. (1993)**. _"The proper orthogonal decomposition in the analysis of turbulent flows."_  
  **Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics**, 25, pp. 539–575. DOI: [10.1146/annurev.fl.25.010193.002543](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.fl.25.010193.002543)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Extracts reduced-order models (ROM) from massive 3D CFD or FEA simulation field snapshots ($N > 10^6$ nodes):
$$u(x, t) \approx \bar{u}(x) + \sum_{k=1}^r a_k(t) \phi_k(x)$$

- **Modifications**: Employs Sirovich's snapshot method to compute eigenvalues of the small $M \times M$ temporal correlation matrix ($M \ll N$ snapshots), retaining $99\%$ cumulative kinetic energy in $\le 16$ spatial modes.

## 7. Operational Digital Twin Estimation & Prognostics (`packages/simulate/src/twin/`)

### Academic Citations

  **IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control**, 48(2), pp. 246–258. DOI: [10.1109/TAC.2002.808470](https://doi.org/10.1109/TAC.2002.808470)
- **Julier, S. J., & Uhlmann, J. K. (2004)**. _"Unscented filtering and nonlinear estimation."_  
  **Proceedings of the IEEE**, 92(3), pp. 401–422. DOI: [10.1109/JPROC.2003.823141](https://doi.org/10.1109/JPROC.2003.823141)
- **Page, E. S. (1954)**. _"Continuous inspection schemes."_  
  **Biometrika**, 41(1/2), pp. 100–115. DOI: [10.2307/2333009](https://doi.org/10.2307/2333009)
- **Miner, M. A. (1945)**. _"Cumulative damage in fatigue."_  
  **Journal of Applied Mechanics**, 12(3), pp. A159–A164.

### ModelScript Architectural Overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    TELEM["Streaming Telemetry Window [t - W, t]"] --> MHE["MovingHorizonEstimator (arena-mhe.ts)<br/>Continuous DAE Adjoint + L-BFGS-B"]
    TELEM --> UKF["BayesianParameterCalibrator & ModelicaCalibrator<br/>Joint-State UKF / MCMC / Hybrid CMA-ES + LM"]
    MHE --> RESID["Innovation Residuals r(t) = y_meas - y_twin"]
    UKF --> RESID
    RESID --> CUSUM["CusumDriftDetector (drift-detector.ts)<br/>Two-Sided Page-Hinkley / CUSUM Test"]
    MHE --> TAPE["DenseHermiteCheckpointTape"]
    TAPE --> VSENS["VirtualSensorSynthesizer & RulPredictor (prognostics.ts)<br/>Arrhenius, Miner Fatigue & Log-Normal RUL (P10/P50/P90)"]
```

### 1. Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) over the Linear-Memory DAE Arena (`arena-mhe.ts`)

`MovingHorizonEstimator` reconciles streaming physical sensor windows (`TelemetryWindow` over $[t - W, t]$) against the in-memory `DAEBuilder` arena by solving a box-constrained trajectory-tracking problem:
$$\min_{\theta, w} \; \frac{1}{2} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \left\| y^{\text{sim}}(t_k; \theta, w) - y^{\text{meas}}(t_k) \right\|_2^2 + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i} \lambda_i (\theta_i - \theta_i^{\text{prior}})^2 + \frac{\lambda_w}{2} \| w - w^{\text{prior}} \|_2^2$$
$$\text{s.t.} \quad \theta_{\min} \le \theta \le \theta_{\max}, \quad F(\dot{x}, x, y, \theta, w, t) = 0$$

- **Joint Physical & Neural Hybrid Calibration**: Simultaneously estimates physical DAE parameters $\theta$ and embedded `ArenaNeuralBlock` surrogate weights $w$ inside the same optimization vector.
- **Adjoint-Driven L-BFGS-B**: Evaluates exact objective gradients via `DaeAdjointSolver` (`solveDaeAdjoint`) and converges in $\le 25$ quasi-Newton `lbfgsbSolve` iterations, automatically warm-starting initial states from window boundaries $t_0$.

### 2. Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) & Multi-Strategy Parameter Calibration (`calibrator.ts`, `bayesian_calibrator.ts`)

ModelScript provides two complementary calibration engines for offline test-stand identification and online probabilistic tracking:

- **Joint-State Unscented Kalman Filter (`BayesianParameterCalibrator`)**: Augments the continuous state vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^{N_x}$ with unknown physical parameters $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{N_p}$ into $z = [x^T, \theta^T]^T \in \mathbb{R}^{N_x + N_p}$. Propagates $2L + 1$ deterministic sigma points ($\alpha = 10^{-3}, \beta = 2, \kappa = 0$) through the nonlinear DAE transition $z_{k+1} = f_{\text{aug}}(z_k, u_k, \Delta t)$ and measurement model $y_k = h_{\text{aug}}(z_k)$ (`UnscentedKalmanFilter`), extracting full posterior covariance $P_{k|k}$, $95\%$ confidence intervals ($\hat{\theta}_i \pm 1.96 \sigma_i$), and automated Digital Thread hypergraph write-back suggestions.
- **Deterministic & Global Metaheuristic Calibration (`ModelicaCalibrator` in `calibrator.ts`)**: Supports Levenberg-Marquardt (`lm`) with damped normal equations $(J^T J + \lambda I)\Delta\theta = -J^T r$, Sequential Quadratic Programming (`sqp`) with BFGS Hessian updates, scalable adjoint `lbfgsb`, Bayesian MCMC / global evolutionary search (`cmaes`, `de`, `pso`), and two-stage `hybrid-cmaes-lm` global-to-local polishing.

### 3. Page-Hinkley / CUSUM Statistical Residual Drift Detection (`drift-detector.ts`)

`CusumDriftDetector` continuously monitors multi-channel innovation residuals $r_c(t) = y_{\text{meas}, c}(t) - y_{\text{twin}, c}(t)$ to detect incipient actuator degradation, sensor bias, or structural drift while rejecting zero-mean Gaussian measurement noise:

- **Two-Sided Sequential Cumulative Sum**: Normalizes each channel residual $\tilde{z}_c = (r_c - \mu_c) / \sigma_c$ with minimum detectable shift slack $k_c = \frac{\delta_c}{2 \sigma_c}$ (default $\delta_c = 1.5 \sigma_c$) and updates positive and negative CUSUM statistics:
  $$S_c^+(t) = \max\!\left(0, \; S_c^+(t-1) + \tilde{z}_c(t) - k_c\right), \qquad S_c^-(t) = \max\!\left(0, \; S_c^-(t-1) - \tilde{z}_c(t) - k_c\right)$$
- **Adaptive Burn-In & Severity Classification**: Supports empirical baseline calibration (`calibrateFromData`) and triggers structured `DriftEvent` alerts when $\max(S_c^+, S_c^-) \ge h_c$, classifying severity (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`) by threshold ratio $S_c / h_c$ alongside online shift magnitude estimation.

### 4. Virtual Sensor Synthesis & Remaining Useful Life (RUL) Prognostics (`prognostics.ts`)

- **Virtual Sensor Synthesis (`VirtualSensorSynthesizer`)**: Evaluates unobservable internal physical states (e.g., rotor hotspot temperatures, internal valve spool stresses) at arbitrary timestamps $t$ directly from the continuous `DenseHermiteCheckpointTape`.
- **Physics-of-Failure Damage Accumulation (`RulPredictor`)**: Computes instantaneous degradation rates $\frac{dD}{dt}$ under three selectable damage laws:
  1. **Arrhenius Thermal Aging**: $\frac{dD}{dt} = A \exp\!\left(-\frac{E_a}{k_B T}\right)$
  2. **Miner's Power-Law / Basquin Fatigue**: $\frac{dD}{dt} = k_{\text{fat}} \, \sigma^m$
  3. **Archard Linear Mechanical Wear**: $\frac{dD}{dt} = k_{\text{wear}} \, \sigma$
- **Probabilistic RUL Quantiles**: Given current damage $D(t) \in [0, D_{\text{crit}}]$ and operational duty-cycle load variability $\sigma_{\text{load}}$, projects log-normal survival quantiles:
  $$\text{RUL}_{P50} = \frac{D_{\text{crit}} - D(t)}{\dot{D}(\sigma_{\text{duty}})}, \qquad \text{RUL}_{P10} = \text{RUL}_{P50} \exp(-1.28155 \, \sigma_{\text{load}}), \qquad \text{RUL}_{P90} = \text{RUL}_{P50} \exp(+1.28155 \, \sigma_{\text{load}})$$

## ModelScript Architectural Rationale

Unlike classical block diagrams (such as causal signal-flow block diagrams) where connections represent directional causal signal flows ($y = f(u)$), ModelScript models **acausal physical interaction** across multi-energy domains:

- **Electrical**: Voltage $v$ (potential) and Current $i$ (flow).
- **Hydraulic & Pneumatic**: Pressure $p$ (potential) and Volume/Mass flow rate $q$ (flow).
- **Translational Mechanics**: Position/Velocity $s, v$ (potential) and Force $f$ (flow).
- **Rotational Mechanics**: Angle/Angular velocity $\phi, \omega$ (potential) and Torque $\tau$ (flow).
- **Thermal & Fluid Transport**: Temperature/Enthalpy $h$ (stream) and Heat/Mass flow $\dot{m}$ (flow).

In acausal modeling, connection statements `connect(a, b)` do not dictate computational causality. The compiler must automatically generate:

1. **Potential Equality Equations**: Enforcing that all across-variables in a connection set share an identical value.
2. **Kirchhoff Flow Equations**: Enforcing conservation of mass, charge, or energy such that all through-variables sum to zero at the junction.
3. **Convective Stream Transport Equations**: Resolving thermodynamic mixing when fluid direction reverses ($m_j \gtrless 0$) without introducing singular divisions near zero mass flow.

---

## Balancing Algorithm & Mathematical Formulation

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CONNECTS["Modelica Connect Equations: connect(c_1, c_2)"] --> DISJOINT["Tarjan Union-Find Clustering<br/>Build Connected Sets S_k"]
    DISJOINT --> CLASSIFY{"Examine Port Variables in S_k"}
    CLASSIFY -->|Potential / Non-flow| POT["Potential Equalization<br/>v_1 = v_2 = ... = v_m<br/>(m - 1 equations)"]
    CLASSIFY -->|Flow / Through| FLOW["Kirchhoff Balance<br/>∑ f_j = 0<br/>(1 conservation equation)"]
    CLASSIFY -->|Stream| STREAM["Upstream Operator Formulation<br/>inStream(c_j.h) & actualStream(c_j.h)<br/>Zero-Flow Regularization"]
    POT --> DAE["DAEBuilder Linear Equations"]
    FLOW --> DAE
    STREAM --> DAE
```

### 1. Disjoint Connection Set Resolution (Union-Find)

The set of all declared `connect(c_a, c_b)` statements forms an undirected graph. ModelScript partitions all connector references into disjoint equivalence classes using an integer array-based Union-Find with path compression and rank heuristics:
$$\alpha(N) \le 4 \quad \text{for all physical models}$$
For each connection set $S = \{c_1, c_2, \dots, c_m\}$ of size $m$:

### 2. Potential Variable Equalization

For every non-flow, non-stream variable $v$ declared inside the connector type:
$$v(c_1) = v(c_2) = \dots = v(c_m)$$
This yields exactly $m - 1$ scalar equations. One variable is chosen as the canonical representative, eliminating $m - 1$ redundant states during alias elimination.

### 3. Kirchhoff Flow Variable Balancing

For every `flow` variable $f$ declared inside the connector type:
$$\sum_{j=1}^m f(c_j) = 0$$
This yields exactly $1$ scalar conservation equation per connection set. If an inside-outside connector hierarchy boundary is crossed, the outer flow sign is inverted to preserve directional conservation:
$$f_{\text{outer}} = \sum_{j \in \text{inner}} f(c_j)$$

### 4. Stream Variable Convective Transport

For fluid ports, transport enthalpy depends on flow direction:

$$
h_{\text{transported}} = \begin{cases}
h_{\text{upstream}} & \text{if } \dot{m} > 0 \\
h_{\text{downstream}} & \text{if } \dot{m} < 0
\end{cases}
$$

Direct formulation introduces a discontinuous switch that causes Newton solvers to oscillate around $\dot{m} = 0$. ModelScript lowers stream variables using Franke's regularized `inStream()` and `actualStream()` operators:
$$\text{inStream}(c_i.h) = \frac{\sum_{j \neq i, \dot{m}_j > 0} \dot{m}_j \cdot c_j.h}{\sum_{j \neq i, \dot{m}_j > 0} \dot{m}_j}$$
Near zero flow ($\|\dot{m}_j\| < \epsilon$), smooth polynomial regularization is applied to maintain $C^1$-continuity of the residual Jacobian.

## 3. Craig Interpolation

### Academic Citations

- **Craig, W. (1957)**. _"Linear reasoning. A new form of the Herbrand-Gentzen theorem."_  
  **Journal of Symbolic Logic**, 22(3), pp. 250–268. DOI: [10.2307/2963593](https://doi.org/10.2307/2963593)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Given unsatisfiable mutually contradictory formulas $A \land B \models \bot$, Craig interpolation synthesizes an interpolant $I$ such that:
$$A \implies I \quad \text{and} \quad I \land B \models \bot$$
where $\text{vars}(I) \subseteq \text{vars}(A) \cap \text{vars}(B)$.

- **Modifications**: Employs Pudlák-McMillan resolution graph traversal to generate certified interpolants explaining cross-domain requirement violations without revealing proprietary subsystem equations.

- **Modifications**: Formulates Leapfrog Triejoin iteration orders using descending vertex degree heuristics; emits execution plans directly into the AOT WebAssembly compilation engine.

## 1. Spacer CHC Engine (Generalized PDR)

### Academic Citations

- **Komuravelli, A., Gurfinkel, A., & Chaki, S. (2014)**. _"SMT-Based Model Checking for Recursive Programs."_  
  **Computer Aided Verification (CAV 2014)**, LNCS 8559, pp. 17–34.  
  DOI: [10.1007/978-3-319-08867-9_2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-08867-9_2)
- **Hoder, K., & Bjørner, N. (2012)**. _"Generalized Property Directed Reachability."_  
  **Theory and Applications of Satisfiability Testing (SAT 2012)**, LNCS 7317, pp. 157–171.  
  DOI: [10.1007/978-3-642-31612-8_13](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-31612-8_13)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Constrained Horn Clauses (CHCs) represent systems of logical relations of the form:
$$\forall X. \; \phi(X) \land P_1(X) \land \dots \land P_k(X) \implies H(X)$$
Spacer solves CHCs by combining inductive generalization, Craig interpolation, and under-approximated reachability trees without bounding the unrolling depth. In ModelScript, Spacer verifies infinite-state state machine transitions and recursive cyber-physical control architectures.

- **Modifications**: Directly integrates with ModelScript's in-WASM CDCL SAT core and Craig interpolator; implements specialized heuristics for linear real arithmetic over cyber-physical invariants.

## 2. IC3 / Property Directed Reachability (PDR)

### Academic Citations

- **Bradley, A. R. (2011)**. _"SAT-based model checking without unrolling."_  
  **VMCAI 2011**, LNCS 6538, pp. 70–87.  
  DOI: [10.1007/978-3-642-18275-4_7](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-18275-4_7)
- **Een, N., Mishchenko, A., & Brayton, R. (2011)**. _"Efficient implementation of property directed reachability."_  
  **Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2011)**, pp. 125–134.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Proves whether safety property $P$ holds across all reachable states of a discrete or hybrid transition system without unrolling the transition relation $T(s, s')$ to a fixed horizon $k$.

- **Modifications**: Maintains inductive clause frames $F_0, F_1, \dots, F_k$ where $F_i$ over-approximates states reachable in up to $i$ steps; uses counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR) to block Proof Obligations (POBs); propagates clauses forward to find an inductive invariant ($F_i \equiv F_{i+1}$) proving unbounded safety.

## 3. Stochastic Barrier Certificates (`wasm_stochastic_barrier.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **Prajna, S., Jadbabaie, A., & Pappas, G. J. (2007)**. _"A framework for worst-case and stochastic safety verification using barrier certificates."_  
  **IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control**, 52(8), pp. 1415–1428.  
  DOI: [10.1109/TAC.2007.902736](https://doi.org/10.1109/TAC.2007.902736)
- **Kushner, H. J. (1967)**. _Stochastic Stability and Control._  
  **Academic Press**.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

For continuous-time stochastic differential equations (Itô diffusions) driven by standard Wiener processes $W_t$:
$$dx(t) = f(x) \, dt + \sigma(x) \, dW_t$$
deterministic trajectories do not exist, and safety verification requires bounding the tail probability that $x(t)$ ever enters an unsafe region $\mathcal{X}_u = \{ x \mid \|x\|_2 \ge r_u \}$.

`StochasticBarrierSynthesizer` (`packages/runtime/src/analysis/wasm_stochastic_barrier.ts`) synthesizes non-negative supermartingale barrier candidates $B(x) = x^T P x \ge 0$ using the **infinitesimal generator** $\mathcal{L}$ of the Itô process:
$$\mathcal{L} B(x) = \nabla B(x) \cdot f(x) + \frac{1}{2} \text{tr}\!\left(\sigma(x) \sigma(x)^T \nabla^2 B(x)\right) \le -c$$

- **Doob's Maximal Supermartingale Inequality**: Bounds the infinite-horizon and finite-horizon probability of unsafe set entry via:
  $$\mathbb{P}\!\left(\sup_{t \ge 0} \|x(t)\|_2 \ge r_u\right) \le \frac{B(x_0) + \frac{\text{tr}(\Sigma P)}{2 \alpha}}{\lambda_{\min}(P) r_u^2} \le \delta_{\text{risk}}$$
  where $\Sigma = \sigma(0)\sigma(0)^T$ is the diffusion noise covariance and $\alpha$ is the linearized drift decay rate.
- **Soundness & Rigor Reporting**: Emits structured `VerificationVerdict` diagnostics distinguishing fast linearized quadratic risk estimates from Sum-of-Squares (SOS) / LP certified supermartingales.

---

## 4. WebGPU Datalog / OWL 2 RL Saturation Reasoner (`webgpu_reasoner.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **Motik, B., Patel-Schneider, P. F., & Parsia, B. (2012)**. _"OWL 2 Web Ontology Language: Profiles (Second Edition) — OWL 2 RL."_  
  **W3C Recommendation**. [https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-profiles/](https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-profiles/)
- **Warshall, S. (1962)**. _"A theorem on Boolean matrices."_  
  **Journal of the ACM**, 9(1), pp. 11–12. DOI: [10.1145/321105.321107](https://doi.org/10.1145/321105.321107)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Large-scale systems engineering ontologies (`languages/owl2/` and SysML v2 KerML specialization hierarchies) contain $10^5$ to $10^7$ ABox/TBox assertions. Evaluating transitive role closures (`subClassOf`, `partOf`, `satisfies`) and SHACL numeric property constraints sequentially on the CPU becomes a bottleneck during workspace-wide verification.

`WebGPUOntologyReasoner` (`packages/runtime/src/gpu/webgpu_reasoner.ts`) implements a massively parallel GPU relational join and saturation co-processor with a CPU SIMD bitset fallback:

- **Bit-Packed Adjacency Matrix (`BitsetGraph`)**: Encodes an $N \times N$ directed graph as a flat `Uint32Array` where each node row $u$ occupies $\lceil N / 32 \rceil$ 32-bit words, achieving $32\times$ memory compression and single-instruction bitwise row unions.
- **Parallel Logarithmic Doubling in WGSL (`TRANSITIVE_CLOSURE_WGSL`)**: Dispatches compute workgroups (`workgroups = ceil(N / 64)`) over ping-pong storage buffers (`bufIn`, `bufOut`) for $\lceil \log_2 N \rceil + 1$ doubling rounds, computing the full reflexive-transitive closure $R^*$ in $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ GPU passes.
- **Parallel SHACL Constraint Kernel (`SHACL_VALIDATION_WGSL`)**: Validates `SHACLNumericConstraint` bounds (`minInclusive`, `maxInclusive`, `expectedClassId`) across strided `Float32Array` instance attribute tables and writes compact violation bitsets.

---

## 5. ISO 26262 / DO-178C Back-to-Back Equivalence Verification (`b2b_verifier.ts`, `v_cycle_verifier.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **ISO 26262-6:2018 & ISO 26262-8:2018**. _Road vehicles — Functional safety — Part 6: Product development at the software level (Table 7: Back-to-back comparison test between model and code) & Part 8: Supporting processes (Clause 11: Confidence in the use of software tools, TCL1)._
- **RTCA DO-178C /DO-331 (2011)**. _Software Considerations in Airborne Systems and Equipment Certification — Model-Based Development and Verification Supplement._

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Safety-critical automotive (ISO 26262 ASIL-D) and avionics (DO-178C DAL-A) standards require proving that generated embedded production code (zero-allocation C99 or standalone WASM FMU artifacts) is numerically and behaviorally equivalent to the high-level specification model (SysML v2 / Modelica).

`B2BEquivalenceVerifier` (`packages/runtime/src/simulation/b2b_verifier.ts`, orchestrated by `UnifiedVerifier` in `packages/runtime/src/simulation/unified_verifier.ts`) automates end-to-end **Model-in-the-Loop (MiL) vs. Software-in-the-Loop (SiL)** back-to-back verification:

1. **MiL Reference Trajectory Execution**: Simulates the high-level DAE arena (`simulateArenaAsync`) over $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{stop}}]$ to obtain reference trajectories $y^{\text{MiL}}_j(t)$.
2. **Standalone C99 Code Generation & Cryptographic Hashing**: Invokes `generateStandaloneCSources` (`@modelscript/exchange/fmu`) to emit self-contained, zero-allocation C99 sources (`<Model>_standalone.h`, `<Model>_standalone.c`), computing a SHA-256 artifact digest (`cSourceHash`) for V-cycle traceability.
3. **Automated Test Harness & Native Compilation**: Synthesizes a deterministic C99 fixed-step RK4 test harness (`<Model>_b2b_harness.c`), compiles the binary via `gcc -O2 -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -lm`, and streams CSV output trajectories $y^{\text{SiL}}_j(t_k)$.
4. **Bisimulation & Signal-Tolerance Equivalence Checking**: Aligns SiL samples against binary-searched linearly interpolated MiL trajectories and verifies the combined absolute/relative tolerance envelope across all $K$ time steps and $M$ output signals:
   $$\forall j \in \{1, \dots, M\}, \; \forall k \in \{1, \dots, K\}: \quad \left| y^{\text{MiL}}_j(t_k) - y^{\text{SiL}}_j(t_k) \right| \le \epsilon_{\text{abs}} + \epsilon_{\text{rel}} \left| y^{\text{MiL}}_j(t_k) \right|$$

## 1. Bourdoncle Weak Topological Ordering (WTO) Fixpoint Solver

### Academic Citations

- **Bourdoncle, F. (1993)**. _"Efficient chaotic iteration strategies with widenings."_  
  **Formal Methods in Programming and Their Applications**, LNCS 735, pp. 128–141. DOI: [10.1007/BFb0039704](https://doi.org/10.1007/BFb0039704)
- **Cousot, P., & Cousot, R. (1977)**. _"Abstract interpretation: A unified lattice model for static analysis of programs by construction or approximation of fixpoints."_  
  **ACM POPL'77**, pp. 238–252. DOI: [10.1145/512950.512973](https://doi.org/10.1145/512950.512973)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Computes sound abstract over-approximations of state variables across complex nested loops and recursion without simulating unbounded trajectories.

- **Modifications**: Implements Bourdoncle's recursive hierarchical WTO decomposition to identify minimal loop heads; accelerates convergence using delayed widening ($\nabla$) followed by monotonic narrowing ($\Delta$).

## 2. Two Variables Per Inequality (TVPI) Polyhedral Domain

### Academic Citations

- **Simon, A., King, A., & Howe, J. M. (2002)**. _"Two Variables per Inequality as an Abstract Domain."_  
  **LOPSTR 2002**, LNCS 2664, pp. 71–89. DOI: [10.1007/3-540-36388-2_7](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-36388-2_7)
- **Nelson, G. (1978)**. _"An $n^{O(\log n)}$ algorithm for the two-variable-per-inequality integer programming problem."_  
  **Technical Report**, Stanford University.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Captures planar relational linear invariants of the form:
$$a x_i + b x_j \le c \quad (a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q})$$
Much more expressive than simple intervals or octagons, allowing ModelScript to prove physical conservation laws (e.g. $p_1 + p_2 = \text{const}$) without the exponential vertex-facet explosion of general convex polyhedra.

- **Modifications**: Planar Graham-scan convex hull algorithms in WebAssembly typed memory; relational projection routines optimized for physical parameter spaces.

---

## 3. Octagon Difference Bound Matrices (DBM) Domain

### Academic Citations

- **Miné, A. (2006)**. _"The octagon abstract domain."_  
  **Higher-Order and Symbolic Computation**, 19(1), pp. 31–100.  
  DOI: [10.1007/s10990-006-8609-1](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10990-006-8609-1)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Restricts linear relationships to constraints of the form:
$$\pm x_i \pm x_j \le c$$
Achieves cubic time complexity $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$ via Floyd-Warshall shortest path algorithms over $2n \times 2n$ potential graphs.

- **Modifications**: Direct integration into the `@modelscript/dsl` type inference system and `AbstractDomainOracle` in the Nelson-Oppen coordinator.

## 4. Array Segment Partitioning

### Academic Citations

- **Cousot, P., Cousot, R., & Logozzo, F. (2011)**. _"A Parametric Segmentation Functor for Fully Automatic and Scalable Array Content Analysis."_  
  **ACM POPL'11**, pp. 505–518. DOI: [10.1145/1926385.1926444](https://doi.org/10.1145/1926385.1926444)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Verifies large array equations and indexed multi-dimensional components in Modelica without unrolling every array index into separate scalar variables. Partitions index sets into contiguous segments whose bounds and elements share uniform properties.

## 5. Delay Differential Equation (DDE) Method-of-Steps Flowpipes (`wasm_dde_flowpipe.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **Bellman, R., & Cooke, K. L. (1963)**. _Differential-Difference Equations._  
  **Academic Press**.
- **Zou, L., Fränzle, M., Xue, B., & Zhan, N. (2015)**. _"orda: An Ode and Dde Reachability Analysis Tool."_  
  **SETTA 2015**, LNCS 9409, pp. 109–123. DOI: [10.1007/978-3-319-25942-0_8](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-25942-0_8)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Physical transport delays, networked control loops, and Modelica `delay(x, tau)` operators yield infinite-dimensional Delay Differential Equations (DDEs):
$$\dot{x}(t) = f\big(t, x(t), x(t - \tau)\big), \qquad x(t) \in \Phi(t) \text{ for } t \in [-\tau, 0]$$
`DdeFlowpipeSolver` (`packages/runtime/src/analysis/wasm_dde_flowpipe.ts`) implements **Method-of-Steps** reachability propagation across consecutive delay horizons $[0, \tau], [\tau, 2\tau], \dots$:

- **History Interval Buffering**: Maintains a timestamped ring buffer `historyMap` storing both nominal trajectories $\bar{x}(t)$ and interval/zonotope tube enclosures $\mathcal{X}(t) = [\underline{x}(t), \overline{x}(t)]$. For $t - \tau \le t_0$, queries evaluate the initial functional history enclosure $\Phi(t - \tau)$; for $t - \tau > t_0$, historical enclosures are interpolated from stored flowpipe steps.
- **Interval Picard Enclosure Step**: Advances the state tube across $[t_k, t_k + \Delta t]$ by combining current state bounds $\mathcal{X}(t_k)$ and delayed history bounds $\mathcal{X}(t_k - \tau)$:
  $$\mathcal{X}(t_{k+1}) = \mathcal{X}(t_k) + \Delta t \cdot \square f\big(t_k, \mathcal{X}(t_k), \mathcal{X}(t_k - \tau)\big)$$
- **Epistemic Soundness Tagging**: Explicitly tags the resulting `VerificationVerdict` with rigor metadata (`heuristic` vs. `certified`) so downstream safety monitors distinguish fast corner-sampled delay tube estimates from fully Taylor-enclosed flowpipes.

---

## 6. Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs (HJI) PDE Level-Set Reachability (`wasm_hji_solver.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **Mitchell, I. M., Bayen, A. M., & Tomlin, C. J. (2005)**. _"A time-dependent Hamilton-Jacobi formulation of reachable sets for continuous dynamic games."_  
  **IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control**, 50(7), pp. 947–957.  
  DOI: [10.1109/TAC.2005.851439](https://doi.org/10.1109/TAC.2005.851439)
- **Jiang, G. S., & Shu, C. W. (2000)**. _"Weighted ENO schemes for Hamilton-Jacobi equations."_  
  **SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing**, 21(6), pp. 2126–2143.  
  DOI: [10.1137/S106482759732455X](https://doi.org/10.1137/S106482759732455X)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

When verifying safety of nonlinear control systems under worst-case adversarial disturbances $d \in \mathcal{D}$ and control authority $u \in \mathcal{U}$, convex set-propagation (zonotopes) can suffer from wrapping effects. `HjiLevelSetSolver` (`packages/runtime/src/analysis/wasm_hji_solver.ts`) computes the exact **Backward Reachable Tube (BRT)** by solving the zero-sum differential game **Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs (HJI) PDE** viscosity solution on an Eulerian level-set grid:
$$\frac{\partial V}{\partial t} + \min \left\{ 0, \; \min_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \max_{d \in \mathcal{D}} \nabla V(x, t) \cdot f(x, u, d) \right\} = 0, \qquad V(x, 0) = \ell(x)$$
where the sub-zero level set $\mathcal{K}_{\text{unsafe}} = \{ x \mid \ell(x) \le 0 \}$ defines the target failure region and $\{ x \mid V(x, T) \le 0 \}$ captures all initial states from which the adversary $d$ can force the trajectory into $\mathcal{K}_{\text{unsafe}}$ within horizon $T$ despite optimal safety control $u$.

- **5th-Order WENO Upwind Spatial Reconstruction (`weno5Derivatives`)**: Approximates left and right spatial derivatives $(p^-, p^+)$ along each state axis using 3-stencil smoothness indicators ($s_1, s_2, s_3$) and nonlinear weights $a_k = \frac{\gamma_k}{(\epsilon + s_k)^2}$, eliminating spurious oscillations near non-smooth value-function kinks.
- **Lax-Friedrichs Numerical Hamiltonian**: Evaluates the saddle-point Hamiltonian $H(x, p) = \min_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \max_{d \in \mathcal{D}} p \cdot f(x, u, d)$ at central gradients $p = \frac{1}{2}(p^- + p^+)$ augmented by artificial viscosity dissipation:
  $$\hat{H}(x, p^-, p^+) = H\left(x, \frac{p^- + p^+}{2}\right) - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i} \alpha_i (p_i^+ - p_i^-), \qquad \alpha_i = \max_{u, d} |f_i(x, u, d)|$$
- **Monotone BRT Accumulation**: Steps the level-set array backward in time with `nextV[idx] = Math.min(V[idx], V[idx] - dt * dVdt)` and reports the exact unsafe volume fraction across the state space.

## ModelScript Architectural Rationale

1. **Semidefinite Programming (SDP) for Verified Safety**: Formal continuous verification of non-linear physical models requires proving that state trajectories $\mathbf{x}(t)$ never breach unsafe operating envelopes. Synthesizing polynomial Lyapunov functions $V(\mathbf{x}) > 0$ and barrier certificates $B(\mathbf{x}) \le 0$ reduces to finding Sum-of-Squares (SOS) decompositions:
   $$p(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{z}(\mathbf{x})^T Q \, \mathbf{z}(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0 \iff Q \succeq 0$$
   By implementing a native primal-dual interior-point SDP solver in WebAssembly, ModelScript provides mathematically verified stability proofs directly in the browser and CLI without relying on external monolithic commercial solvers.
2. **Multiple Shooting BVP for Optimal Trajectories**: Boundary Value Problems (BVPs) govern optimal trajectory planning, model predictive control (MPC), and periodic limit cycle detection with split boundary conditions:
   $$g(\mathbf{y}(t_0), \mathbf{y}(t_{\text{end}}), \mathbf{p}) = \mathbf{0}$$
   Standard single shooting suffers from catastrophic numerical instability on stiff or chaotic dynamics. Multiple shooting subdivides the time horizon into $M$ subintervals, guaranteeing numerical stability and fast Newton-Raphson convergence.
3. **Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) for Multi-Physics 3D Packaging**: Lumped-parameter 1D physical models (Modelica) rely on 3D geometric properties (mass, inertia tensor, aerodynamic drag area, hydraulic volume). ModelScript evaluates OpenSCAD models into normalized CSG solid trees (`@modelscript/cad`), auto-tagging boundary patches (`inlet`, `outlet`, `wall`, `symmetry`) for downstream OpenCascade B-Rep evaluation, STEP export, and SU2/OpenFOAM CFD meshing.

---

## Mathematical Formulation & Execution Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SOS["Polynomial Barrier / Lyapunov Inequalities"] --> SDP_SOLVER["WASM Primal-Dual Interior-Point SDP<br/>Minimize tr(C X) s.t. A(X) = b, X ⪰ 0<br/>Cholesky Factorization & Central Path"]
    SDP_SOLVER --> CERT["Formal SOS Witness Certificate"]

    BVP_REQ["BVP Problem & Split Boundary Conditions"] --> BVP_SOLVER["Multiple Shooting Solver<br/>1. Subdivide Horizon [t_0, t_M]<br/>2. Tsit5 Parallel Forward Steps<br/>3. Continuity & Boundary Residuals<br/>4. WASM LU Factorization"]
    BVP_SOLVER --> TRAJ["Converged Optimal State Trajectory"]

    SCAD_CODE["OpenSCAD / STEP Geometry"] --> CSG_EVAL["CSG & StepMesher (@modelscript/cad & simulate)<br/>Tet4/Tet10 Meshing & Prismatic Boundary Inflation"]
    CSG_EVAL --> CONTINUUM["WebGPU D3Q19 LBM CFD & Corotational PCG FEA"]
    CSG_EVAL --> MECH_VERIFY["Swept-Volume Clearance, GD&T Stack-Up & Inverse CAD"]
```

### 1. Primal-Dual Interior Point SDP Solver

Solves standard primal and dual semidefinite programs:
$$\text{Primal: } \min_{X \in \mathbb{S}^n} \text{tr}(C X) \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \text{tr}(A_i X) = b_i, \; X \succeq 0$$
$$\text{Dual: } \max_{y \in \mathbb{R}^m, S \in \mathbb{S}^n} b^T y \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{i=1}^m y_i A_i + S = C, \; S \succeq 0$$

- **Central Path Following**: Enforces the perturbed complementarity condition $X S = \mu I$ with barrier parameter $\mu = \frac{\text{tr}(X S)}{n}$.
- **WASM Linear Algebra**: Predictor-corrector search directions $(\Delta X, \Delta y, \Delta S)$ are computed using fast in-memory Cholesky factorizations (`wasm_gaussian.ts`), with backtracking line search to ensure $X + \alpha \Delta X \succ 0$ and $S + \alpha \Delta S \succ 0$.

### 2. Multiple Shooting BVP Solver

Subdivides the horizon $[t_0, t_{\text{end}}]$ into $M$ subintervals with mesh points $t_0 < t_1 < \dots < t_M = t_{\text{end}}$:

- **State Trajectory Variables**: Introduces free initial conditions $\mathbf{s}_m$ at each node $t_m$.
- **Subinterval Integration**: Integrates forward from $t_m$ to $t_{m+1}$ using adaptive `tsit5`:
  $$\mathbf{y}(t_{m+1}; \mathbf{s}_m, \mathbf{p})$$
- **Matching Residual System**: Solves the $(M \cdot n + k) \times (M \cdot n + k)$ simultaneous nonlinear system:
  $$F_m(\mathbf{s}_m, \mathbf{s}_{m+1}) = \mathbf{y}(t_{m+1}; \mathbf{s}_m, \mathbf{p}) - \mathbf{s}_{m+1} = \mathbf{0}, \quad m = 0, \dots, M-1$$
  $$g(\mathbf{s}_0, \mathbf{s}_M, \mathbf{p}) = \mathbf{0}$$
- **Newton-Raphson Update**: Evaluates sensitivity Jacobians along trajectories and solves the block-banded linear system via WASM Gaussian LU elimination.

### 3. OpenSCAD CSG Engine & CFD Boundary Tagging

Transforms procedural CSG trees into boundary-tagged solid geometries:

- Evaluates transformations (`translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, `mirror`) and regularized Boolean operators (`union`, `difference`, `intersection`).
- Decorates faces with CFD boundary tags (`tagPatch`, `BoundaryPatchType`: `inlet`, `outlet`, `wall`, `symmetry`), for handoff to automated SU2 mesh generators.

### 4. 3D Continuum Physics & B-Rep Meshing (`packages/simulate`)

ModelScript embeds native 3D continuum fluid, structural, and volumetric meshing engines that couple directly to 1D DAE simulations:

1. **WebGPU D3Q19 Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) CFD Solver (`webgpu-lbm-runner.ts`)**:
   - Discretizes the Boltzmann transport equation over a 19-velocity 3D lattice (`D3Q19`) stored in a zero-copy Structure-of-Arrays arena (`CfdFieldArena`) with ping-pong distribution buffers (`f0`, `f1`) and WGSL compute shader execution (`LBM_D3Q19_WGSL`, workgroups $8 \times 8 \times 4$):
     $$f_i^{\text{post}}(\mathbf{x}, t) = f_i(\mathbf{x}, t) - \omega_{\text{loc}}\!\left(f_i(\mathbf{x}, t) - f_i^{\text{eq}}(\rho, \mathbf{u})\right), \qquad f_i^{\text{eq}} = w_i \rho \!\left(1 + 3(\mathbf{c}_i \cdot \mathbf{u}) + \frac{9}{2}(\mathbf{c}_i \cdot \mathbf{u})^2 - \frac{3}{2}\|\mathbf{u}\|^2\right)$$
   - **Smagorinsky Subgrid LES Turbulence**: Dynamically adapts the local relaxation frequency $\omega_{\text{loc}} = (\tau_0 + \Delta\tau_{\text{LES}})^{-1}$ from the non-equilibrium momentum flux tensor $\Pi_{\alpha\beta}^{\text{neq}} = \sum_i c_{i\alpha} c_{i\beta} (f_i - f_i^{\text{eq}})$.
   - **Bouzidi Curved Boundaries & Moving-Wall FSI**: Applies sub-cell linear interpolation for curved solid obstacles ($\delta_{\text{wall}} < 0.5$ vs. $\delta_{\text{wall}} \ge 0.5$), injects moving-wall momentum $\Delta f_i = 6 w_i \rho (\mathbf{c}_i \cdot \mathbf{u}_{\text{wall}})$ for two-way aeroelastic FSI, and integrates surface drag forces via momentum exchange.
2. **3D Tet4/Tet10 Linear/Nonlinear Corotational Elasticity & Thermal FEA Solver (`fea-solver.ts`)**:
   - Assembles global sparse stiffness $K$ and consistent mass $M$ matrices in Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) format for 4-node linear (`Tet4Element`) and 10-node quadratic (`Tet10Element`) tetrahedra.
   - **Corotational Large-Rotation Kinematics**: Extracts element rigid-body rotation $R_e \in \text{SO}(3)$ from the deformation gradient $F = e_0 E_0^{-1}$ via 6-step Higham polar decomposition iterations $R_{k+1} = \frac{1}{2}(R_k + R_k^{-T})$, rotating local element stiffness blocks $K_{\text{rot}} = R_e K_e R_e^T$ for geometric nonlinearity invariance.
   - **Jacobi-Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient (PCG) & Newmark-$\beta$ Dynamics**: Solves static equilibrium $K u = f$ and Rayleigh-damped transient elastodynamics $M \ddot{u} + (\alpha_M M + \beta_K K)\dot{u} + K u = f$ using unconditional-stability Newmark-$\beta$ ($\beta = 0.25, \gamma = 0.5$) time stepping, outputting nodal/element von Mises stresses and yield safety factors.
3. **STEP B-Rep Tetrahedral Mesher & Prismatic Boundary-Layer Extrusion (`step-mesher.ts`)**:
   - `StepMesher` converts ISO 10303-21 STEP B-Rep entities and watertight surface triangulations into volumetric `Tet4` / `Tet10` meshes (`Tet4Mesher`), classifies exterior boundary patches (`PatchClassifier`), extrudes viscous prismatic inflation layers along `WALL_BODY` surfaces (`BoundaryLayerExtruder`), evaluates Jacobian/aspect-ratio quality (`MeshQualityAnalyzer`), and exports ready-to-run CalculiX (`*.inp`) and SU2 (`*.su2`) decks.

### 5. Mechanical Swept-Volume, GD&T Stack-Up & Inverse CAD (`packages/cad`)

1. **Dynamic Swept-Volume Collision & Clearance Envelopes (`dynamic-clearance.ts`)**:
   - `DynamicClearanceVerifier` bridges continuous reachability flowpipes (`TrajectoryStepEnclosure[]`) into 3D CAD assemblies (`Assembly`). At each time step, it propagates interval state enclosures $[x_i^{\text{lo}}, x_i^{\text{hi}}]$ through translational Minkowski sums, rotational corner-envelope expansions, and soft-tissue/compliant cavity morphing (`volume_radial` $s = (V/V_0)^{1/3}$, `anisotropic`, and `modal` skinning).
   - Evaluates exact pairwise AABB separation distances (`computeAABBDistance`) and closest witness points (`computeAABBClosestPoints`), automatically synthesizing a 3D counterexample CAD assembly at the worst-case collision timestamp $t^*$ if any clearance rule is violated.
2. **Worst-Case, Statistical RSS & Coupled Thermal-Elastic GD&T Stack-Up (`tolerance-stack.ts`)**:
   - `ToleranceStackVerifier` verifies 1D/3D kinematic assembly gap loops across directional contributors ($d_i \in \{+1, -1\}$) combining bilateral manufacturing tolerances $[t_i^L, t_i^U]$, thermal expansion over $[T_{\min}, T_{\max}]$ ($\Delta L_{\text{th}} = L_0 \alpha_{\text{CTE}} \Delta T$), and axial elastic deflection under dynamic loads $[F_{\min}, F_{\max}]$ ($\Delta L_{\text{el}} = \frac{F L_0}{E A}$):
     $$g_{\text{min, WC}} = \sum_{i} d_i L_{0,i} + \sum_{i} \min(d_i t_i^L, d_i t_i^U) + \Delta g_{\text{th, min}} + \Delta g_{\text{el, min}}, \qquad \sigma_{\text{RSS}} = \sqrt{\sum_{i} \left(\frac{t_i^U - t_i^L}{6}\right)^2}$$
3. **Certified Bi-Directional CAD Parameter Inversion (`parameter-inversion.ts`)**:
   - `ParameterInversionEngine` closes the loop from 1D system optimization back to 3D MCAD source code. Given target mass/inertia constraints (`solveLengthForMass`, `scaleDimensionsForMass`) or optimized Modelica parameters, `patchMcadSourceCertified` verifies candidate dimensions against a multidisciplinary `SafeRegionGuard` ($\mathcal{P}_{\text{safe}}$ box bounds and buckling/stress/clearance predicates) before rewriting the parametric MCAD AST and regenerating STEP geometry.

### 6. ECAD / PCB Geometry, Autorouting & DRC (`packages/cad/src/ecad/`)

1. **RS-274X Gerber Aperture Evaluation & Excellon Drill Synthesis (`gerber.ts`)**:
   - `generateManufacturingFiles` compiles multi-layer `PCBLayout` models (`TopCopper`, `BottomCopper`, `InnerCopper1/2`, `Top/BottomSilkscreen`, `Top/BottomSolderMask`, `BoardOutline`) into IPC-compliant **RS-274X Gerber** (`%FSLAX46Y46*%`, $10^{-6}\text{ mm}$ integer precision) with deduplicated aperture macros (`%ADD10C,...*%`, circle/rect/oval pads, $0.1\text{ mm}$ negative-polarity solder mask expansion `%IPNEG*%`) and **Excellon** NC drill programs (`drill.xln`, `METRIC,TZ`).
2. **Multi-Layer Interactive & Constrained PCB Trace Router (`engine/router.ts`)**:
   - `PCBRouter` (`pcb-router.ts` / `engine/router.ts`) implements a multi-layer trace routing engine supporting pad snap-targeting (`snapToPad`), $90^\circ$ Manhattan (`manhattanRoute`) and $45^\circ$ octilinear (`diagonal45Route`: $\text{diag} = \min(|\Delta x|, |\Delta y|)$) segment constraints, and automatic plated through-hole via insertion (`insertVia`) on layer transitions.
3. **Euclidean Trace/Pad Clearance Design Rule Checking (`engine/drc.ts`)**:
   - `runDRC` (`pcb-drc.ts` / `engine/drc.ts`) executes non-blocking geometric verification across copper layers, checking minimum trace widths, trace-to-trace, trace-to-pad, and pad-to-pad Euclidean clearances ($d(\mathbf{p}_1, \mathbf{p}_2) - \frac{w_1 + w_2}{2} \ge c_{\min}$), via drill and annular ring minimums ($r_{\text{outer}} - r_{\text{drill}} \ge a_{\min}$), point-to-segment board-outline polygon distances (`minDistToPolygon`), and unconnected ratsnest net completeness.

## ModelScript Architectural Rationale

Physical engineering schematics (such as Modelica connection diagrams, SysML v2 Internal Block Diagrams, and hydraulic/piping schematics) require strict geometric conventions:

- **Orthogonal Edges**: Connections must run strictly along horizontal and vertical channels with clean $90^\circ$ bends.
- **Port-Constraint Preservation**: High-degree engineering components have physical boundary pins (e.g. electrical resistors have pins $p$ and $n$ on opposite faces; hydraulic valves have ports $A$, $B$, $P$, $T$). Layout engines must place connection points on explicit component boundaries rather than abstract node centers.
- **Zero-Obstacle Penetration**: Wires must never traverse component bounding boxes.
- **Bus Disambiguation**: Multi-variable connections between blocks must not collapse onto identical collinear segments.

ModelScript implements the **Topology-Shape-Metrics (TSM)** pipeline augmented with a **Global Port ILP Solver** and **Dogleg Channel Router** natively in the browser and CLI.

---

## Three-Phase Layout & Routing Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT["Modelica Connects / SysML v2 Item Flows"] --> PORT_OPT["Phase 1: Port Constraint Optimization<br/>(Face Assignment & Cross-Free Ordering)"]
    PORT_OPT --> TSM["Phase 2: Topology-Shape-Metrics (TSM)<br/>1. Planarization & Crossing Minimization<br/>2. Orthogonal Shape via Network Flow<br/>3. Metric Coordinate Compaction"]
    TSM --> ROUTER["Phase 3: Orthogonal Channel Routing<br/>1. Normal Outward Port Stubs<br/>2. Obstacle-Avoiding Bend-Penalized A*<br/>3. Staggered Parallel Dogleg Offsets"]
    ROUTER --> RENDER["SVG / Canvas / Web IDE Viewport"]
```

### 1. Port Constraint & Continuous Alignment Solver

Resolves port assignment along component perimeters ($x, y \in \partial \text{Node}$):

- **Discrete Face Selection**: Assigns ports to Cardinal sides (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) minimizing Manhattan connection distance:
  $$\min \sum_{e = (u_i, v_j) \in E} \| \mathbf{p}(u_i) - \mathbf{p}(v_j) \|_1$$
- **Causality Biasing**: Automatically places `input` ports on the left face and `output` ports on the right face for signal-flow blocks.
- **Collinear Port Snapping**: Enforces 0-bend straight lines whenever two connected ports are horizontally or vertically aligned within a configurable tolerance `straightTolerance`.

### 2. Topology-Shape-Metrics (TSM) Engine

Extends Tamassia's Kandinsky model for high-degree engineering vertices:

1. **Planarization**: Replaces unavoidable edge crossings with dummy vertices of degree 4.
2. **Orthogonalization (Minimum Bend Flow)**: Formulates bend minimization as a minimum-cost network flow problem over the dual graph, assigning angles $\alpha \in \{90^\circ, 180^\circ, 270^\circ, 360^\circ\}$ to faces.
3. **Compaction**: Solves two independent 1D longest path problems on horizontal and vertical constraint DAGs to compute minimal integer grid coordinates.

### 3. Obstacle-Avoiding Dogleg Channel Router

Renders clean multi-segment connection polylines:

- **Perpendicular Port Stubs**: Edge paths extend outward along the port normal vector by a distance `stubLength` before turning.
- **A\* Grid Search with Bend Penalty**: Avoids component AABB bounding boxes using fast `segmentIntersectsRect` intersection tests while penalizing unnecessary turns:
  $$\text{Cost}(p \to q) = \text{dist}(p, q) + \lambda_{\text{bend}} \cdot [\text{isTurn}(p, q)]$$
- **Staggered Parallel Channels**: Multi-wire bus connections share a common corridor but are offset by `parallelIndex * channelSpacing`, preventing overlapping lines.

### 4. Specialized Engineering Diagram Layouts

Beyond acausal block schematics, ModelScript provides domain-specific geometric layout engines tailored to safety, behavioral, and power-systems engineering notations:

1. **Fault Tree Gate Hierarchy Layout (`fault-tree.ts` / `fault-tree-layout.ts`)**:
   - `synthesizeFaultTreeDiagram` transforms Minimal Cut Sets ($\text{MCS} = \{ C_1, \dots, C_m \}$) into four-tier standardized Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) diagrams:
     - **Tier 1 ($y = 40$)**: Top Hazard Event rect node centered at $x_{\text{center}} = W / 2$.
     - **Tier 2 ($y = 160$)**: Root Boolean `OR` gate (`createGateMarkup("OR")` SVG bezier shield) aggregating cut-set branches.
     - **Tier 3 ($y = 280$)**: Intermediate `AND` gates for multi-point failure cut sets ($\text{order} > 1$), while order-1 Single Points of Failure (SPOFs) route directly in high-visibility crimson (`#dc2626`) to basic events.
     - **Tier 4 ($y = 420$)**: Deduplicated circular Basic Event leaf nodes (`basicEventNodesMap`) distributed symmetrically across the horizontal span.
2. **UML / SysML v2 Sequence & Activity Swimlane Layouts (`sequence-layout.ts`, `swimlane-layout.ts`)**:
   - **Dual-Axis Sequence Layout (`computeSequenceLayout` / `applySequenceLayout`)**: Orders participant lifelines left-to-right ($x_i = x_{\text{left}} + i \cdot \Delta x_{\text{lifeline}} + W_{\text{hdr}}/2$), renders dashed vertical lifeline stems (`__seq_stem_*`), and stacks temporal messages top-to-bottom ($y_{k+1} = y_k + \Delta y_{\text{msg}}$) with distinct styling for synchronous (`sync`), asynchronous (`async`), dashed `reply`, and self-loop (`isSelf`, $1.5\times$ vertical spacing) messages.
   - **2D Activity Swimlane Partitioning (`applySwimlaneLayout`)**: Groups SysML v2 action nodes into vertical or horizontal allocation partitions (`SwimlanePartition`), sizing uniform lane containers (`swimlane_<id>`) to the maximum member stack height and routing cross-lane object/control flows via `port-orthogonal-astar`.
3. **PSCAD Power-System Single-Line Diagram (SLD) Busbar/Feeder Orthogonal Routing (`pscad-diagram-builder.ts` / `pscad-sld-builder.ts`)**:
   - `buildPscadDiagram` renders `.pscx`/`.pslx` electromagnetic transient models into IEEE-standard Single-Line Diagrams with voltage-coded busbar glyphs ($\ge 200\text{ kV}$ red `#ff5252`, $\ge 69\text{ kV}$ amber `#ffab40`, $< 69\text{ kV}$ cyan `#40c4ff`), specialized IEEE apparatus vector glyphs (`transformerGlyph`, `generatorGlyph`, `inverterIbrGlyph`, `breakerGlyph`, `surgeArresterGlyph`, `faultGlyph`, `converterBridgeGlyph`), solder-dot wire T-junctions, and orthogonal feeder routing.

### 5. Semantic Visual Diffing & Collaborative Presence

1. **AST-Aware Structural Graph Diffing & Mental-Map Stabilization (`visual-diff-graph.ts`, `visual-diff-renderer.ts` / `visual-diff.ts`)**:
   - `buildVisualDiffGraph` computes a semantic delta between `Base` and `Head` diagram revisions, classifying nodes and edges into `added`, `deleted`, `modified`, and `unchanged` states (`DiffStatus`).
   - **Breaking Interface Detection**: Inspects property and port changes (`diffProperties`) against architectural breaking keys (`direction`, `isAbstract`, `typeName`, `multiplicity`, `causality`, `variability`, `flowDirection`) and flags deleted components or port-count mutations as `MODIFIED (BREAKING)`.
   - **Anchor-Preserving Layout Stabilization (`computeIncrementalStabilization`)**: Locks `Base` node coordinates as immutable spatial anchors while iteratively relaxing newly added/modified `Head` nodes to eliminate bounding-box overlaps without destroying the reviewer's spatial mental map.
2. **CRDT / WebSocket Cursor, Selection Lock & Spatial Delta Synchronization (`collab-manager.ts`)**:
   - `CollabManager` coordinates real-time multi-user diagramming over WebSocket and VS Code Live Share transports:
     - **60 FPS Spatial Delta Streaming (`broadcastSpatialDelta`)**: Streams live component drag transformations (`PlacementItem`) with Last-Write-Wins (`LWW`) timestamp conflict resolution (`d.timestamp >= existing.timestamp`).
     - **Component Selection Locks (`SelectionLock`)**: Broadcasts per-peer component locks with distinct peer colors and automatic stale-peer heartbeat eviction (`purgeStalePeers`).
     - **Anchored Visual Review Comments (`DiagramComment`)**: Synchronizes spatially pinned sticky-note threads (`addComment`, `resolveComment`) directly on the schematic canvas.
