## ModelScript Architectural Rationale

ModelScript compiles and indexes multi-million-element engineering workspaces, including the complete Modelica Standard Library (MSL), SysML v2 standard libraries (KerML), ISO 10303 STEP schemata, and OWL2 domain ontologies.

Representing these vast semantic graphs using standard JavaScript object heaps incurs:

- Extreme memory bloat (JavaScript objects typically consume 40–80 bytes of overhead per node).
- Heavy Garbage Collector (GC) pressure and unpredictable pause times during interactive IDE editing.
- Slow pointer chasing across cache lines.

To solve this, ModelScript implements **compact, zero-GC data structures** operating directly inside WebAssembly 64-bit linear memory.

---

## Architecture of Core WASM Structures

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    WORKSPACE["Workspace Indexer & AST Symbols"] --> ROARING["Roaring Bitmaps<br/>12-byte Chunk Descriptors<br/>Array / Dense Bitset"]
    WORKSPACE --> TRIE["Front-Coded Dictionary<br/>Shared Prefixes (8-entry blocks)<br/>+ Robin Hood Hash Map"]
    WORKSPACE --> BTREE["Paged B+ Tree (4KB Slotted Pages)<br/>Subject-Predicate-Object (SPO)<br/>Predicate-Object-Subject (POS)"]
    ROARING --> SALSA["Salsa Query Dependency Tracking"]
    TRIE --> INTERN["Symbol & IRI ID Interning"]
    BTREE --> SPARQL["WCOJ Pattern Matching & SPARQL Engine"]
```

### 1. Unmanaged Roaring Bitmaps

Partitions the 32-bit integer space into $2^{16} = 65{,}536$ chunks based on the upper 16 bits:

- **12-Byte Chunk Descriptor**:
  ```
  Offset 0..3:   [key: u16] | [containerType: u16]
  Offset 4..7:   [containerPtr: u32]
  Offset 8..9:   [cardinality: u16]
  Offset 10..11: [capacity: u16]
  ```
- **Adaptive Containers**:
  - **Array Container**: Used when cardinality $< 4{,}096$. Elements are stored as sorted `u16` integers in linear memory.
  - **Bitmap Container**: When cardinality reaches $4{,}096$, the container automatically converts to a dense 8,192-byte bitset ($1{,}024 \times \text{u64}$ words), allowing bitwise `AND`, `OR`, `XOR` operations at hardware SIMD speeds.

### 2. Front-Coded String & IRI Dictionary

Engineering identifiers and semantic URIs often share massive common prefixes:

```
http://modelscript.io/sysml2/core#PartDefinition
http://modelscript.io/sysml2/core#ItemDefinition
http://modelscript.io/sysml2/core#ActionDefinition
```

The front-coded dictionary partitions sorted strings into blocks of size $K = 8$:

- **Header String**: Stored uncompressed at the beginning of each block.
- **Suffix Entries**: Encoded as `[commonPrefixLen: u8, suffixLen: u8, suffixBytes]`.
- **Hybrid Lookups**: Combines front-coding (achieving 75–85% memory compression) with a zero-cost 64-bit Robin Hood hash map (`UnmanagedMap64`) for $O(1)$ string-to-ID interning.

### 3. Paged 4KB Slotted B+ Tree

Stores billions of semantic assertions and relational tuples:

- **4KB Slotted Page Layout (32-byte header + 254 entries)**:
  ```
  [0..3]   pageId: u32
  [4..5]   pageType: u16 (1 = Leaf, 2 = Internal)
  [6..7]   itemCount: u16
  [8..11]  prevPage: u32 (doubly-linked leaf chain for range scans)
  [12..15] nextPage: u32
  [16..19] parentPage: u32
  [20..23] flags: u32
  [24..31] lsn: u64 (Log Sequence Number for crash consistency)
  ```
- **RDF-3X Triples**: Triples $(S, P, O)$ are indexed in clustered B+ tree leaf chains. Full index permutations (`SPO`, `POS`, `OSP`) permit fast range scans for multi-way graph joins without intermediate hash joins.

---

## Upstream & Downstream Integration

| Data Structure           | Upstream Dependencies                      | Downstream Consumers                                     |
| :----------------------- | :----------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------- |
| **RoaringBitmap**        | Symbol IDs from `SymbolIndexer`            | Invalidation sets in `QueryEngine`, type sets            |
| **FrontCodedDictionary** | AST string literals, Qualified names, URIs | Inter-file symbol resolution, memory-mapped LSP indexing |
| **PagedBTree**           | AST semantic relationships, OWL2 axioms    | Leapfrog Triejoin (WCOJ), graph query evaluators, SPARQL |

# CLI Overview

The `@modelscript/cli` package provides two identical binary executables: `modelscript` and its shorthand alias `msx`. The command-line interface serves as the primary headless automation driver for compiling, simulating, verifying, linting, rendering, and orchestrating polyglot engineering systems across local workspaces, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud HPC clusters.

## Installation

You can run the CLI directly from the monorepo workspace using `npx`, or install it globally for system-wide access:

```bash
# Run directly via npx
npx msx --help

# Install globally
npm install -g @modelscript/cli
msx --version
```

## Global Options & Environment Variables

The CLI parser (`apps/cli/src/main.ts`) intercepts global execution flags prior to command dispatch and respects standard environment variables for headless CI/CD and enterprise hub integration:

### Global Flags

| Flag        | Type      | Description                                                                                                                                                                    |
| :---------- | :-------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--daemon`  | `boolean` | Route command execution through the persistent background compiler daemon (`~/.modelscript/daemon.sock`) to bypass cold-start WASM initialization and reuse warm Salsa caches. |
| `--help`    | `boolean` | Display usage information and command-specific options.                                                                                                                        |
| `--version` | `boolean` | Print the installed `@modelscript/cli` semantic version.                                                                                                                       |

### Environment Variables

| Variable                                     | Default                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| :------------------------------------------- | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NO_COLOR`                                   | Unset                   | When set to any non-empty value, disables ANSI color sequences in terminal diagnostics, tables, and diff output.                                                                             |
| `ANSATZ_API_URL` / `MODELSCRIPT_API_URL`     | `http://localhost:3000` | Base URL for the Ansatz Platform, Package Registry, and Cloud HPC dispatch API (`~/.ansatzrc` / `~/.modelscriptrc` fallback).                                                                |
| `ANSATZ_API_TOKEN` / `MODELSCRIPT_API_TOKEN` | Unset                   | Bearer token (`JWT` or `ms_bot_*` service token) used for non-interactive authentication against the Registry, Cloud HPC, and Hub APIs (also accepts `ANSATZ_TOKEN` or `MODELSCRIPT_TOKEN`). |

## Persistent Compiler Daemon (`--daemon`)

Standard CLI invocations spin up an isolated Node.js process, compile or load `.wasm` parser binaries, and index workspace dependencies from disk. When iterating rapidly or running hundreds of checks in a pre-commit hook, pass `--daemon` to any command:

```bash
# Start or auto-spawn the background daemon and run lint with warm Salsa caches
msx lint model.mo --daemon

# Explicitly manage the daemon lifecycle
msx daemon status
msx daemon restart
msx daemon stop
```

When `--daemon` is passed, `msx` connects to the local Unix domain socket (`~/.modelscript/daemon.sock` on Linux/macOS or named pipe `\\.\pipe\modelscript-daemon` on Windows). If no daemon is running, the CLI automatically spawns one in the background, waits for readiness, and streams the command's `stdout`, `stderr`, and exit code back to the terminal.

## Return Codes & CI/CD Integration

All `msx` commands return POSIX-compliant exit codes suitable for gating GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins pipelines:

| Exit Code | Meaning                                                                                                             |
| :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `0`       | Command succeeded with zero errors (or all verification obligations proved `SAFE`).                                 |
| `1`       | Compilation error, static lint error (`severity: "error"`), counterexample falsification found, or runtime failure. |
| `2`       | Invalid CLI arguments, missing required flags, or unreadable input paths.                                           |

# CLI Commands Reference

This reference documents every command, subcommand, and flag registered in `@modelscript/cli` (`apps/cli/src/main.ts` and `apps/cli/src/commands/`). All commands can be invoked via `modelscript` or its shorthand alias `msx`, and any command can be accelerated with the global `--daemon` flag.

---

## Compilation, Simulation & Optimization

### `compile` / `flatten`

Compiles and flattens a hierarchical Modelica class into a canonical Differential-Algebraic Equation (DAE) representation in linear WebAssembly memory (`DAEBuilder`). `flatten` is an exact alias for `compile`.

### CLI Command: `compile <name> [paths..]`
Flatten or lower a Modelica, SysML v2, or domain engineering model to DAE, Modelica, SysML v2, SSP, or FMU

Options:
  - `--output, -o, --out <string>`: output file path for compiled representation
  - `--to, -t <string>`: target output representation (dae, modelica, sysml2, ssp, fmu) (default: "dae")
  - `--model, -m <string>`: explicit class/system name when first positional argument is a file
  - `--language, -l, --lang <string>`: explicit language ID override
  - `--modelica-path, -L <string>`: directories to search for Modelica libraries (colon-separated)
  - `--flattener, -F <string>`: Flattener backend: 'ts' (reference TS), 'wasm' (zero-GC kernel), 'hybrid' (WASM with TS fallback), or 'diff' (parity comparison) (default: "hybrid")
  - `--timing <boolean>`: report timing information for each stage as JSON to stderr (default: false)
  - `--memory-profile <boolean>`: profile memory usage across phases and report as JSON to stderr (default: false)

```bash
# Flatten a model using the hybrid WASM kernel with timing breakdowns
msx flatten Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Examples.ChuaCircuit -L ./libraries --timing
```

---

### `instantiate`

Instantiates a Modelica class via the Salsa `QueryEngine` and prints the resolved component hierarchy, inherited modifications, and bindings prior to DAE index reduction.

### CLI Command: `instantiate <name> <paths...>`
Instantiate and query AST structure of a Modelica model

---

### `simulate`

Compiles a model, performs Block Lower Triangular (BLT) Pantelides index reduction and tearing, and executes a numerical time-domain or steady-state simulation locally or on a remote Slurm HPC cluster.

### CLI Command: `simulate <name> [paths..]`
Simulate a Modelica model, SysML v2 system, FMU archive, or domain engineering deck

Options:
  - `--output, -o, --out <string>`: output file path for simulation results
  - `--model, -m <string>`: explicit class/system name when first positional argument is a file
  - `--language, -l, --lang <string>`: explicit language ID override
  - `--start-time <number>`: override experiment start time
  - `--stop-time <number>`: override experiment stop time
  - `--tolerance <number>`: override experiment tolerance
  - `--interval, --step-size, --output-interval <number>`: override experiment output interval / step size
  - `--format, -f <string>`: output format (default: "csv")
  - `--solver <string>`: ODE solver to use (default: "dopri5")
  - `--interface-type <string>`: FMI interface type when simulating an FMU: 'cs', 'me', or 'auto'
  - `--start-value <string>`: override FMU variable start value as name=value (repeatable)
  - `--input-file <string>`: CSV file providing time-varying input trajectories (time,u1,u2,...)
  - `--output-variable <string>`: variable name(s) to record in FMU simulation output (repeatable)
  - `--initial-fmu-state-file <string>`: restore serialized FMU state from file before stepping
  - `--final-fmu-state-file <string>`: save serialized FMU state to file after simulation finishes
  - `--log-fmi-calls <boolean>`: log all FMI C API calls and logger callbacks to stderr (default: false)
  - `--realtime <number>`: run simulation in real-time mode with given scale factor (e.g., 1.0 for 1x)
  - `--engine <string>`: simulation backend: js (pure JavaScript), arena (arena-native DoD), wasm (WebAssembly via emcc), c (native compiled), jit (in-memory JIT) (default: "js")
  - `--jit <boolean>`: enable in-memory JIT compilation engine (sub-15ms execution) (default: false)
  - `--timing <boolean>`: report timing information for each stage as JSON to stderr (default: false)
  - `--memory-profile <boolean>`: profile memory usage across phases and report as JSON to stderr (default: false)
  - `--jacobian`: Jacobian calculation method (default: "sparse")
  - `--flattener, -F <string>`: Flattener backend: 'ts' (reference TS), 'wasm' (zero-GC kernel), 'hybrid' (WASM with TS fallback), or 'diff' (parity comparison) (default: "hybrid")
  - `--steady-state <boolean>`: Solve steady-state initial equilibrium only without time integration (default: false)
  - `--cloud <boolean>`: dispatch simulation to ModelScript Cloud HPC cluster (default: false)
  - `--profile <string>`: cloud compute profile (standard, high-memory, gpu-a100, hpc-mpi-64) (default: "standard")
  - `--async <boolean>`: submit cloud job asynchronously and return immediately with Job ID (default: false)
  - `--poll-interval <number>`: polling interval in milliseconds for cloud simulation status (default: 1500)
  - `--output-dir <string>`: directory to write downloaded simulation result file (default: "./results")
  - `--api-url <string>`: override ModelScript API base URL

```bash
# Run a stiff DAE simulation using the 4th-order Rosenbrock solver and sparse symbolic Jacobians
msx simulate RLC_Circuit circuit.mo --stop-time 10.0 --solver rodas4p --engine arena --jacobian sparse --format csv > trajectory.csv

# Dispatch a heavy multi-domain simulation to the Cloud HPC cluster
msx simulate ThermalGrid plant.mo --cloud --profile high-cpu --stop-time 3600 --output-dir ./runs/thermal
```

---

### `optimize`

Formulates and solves a nonlinear Dynamic Optimization / Optimal Control Problem (OCP) over a flattened DAE using direct collocation and sequential quadratic programming (SQP).

### CLI Command: `optimize <name> <paths..>`
Solve an optimal control problem for a Modelica model

Options:
  - `--objective <string>`: cost integrand expression (e.g. "u^2")
  - `--controls <string>`: control variable names (comma-separated)
  - `--control-bounds <string>`: control bounds as var:min:max (comma-separated)
  - `--start-time <number>`: override start time
  - `--stop-time <number>`: override stop time
  - `--num-intervals <number>`: number of collocation intervals (default: 50)
  - `--tolerance <number>`: NLP convergence tolerance (default: 0.000001)
  - `--max-iterations <number>`: maximum SQP iterations (default: 200)
  - `--format`: output format (default: "csv")

```bash
msx optimize EV_BatteryPack vehicle.mo \
  --objective energyLoss \
  --controls currentCommand \
  --control-bounds "currentCommand:-200:200" \
  --stop-time 600 \
  --num-intervals 100 \
  --format json > optimal_profile.json
```

---

### `grad`

Computes forward, adjoint, or central finite-difference parameter sensitivities ($\nabla_{\mathbf{p}} J$) of scalar objective metrics with respect to model parameters.

### CLI Command: `grad <name> <paths..>`
Compute exact parameter sensitivities through simulation using continuous adjoints

Options:
  - `--params <string>`: comma-separated list of parameter names to differentiate
  - `--target <string>`: target state variable name to compute terminal sensitivity for (default: first state)
  - `--start-time <number>`: override experiment start time
  - `--stop-time <number>`: override experiment stop time
  - `--step <number>`: communication step size
  - `--json <boolean>`: output results as JSON (default: false)

---

### `surrogate`

Executes a Design of Experiments (DoE) campaign over a physics model, trains a Reduced-Order Model (ROM) surrogate, attaches convex-hull/bounding-box extrapolation guardrails, and exports standalone C, ONNX, or Modelica `.mo` blocks.

### CLI Command: `surrogate <name> [paths..]`
Train or import an AI surrogate model (ROM) and generate C, ONNX, or Modelica code

Options:
  - `--inputs <string>`: input parameter names (comma-separated)
  - `--input-bounds <string>`: input bounds as var:min:max (comma-separated)
  - `--outputs <string>`: output variable names (comma-separated)
  - `--strategy`: Design of Experiments (DoE) sampling strategy (default: "latin-hypercube")
  - `--num-samples <number>`: number of samples to generate (default: 50)
  - `--architecture`: Reduced Order Model (ROM) architecture (default: "mlp")
  - `--start-time <number>`: override start time
  - `--stop-time <number>`: override stop time
  - `--format`: target export format: C/WASM ('c'), ONNX graph ('onnx'), Modelica block ('mo'), or all ('all') (default: "c")
  - `--from-onnx <string>`: path to external ONNX JSON model file to import instead of training from Modelica source
  - `--extrapolation-guardrails <boolean>`: embed Modelica assertion guardrails for input bounds (default: true)
  - `--extrapolation-level`: severity level of Modelica extrapolation assertions (default: "warning")
  - `--extrapolation-flag <boolean>`: emit Boolean isExtrapolating output variable in Modelica (default: true)
  - `--out-file <string>`: output file name (defaults to <model>_surrogate.<ext>)
  - `--replace-component <string>`: name of component declaration in Modelica model to replace with surrogate
  - `--replace-out <string>`: output path for modified Modelica model with replaced component
  - `--report <string>`: output report JSON file (default: "report.json")

```bash
msx surrogate HeatExchanger thermal.mo \
  --inputs "massFlow,inletTemp" \
  --input-bounds "massFlow:0.1:5.0,inletTemp:280:380" \
  --outputs "outletTemp,pressureDrop" \
  --strategy sobol \
  --num-samples 128 \
  --architecture mlp \
  --format all \
  --out-file build/hx_rom
```

---

### `mc`

Runs high-throughput Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation across stochastic parameter distributions using worker threads and the linear-memory WASM evaluator.

### CLI Command: `mc <name> <paths..>`
Run Monte Carlo simulation

Options:
  - `--runs <number>`: Number of Monte Carlo runs (default: 1000)
  - `--threads <number>`: Number of parallel threads (default: 1)
  - `--params <string>`: Random variables in format name:dist:arg1:arg2 (comma-separated)
  - `--seed <number>`: PRNG seed
  - `--lhs <boolean>`: Use Latin Hypercube Sampling (default: false)
  - `--format`: Output format (default: "json")
  - `--output <string>`: Output file path (defaults to stdout if not provided)
  - `--engine <string>`: simulation backend: wasm or js (default: "wasm")

```bash
msx mc RLC_Filter filter.mo \
  --params "R:gaussian:100:5,C:uniform:1e-6:1.2e-6" \
  --runs 5000 \
  --lhs \
  --threads 8 \
  --seed 42 \
  --output mc_summary.json
```

### `csg`

Extracts Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) primitives and kinematic frame transformations from a Modelica class, writes `build/csg/execution_graph.json`, and invokes the OpenCASCADE (`@modelscript/cad`) worker to generate 3D CAD meshes.

### CLI Command: `csg <name> <paths...>`
Compile and extract CSG topologies to 3D meshes

## Linting, Formatting, Diffing & Compiler Inspection

### `lint`

Executes the static analysis pipeline (WASM GLR parse validation, CST lint rules, Salsa semantic queries, unit checking, and control-flow analysis) across one or more files or directories.

### CLI Command: `lint <path> [paths...]`
Lint polyglot libraries using QueryEngine and DSL parsers

Options:
  - `--language, -l, --lang <string>`: Filter to specific language (e.g. modelica, sysml2, owl2, scad, ssp, cfd, fea, pscad, fortran, easy5, rocets, lps, sima, gtsuite)
  - `--format, -f <string>`: Output format: terminal or json (default: "terminal")
  - `--profile <string>`: OWL 2 ontology profile to validate against (DL or EL) (default: "DL")
  - `--strict <boolean>`: Treat warnings as errors (default: false)

```bash
# Lint an entire polyglot workspace and emit JSON for CI processing
msx lint ./models ./requirements --format json
```

---

### `parse`

Parses a file using its registered native WebAssembly GLR parser (`parser.wasm`) and prints the concrete syntax tree (CST), node byte offsets, or parse errors.

### CLI Command: `parse <file>`
Parse a file using its language DSL parser (supports any registered language)

Options:
  - `--language, -l <string>`: Explicit language override (e.g. modelica, sysml2, scad, step, owl2, csv)
  - `--encoding <string>`: Input encoding to use (default: "utf8")

---

### `format`

Formats source files canonically using the grammar's CST-preserving pretty-printer while preserving comments and annotations.

### CLI Command: `format <files..>`
Format source files using their language DSL formatter or unparser

Options:
  - `--write, -w <boolean>`: Edit files in place (default: false)
  - `--check, -c <boolean>`: Check if files are formatted without writing (exits with code 1 if unformatted) (default: false)
  - `--language, -l <string>`: Explicit language override (e.g. modelica, sysml2, scad, step)
  - `--indent-size <number>`: Number of spaces per indentation level (default: 2)
  - `--preserve-formatting <boolean>`: Preserve original token layout where grammar permits (default: false)

---

### `unparse`

Parses a source file into linear CST memory and unparses it back into text to verify lossless round-trip grammar rules.

### CLI Command: `unparse <file>`
Unparse and re-synthesize clean source code from the language AST

Options:
  - `--output, -o <string>`: Output file path (default prints to stdout)
  - `--language, -l <string>`: Explicit language override
  - `--indent-size <number>`: Number of spaces per indentation level (default: 2)

---

### `diff`

Computes a structural CST/AST and semantic DAE comparison between two files (`oldFile` and `newFile`), identifying added/removed components, modified parameter bindings, and altered equations regardless of whitespace formatting.

### CLI Command: `diff <file1> <file2>`
Compute an AST-aware semantic diff between two model files (supports any registered DSL)

Options:
  - `--language, -l <string>`: Explicit language override (e.g. modelica, sysml2, scad)
  - `--order-agnostic <boolean>`: Ignore child order changes in declarative sections (e.g. equation sets) (default: true)
  - `--breaking-only <boolean>`: Only report breaking changes (API modifications, deleted connectors, type switches) (default: false)
  - `--format`: Output format (default: "terminal")
  - `--output, -o <string>`: Output file path for visual formats

---

### `pr-diff`

Generates visual schematic/architectural diffs (highlighting added components in green, modified in amber, and deleted in red) and PR review summaries between two Git revisions.

### CLI Command: `pr-diff [file]`
Compute visual and semantic pull request diff across Git revisions (SysML v2, Modelica)

Options:
  - `--base, -b <string>`: Base Git reference (branch, tag, or commit hash) (default: "HEAD~1")
  - `--head <string>`: Head Git reference (branch, commit hash, or omit for working tree)
  - `--format, -f`: Output format for the visual diff (default: "visual-html")
  - `--output, -o <string>`: Output file path (defaults to stdout or visual-diff.html / visual-diff.svg)
  - `--view, -v <string>`: SysML v2 viewpoint projection filter (e.g. All, BDD, IBD, StateMachine) (default: "All")
  - `--breaking-only <boolean>`: Only report breaking changes (default: false)
  - `--open <boolean>`: Automatically open generated visual HTML in default web browser (default: false)

---

### `i18n`

Extracts translatable descriptions, documentation strings, and identifier aliases from models (`extract`), compiles translation catalogs (`compile`), or translates a model into a target locale (`translate`).

### CLI Command: `i18n <paths..>`
Extract internationalization (.pot) translation templates from Modelica models

Options:
  - `--output, -o <string>`: path to the output .pot file

---

## Formal Verification, Safety & Test Synthesis

### `verify`

Unified formal verification and simulation validation for SysML v2 and Modelica: decision tables, assume-guarantee contracts, state machines, and optional flowpipe reachability. Results can be emitted as terminal output or as JSON, CTRF, JUnit, SARIF, HTML, or DHF reports for CI/CD and compliance workflows.

### CLI Command: `verify [target] [paths..]`
Unified formal verification and simulation validation for SysML v2 and Modelica

Options:
  - `--all <boolean>`: execute all applicable formal verification stages (default: false)
  - `--decisions <boolean>`: verify decision table exhaustiveness and determinism (default: true)
  - `--contracts <boolean>`: verify assume-guarantee contract compatibility and refinement (default: true)
  - `--state-machines <boolean>`: verify state machine and activity workflow soundness/deadlock-freedom (default: true)
  - `--flowpipe <boolean>`: enable validated continuous/hybrid reachability flowpipes (default: false)
  - `--order <number>`: Taylor model flowpipe expansion order (default: 4)
  - `--dt <number>`: time step size in seconds for flowpipe reachability
  - `--horizon <number>`: time horizon (stop time) in seconds for flowpipe reachability
  - `--initial-set <string>`: initial state set bounds (e.g. 'x=[0.9,1.1],y=[-0.1,0.1]')
  - `--barriers <boolean>`: enable sum-of-squares barrier certificate synthesis (default: false)
  - `--falsify <boolean>`: enable adversarial requirement falsification (default: false)
  - `--simulation <boolean>`: verify dynamic simulation trajectory requirements (default: true)
  - `--clearance <boolean>`: enable 3D CAD clearance and physical collision verification (default: false)
  - `--mcdc <boolean>`: synthesize 100% MC/DC independent condition test pairs (default: false)
  - `--b2b <boolean>`: verify Back-to-Back MiL-vs-SiL equivalence against standalone C99 (default: false)
  - `--b2b-tol <number>`: maximum allowable numerical tolerance between MiL and SiL (default: 0.0001)
  - `--b2b-compiler <string>`: host/target C compiler for SiL compilation (default: "gcc")
  - `--b2b-dt <number>`: fixed integration step size in seconds for SiL RK4
  - `--algorithms <boolean>`: execute sound algorithmic abstract interpretation for zero RTEs (default: true)
  - `--format <string>`: output report format: terminal, json, ctrf, junit, sarif, html, or dhf (default: "terminal")
  - `--report <string>`: write test report to specified file path
  - `--export <string>`: comma-separated list of formal spec export formats: smt2, nuxmv, ocra, mos
  - `--export-dir <string>`: target directory for exported formal specifications (default: ".")
  - `--flattener, -F <string>`: Flattener backend: 'ts', 'wasm', 'hybrid', or 'diff' (default: "hybrid")
  - `--engine <string>`: simulation backend: wasm or js (default: "wasm")
  - `--timing <boolean>`: output timing JSON to stderr (default: false)
  - `--update-hypergraph <boolean>`: synchronize verification verdicts directly into digital thread hypergraph (default: false)

```bash
# Verify a controller and emit a GitHub Code Scanning SARIF report
msx verify BrakingController brake.mo --format sarif --report results.sarif
```

---

### `falsify`

Performs optimization-guided falsification of Signal Temporal Logic (STL) safety properties ($\square_{[a,b]} \phi$, $\lozenge_{[a,b]} \phi$, $\phi_1 \mathcal{U}_{[a,b]} \phi_2$) by searching disturbance and parameter spaces to minimize quantitative robustness $\rho(\phi, \mathbf{x}, t) < 0$.

### CLI Command: `falsify`
Run adversarial multi-domain requirement falsification across SysML, Modelica, and CAD

Options:
  - `--property <string>`: Name of the target SysML requirement or property
  - `--sysml <string>`: Path to SysML v2 model file (.sysml)
  - `--modelica <string>`: Path to Modelica DAE model file (.mo)
  - `--cad <string>`: Path to CAD procedural file (.scad or .ts)
  - `--params <string>`: JSON array or file path containing parameter bounds
  - `--formula <string>`: STL formula JSON or predicate shorthand (e.g. 'stress <= 200')
  - `--algorithm`: Falsification global optimization algorithm (default: "de")
  - `--generations <number>`: Maximum optimization generations (default: 10)
  - `--population <number>`: Population size per generation (default: 12)
  - `--outTrace <string>`: Path to output CanonicalTraceRecord JSON
  - `--outCad <string>`: Path to output counterexample CAD model file

---

### `export-formal`

Translates SysML v2 models into external formal verification formats: SMT-LIB2, nuXmv, and OCRA contract specifications.

### CLI Command: `export-formal <paths..>`
Export SysML v2 models to standard formal verification formats (SMT-LIB2, nuXmv, OCRA)

Options:
  - `--format, -f <string>`: Target formal representation: 'smt2' (SMT-LIB v2.6), 'nuxmv' (nuXmv .smv), or 'ocra' (OCRA .oss) (default: "smt2")
  - `--output, -o <string>`: Output file path (prints to stdout if omitted)
  - `--logic <string>`: SMT-LIB logic directive (default: auto-detected QF_LRA or QF_NRA)
  - `--module, -m <string>`: Module name for nuXmv or top-level component name for OCRA (default: "System")
  - `--scope, -s <string>`: Scope filter for extracted constraints or state machines
  - `--invariants <string>`: Additional safety invariants (INVARSPEC) to emit for nuXmv
  - `--ltl <string>`: Temporal logic specifications (LTLSPEC) to emit for nuXmv
  - `--minimize <string>`: Parametric optimization objectives to minimize in SMT-LIB2
  - `--maximize <string>`: Parametric optimization objectives to maximize in SMT-LIB2

```bash
# Export a SysML v2 controller to a nuXmv model
msx export-formal acc.sysml --format nuxmv -o acc.smv
```

### CLI Command: `verify-decisions <paths..>`
Formally verify SysML v2 decision tables, decide nodes, and state guards for exhaustiveness and disjointness

Options:
  - `--json <boolean>`: Output verification results in structured JSON format (default: false)

### `decompose`

Performs structural subsystem partitioning and Assume-Guarantee ($A/G$) contract decomposition across large system models, checking whether top-level system guarantees follow compositionally from subsystem contracts ($\bigwedge_i (A_i \Rightarrow G_i) \vdash G_{\text{sys}}$).

### CLI Command: `decompose <paths..>`
Perform symbolic state-space region decomposition over SysML v2 decision conditions

Options:
  - `--max-regions, -r <number>`: Maximum number of regions to partition (default: 64) (default: 64)
  - `--max-depth, -d <number>`: Maximum branch condition exploration depth (default: 8) (default: 8)
  - `--json <boolean>`: Output regions in JSON format (default: false)

---

### `generate-tests`

Synthesizes deterministic test vectors and stimulus harnesses from model guard conditions and assertions to achieve Modified Condition/Decision Coverage (MC/DC) and boundary-value coverage.

### CLI Command: `generate-tests <paths..>`
Synthesize formal boundary-condition and 100% MC/DC test suites from SysML v2 models

Options:
  - `--format, -f <string>`: Output report format (terminal, json, ctrf, junit, modelica) (default: "terminal")
  - `--mcdc <boolean>`: Enforce 100% MC/DC condition-outcome test pair synthesis (default: true)
  - `--output, -o <string>`: Write generated test suite to file instead of stdout
  - `--model, -m <string>`: Target model name when generating Modelica .mos simulation scripts (default: "Model")

## Polyglot Digital Thread, Co-Simulation & Standards Interop

### `render`

Renders headless, publication-grade SVG diagrams for Modelica component icons/schematics, SysML v2 architectural views, and PSCAD Single-Line Diagrams (SLDs) using `@modelscript/diagram`.

### CLI Command: `render <name> [paths..]`
Render Modelica class diagram or icon to SVG

Options:
  - `--icon, -i <boolean>`: render icon (Modelica) (default: false)
  - `--view, -v <string>`: diagram view/projection (e.g. All, BDD, IBD, StateMachine, Activity, SLD, Taxonomy, Properties)
  - `--theme, -t`: color theme for polyglot SVG export (dark, light, blueprint) (default: "light")
  - `--output, -o <string>`: output SVG file path (defaults to stdout)

```bash
# Render a SysML v2 Internal Block Diagram in blueprint theme
msx render SpacecraftPower spacecraft.sysml --view IBD --theme blueprint -o docs/ibd.svg
```

---

### `fmu`

Exports a Modelica class as a Functional Mock-up Unit (`.fmu` ZIP archive) compliant with **FMI 2.0** and/or **FMI 3.0** for Model Exchange (`me`) and Co-Simulation (`cs`), or imports/inspects an existing `.fmu` via `msx fmu import <file.fmu>`. `export-fmu` is an alias for `fmu`.

### CLI Command: `fmu <name> [paths..]`
Export, validate, inspect, build, or simulate an FMU archive

Options:
  - `--output, -o <string>`: output file path (default: <name>.fmu or <name>.fmu.xml)
  - `--description <string>`: model description string
  - `--start-time <number>`: default experiment start time
  - `--stop-time <number>`: default experiment stop time
  - `--step-size, --output-interval <number>`: default experiment step size / output interval
  - `--tolerance <number>`: solver relative tolerance
  - `--xml-only <boolean>`: output only the modelDescription.xml (no archive) (default: false)
  - `--type <string>`: FMU type: 'me' (Model Exchange), 'cs' (Co-Simulation), 'both' (default) (default: "both")
  - `--interface-type <string>`: FMI interface type when simulating an FMU: 'cs', 'me', or 'auto'
  - `--solver <string>`: ODE solver when simulating an FMU in Model Exchange mode ('euler', 'rk4', 'cvode') (default: "rk4")
  - `--start-value <string>`: override FMU variable start value as name=value (repeatable)
  - `--input-file <string>`: CSV file providing time-varying input trajectories (time,u1,u2,...)
  - `--output-variable <string>`: variable name(s) to record in simulation output (repeatable)
  - `--initial-fmu-state-file <string>`: restore serialized FMU state from file before stepping
  - `--final-fmu-state-file <string>`: save serialized FMU state to file after simulation finishes
  - `--log-fmi-calls <boolean>`: log all FMI C API calls and logger callbacks to stderr (default: false)
  - `--format <string>`: simulation output format ('csv', 'json', 'none') (default: "csv")
  - `--target <string>`: export target: 'wasm' (WebAssembly), 'c' (C sources), 'js' (JavaScript), or 'all' (multi-target) (default: "all")
  - `--source <boolean>`: include C source files in the FMU archive (default: true)
  - `--compile <boolean>`: compile C sources into a shared library using the system C compiler (default: false)
  - `--fmi-version <string>`: FMI version to include: '2', '3', or 'both' (default: "both")
  - `--wasm <boolean>`: compile model to WebAssembly and include in the FMU archive (default: false)
  - `--flattener, -F <string>`: Flattener backend: 'ts' (reference TS), 'wasm' (zero-GC kernel), 'hybrid' (WASM with TS fallback), or 'diff' (parity comparison) (default: "hybrid")
  - `--golden <string>`: path to golden CSV trajectory for 'verify' subcommand
  - `--timing <boolean>`: report timing information for each stage as JSON to stderr (default: false)

```bash
# Export an FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation FMU with embedded C sources and WebAssembly binary
msx fmu DC_Motor motor.mo --fmi-version 3 --type cs --wasm --output build/DC_Motor.fmu
```

### `import-fmu`

Unpacks an external FMI 2.0 or FMI 3.0 `.fmu` archive, parses its `modelDescription.xml`, and generates a strongly typed Modelica wrapper `block` (and optional SSP system binding) so the FMU can be connected and simulated inside ModelScript. `fmu-import` is an alias for `import-fmu`.

### CLI Command: `import-fmu <fmu>`
Import an FMU archive and generate an acausal or causal Modelica wrapper

Options:
  - `--output, -o <string>`: Output path for the generated .mo file
  - `--package, -p <string>`: Enclosing package name (e.g. ImportedFMUs)
  - `--verbose, -v <boolean>`: Verbose output (default: false)

---

### `cosim`

Manages distributed FMI/SSP Co-Simulation master orchestration sessions, participant FMUs, recorded trajectory histories, and adaptive communication step-size optimization against the ModelScript Hub / Co-Simulation service.

### CLI Command: `cosim`
Co-simulation management (sessions, participants, FMUs, replay)

Options:
  - `--api-url <string>`: ModelScript API base URL (default: "http://localhost:3000")

| Subcommand     | Arguments     | Description                                                                                                         |
| :------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `status`       | —             | Display health and active worker metrics of the Co-Simulation master orchestrator.                                  |
| `sessions`     | —             | List active and completed distributed Co-Simulation sessions.                                                       |
| `participants` | `<sessionId>` | List connected FMU/simulator participants, port couplings, and current simulation time $t$ in a session.            |
| `fmus`         | —             | List registered FMU artifacts available in the Co-Simulation repository.                                            |
| `upload`       | `<path.fmu>`  | Upload a local `.fmu` archive to the Co-Simulation registry.                                                        |
| `replay`       | `<sessionId>` | Deterministically replay a recorded Co-Simulation session from its saved input/coupling log.                        |
| `history`      | `<sessionId>` | Fetch step-by-step coupling residuals, rollbacks, and trajectory history for a session.                             |
| `optimize`     | `<sessionId>` | Run post-mortem Richardson extrapolation analysis on a session to recommend optimal communication step sizes $H_i$. |

### `pscad`

Provides full lifecycle tooling for Manitoba Hydro **PSCAD** electromagnetic transient (EMT) workspaces (`.pscx` cases and `.pswx` workspaces), including domain-specific electrical linting, Single-Line Diagram (SLD) generation, EMT simulation, **IEEE Std 2800-2022** grid interconnection verification, and conversion to Modelica/SSP.

### CLI Command: `pscad <action> [files..]`
Inspect, lint, diff, and simulate PSCAD projects (.pscx, .pslx)

Options:
  - `--out, -o, --output <string>`: Output file path (for diagram SVG, Modelica, SSD, CSV, or COMTRADE export)
  - `--tstop, --stop-time, --duration <number>`: Simulation duration in seconds (default: 1)
  - `--step, --step-size, --dt <string>`: Simulation fixed time step (e.g. '20us' or 20e-6) (default: "20us")
  - `--format, -f <string>`: Result format for 'sim' with --out (base path): pscad (.out/.inf), psout (.psout), comtrade, comtrade-bin, cff (default: "pscad")

| Action            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| :---------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lint`            | Validate `.pscx`/`.pswx` schematics against electrical EMT rules (`M6001`–`M6011`, including floating nodes, transformer winding ratios, CSMF unconnected inputs, and traveling-wave line $\Delta t$ underflow). |
| `diagram`         | Render a publication-quality SVG Single-Line Diagram (SLD) from a `.pscx` project.                                                                                                                               |
| `diff`            | Compute a topological and parameter diff between two `.pscx` revisions.                                                                                                                                          |
| `sim`             | Execute a fixed-step nodal admittance ($\mathbf{G}\mathbf{v}(t) = \mathbf{i}_{\text{hist}}(t - \Delta t)$) EMT simulation.                                                                                       |
| `verify-ieee2800` | Run automated **IEEE Std 2800-2022** Inverter-Based Resource (IBR) compliance checks (Low/High Voltage Ride-Through LVRT/HVRT, frequency ride-through, and reactive current injection step response).            |
| `export-modelica` | Translate a `.pscx` schematic into an equivalent Modelica `.mo` model using `Modelica.Electrical`.                                                                                                               |
| `export-ssp`      | Package a `.pswx` multi-project workspace into an SSP 1.0 `.ssp` architecture container.                                                                                                                         |

```bash
# Verify IEEE 2800-2022 LVRT/HVRT compliance on a solar plant PSCAD case
msx pscad verify-ieee2800 SolarPlant_250MW.pscx --tstop 3.0 --step 20us -o ieee2800_report.json
```

### `polyglot`

Queries the unified multi-language `WorkspaceIndex`, verifies cross-domain traceability links (`@satisfies`, `@verifies`, `@allocates`), inspects digital threads, and monitors operational digital twin drift across all 44 supported languages.

### CLI Command: `polyglot <action>`
Multi-domain TGG projection, formal verification, and digital thread tracking

| Subcommand          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `project [dir]`     | Summarize all indexed languages, files, symbols, and cross-language bindings in a workspace.                                                                                                |
| `verify [dir]`      | Verify cross-language dimensional consistency, port types, requirement satisfaction, and digital thread integrity.                                                                          |
| `thread <symbol>`   | Trace the upstream/downstream polyglot digital thread for a symbol (from OWL2 ontology $\to$ SysML v2 requirement $\to$ Modelica equation $\to$ STEP CAD geometry $\to$ ReqIF/DHF dossier). |
| `query <expr>`      | Execute a cross-language symbol or FLWOR query against the unified `WorkspaceIndex`.                                                                                                        |
| `check-twins [dir]` | Compare live telemetry streams or CSV logs against nominal model predictions to detect parameter drift and anomalies.                                                                       |
| `index [dir]`       | Build and serialize the workspace-wide polyglot symbol and dependency index (`polyglot-index.json`).                                                                                        |

### `dhf`

Generates, inspects, and cryptographically audits **Design History File (DHF)** compliance dossiers structured for **FDA 21 CFR Part 820.30**, **ISO 13485**, **ISO 26262**, and **DO-178C** regulatory submissions.

### CLI Command: `dhf <action> [paths..]`
Design History File (FDA 21 CFR 820.30 / ISO 14971 / IEC 62304) regulatory compliance exporter

Options:
  - `--format, -f`: Output format (default: "markdown")
  - `--output, -o <string>`: File path to save the generated DHF dossier
  - `--title, -t <string>`: Dossier Title (default: "Design History File (DHF) — IEC 62304 / ISO 14971 Compliance Dossier")
  - `--device, -d <string>`: Target medical device or safety-critical system name (default: "Safety-Critical Cyber-Physical System (Class C)")
  - `--author, -a <string>`: Author name (default: "ModelScript Verification Engineering Team")

| Subcommand      | Description                                                                                                                                         |
| :-------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `export [path]` | Compile requirements traceability matrices (RTM), formal verification proofs, simulation summaries, and SHA-256 artifact hashes into a DHF dossier. |

### `olga`

Provides complete command-line tooling for Schlumberger **OLGA** transient multiphase flow models (`.opi`, `.key`, `.genkey`, `.tab`, `.tpl`, `.ppl`), including drift-flux hydrodynamic simulation, severe slugging analysis, PVT flash, autonomous history matching, and flow assurance verification.

### CLI Command: `olga <action> [files..]`
Simulate, lint, verify, and visualize OLGA multiphase flow models (.opi, .key, .genkey)

Options:
  - `--out, -o, --output <string>`: Output file path (e.g. for trajectory CSV, SVG diagram, or .fmu archive)
  - `--duration, -d, --stop-time, --tstop <number>`: Simulation duration in seconds [s]
  - `--dt, --step, --step-size <number>`: Simulation time step in seconds [s]
  - `--diameter <number>`: Pipeline internal diameter in meters [m] for bathymetry survey
  - `--cell-length <number>`: Maximum control volume cell length in meters [m] for bathymetry survey
  - `--restart <string>`: Path to checkpoint (.rst or .json) file to warm restart simulation from
  - `--checkpoint-out <string>`: Path to write simulation state checkpoint (.rst) at completion or periodically
  - `--checkpoint-interval <number>`: Periodic checkpoint snapshot interval in seconds [s]
  - `--tune <string>`: Comma-separated list of parameters to calibrate in 'tune' action (e.g. 'roughness,choke_cd,u_ambient')
  - `--max-evals <number>`: Maximum number of objective evaluations during history matching optimization (default: 150)
  - `--report <string>`: Path to write tuning Markdown report
  - `--view <string>`: Diagram view type: 'profile', 'schematic', 'pvt', 'wellbore', 'slug', 'bathy' (default: "profile")
  - `--to <string>`: Target format for conversion ('genkey', 'opi', 'sysml2') (default: "genkey")
  - `--maop <number>`: Maximum Allowable Operating Pressure limit in bar [bar] (default: 250)
  - `--margin <number>`: Required hydrate avoidance subcooling margin in Kelvin [K] (default: 3)
  - `--capacity <number>`: Topside slug catcher maximum liquid surge capacity in m³ [m³] (default: 150)
  - `--min-vel <number>`: Minimum gas turndown velocity in m/s [m/s] (default: 0.5)
  - `--max-surge <number>`: Maximum allowable topside slug catcher surge volume in m³ [m³] (default: 85)
  - `--min-hydrate-margin <number>`: Minimum required hydrate avoidance subcooling margin in Kelvin [K] (default: 3)
  - `--max-wax <string>`: Maximum allowable wax deposition layer thickness in mm [mm] (default: "2mm")
  - `--max-corrosion <string>`: Maximum allowable internal sweet CO2 corrosion rate in mm/year [mm/yr] (default: "0.1mm/yr")
  - `--out-report <string>`: Path to write Flow Assurance Gate Markdown summary report
  - `--fmi-version <string>`: FMI specification version for FMU export: '2.0', '3.0', or 'both' (default: "2.0")
  - `--macro-step <number>`: Co-simulation communication step size in seconds [s] (default: 1.0) (default: 1)
  - `--algorithm <string>`: Co-simulation coupling algorithm ('gauss-seidel' | 'jacobi') (default: "gauss-seidel")
  - `--comp <string>`: Feed composition string for EOS flash (e.g. 'C1:0.75,C2:0.10,C3:0.08,nC4:0.04,C7:0.03')
  - `--p <number>`: Operating pressure in bar [bar] for flash (default: 50.0) (default: 50)
  - `--t <number>`: Operating temperature in Kelvin or Celsius for flash (default: 300.15 K) (default: 300.15)
  - `--model <string>`: Cubic equation of state model ('pr' | 'srk') (default: "pr")
  - `--envelope <boolean>`: Trace two-phase saturation envelope (cricondenbar & cricondentherm) (default: false)
  - `--anti-slug <boolean>`: Enable active subsea topside closed-loop anti-slug controller during simulation (default: false)
  - `--slug-setpoint <number>`: Anti-slug riser base pressure setpoint in bar [bar] (default: 50.0) (default: 50)
  - `--slug-kp <number>`: Anti-slug PI proportional gain [1/Pa] (default: 1.5e-6) (default: 0.0000015)
  - `--slug-ti <number>`: Anti-slug PI integral time constant in seconds [s] (default: 30.0) (default: 30)
  - `--slug-washout <number>`: Anti-slug high-pass washout filter time constant in seconds [s] (default: 20.0) (default: 20)
  - `--slug-choke <number>`: Anti-slug baseline nominal choke opening [0..1] (default: 0.50) (default: 0.5)
  - `--trip <string>`: Dynamic well trip event specification (e.g. 'WELL_1:20' for shut-in at t=20s)
  - `--junction-vol <number>`: Gathering manifold junction accumulator volume in m³ [m³] (default: 5.0) (default: 5)

| Action        | Description                                                                                                                               |
| :------------ | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `inspect`     | Dump flowpath pipe discretization, valve configurations, sources, and boundary conditions.                                                |
| `lint`        | Run pre-flight flow assurance checks (`M7001`–`M7013`: CFL violations, severe slugging, pig stuck hazards, wax/asphaltene precipitation). |
| `simulate`    | Execute transient 1D drift-flux simulation with Lagrangian slug tracking and scraper pig dynamics.                                        |
| `verify`      | Check formal regulatory limits (MAOP, hydrate subcooling margin, slug surge volume, erosion limits).                                      |
| `diagram`     | Render SVG schematics, seabed bathymetry elevation profiles, PVT envelopes, or slug statistics.                                           |
| `tune`        | Run automated history matching against field measurement CSV telemetry.                                                                   |
| `flash`       | Compute Peng-Robinson (PR) or Soave-Redlich-Kwong (SRK) thermodynamic vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) flash.                               |
| `network`     | Solve coupled gathering network transients across multiple branches and subsea manifolds.                                                 |
| `cosim`       | Run multi-rate SSP co-simulation coupling flowlines with topside process facilities.                                                      |
| `to-dae`      | Lower flowline equations into ModelScript DAE arena.                                                                                      |
| `to-modelica` | Translate pipe and boundary networks into `Modelica.Fluid` models.                                                                        |

```bash
msx olga simulate subsea_tieback.opi --duration=3600 --out=traj.csv
msx olga lint deepwater_riser.genkey
msx olga diagram tieback.opi --view=profile --out=profile.svg
msx olga flash --comp="C1:0.75,C2:0.10,C3:0.08,nC4:0.04,C7:0.03" --p=50 --t=295.15 --envelope
```

  - `--slack <boolean>`: Evaluate open-channel slack line gravity flow on downhill pipes (default: false)

| :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `inspect`     | Dump pipeline pipes, compressors, pumps, delivery regulators, and receipt nodes.                   |
| `lint`        | Check for MAOP overpressure (`M8001`), compressor surge (`M8002`), and high hydrogen blend ratios. |
| `simulate`    | Run transient fluid network pressure propagation and inventory line pack calculations.             |
| `solve`       | Solve the steady-state network.                                                                    |
| `linepack`    | Compute pipeline inventory (line pack).                                                            |
| `sysml`       | Project pipeline topology and control station hierarchies into OMG SysML v2.                       |
| `verify`      | Run design and safety verification on the steady-state solution.                                   |
| `to-modelica` | Project pipe network into `Modelica.Fluid` gas/liquid transmission models.                         |
| `to-dae`      | Lower Euler gas/liquid equations directly into `DAEBuilder` arena.                                 |

# Polyglot Language Ecosystem

ModelScript is not a single-language compiler—it is a **polyglot systems engineering framework**. All engineering languages share the same WebAssembly GLR parser compiler (`@modelscript/dsl`), the same `SymbolIndex` and `WorkspaceIndex` architecture, and the same Triple Graph Grammar (TGG) synchronization engine.

## Unified Polyglot Pipeline

Every language plugin implements the `LanguageDefinition` interface (`packages/dsl/src/language.ts`):

1. **Grammar DSL (`defineGrammar`)**: Compiled Ahead-of-Time into a compact `.wasm` binary parser table.
2. **Symbol Indexer (`SymbolIndexer`)**: Walks the linear-memory CST and populates `SymbolEntry` declarations into the global `WorkspaceIndex`.
3. **Salsa Queries (`queries`)**: Memoized semantic analyses (type resolution, unit inference, structural validation).
4. **Compiler Lints (`lints`)**: Real-time diagnostics surfaced identically in the CLI (`msx lint`), LSP server, and Web IDE.
5. **TGG Rules (`tggRules`)**: Declarative bidirectional synchronization rules linking AST nodes across languages (e.g., `SysMLv2 PartUsage` $\leftrightarrow$ `Modelica Component` $\leftrightarrow$ `STEP Product` $\leftrightarrow$ `ModelScript Struct`).

# ModelScript (`.msx`, `.modelscript`)

`@modelscript/modelscript` (`languages/modelscript`) is the native **ModelScript** systems modeling and query language. It combines zero-cost linear-memory data layout control (`@unmanaged struct`), WebAssembly/C++ native compilation, and declarative XQuery-inspired **FLWOR** (`for`–`let`–`where`–`order by`–`return`) queries over polyglot engineering graphs.

---

## Supported Extensions & Dialects

| Extension      | Description                         |
| :------------- | :---------------------------------- |
| `.msx`         | Canonical ModelScript source module |
| `.modelscript` | Long-form ModelScript source module |

---

## Language Features & Grammar

The native WebAssembly GLR parser (`languages/modelscript/src/language.ts`) parses `.msx` modules into a compact Concrete Syntax Tree (CST) with five primary syntactic constructs:

### 1. Module Imports

Import declarations bind symbols from external ModelScript modules or polyglot engineering artifacts:

```ts
import { ThermalNode, Conductance as G } from "./thermal_kernel.msx";
```

### 2. Unmanaged Linear-Memory Structs (`@unmanaged struct`)

Structs annotated with `@unmanaged` are packed directly into 32-bit WebAssembly linear memory without garbage-collected wrapper allocation:

```ts
@unmanaged struct StateVector {
  id: u32;
  temperature: f64;
  pressure: f64;
  active: bool;
}
```

### 3. Type System

- **Primitive Types**: `i32`, `u32`, `i64`, `u64`, `f32`, `f64`, `bool`, `string`, `usize`, `void`
- **Generic & Pointer Types**: `Array<T>`, `Slice<T>`, `ptr<T>`
- **User-Defined Structs**: Any declared `struct` identifier

### 4. Functions, Statements & Control Flow

Functions declare strongly typed parameters and return types, supporting `let` and `const` variable bindings, `if`/`else` branches, `while` loops, C-style `for` loops, and member/index expressions:

```ts
const BOLTZMANN: f64 = 1.380649e-23;

function computeHeatFlux(k: f64, area: f64, dT: f64, dx: f64): f64 {
  if (dx <= 0.0) {
    return 0.0;
  }
  let flux: f64 = -k * area * (dT / dx);
  return flux;
}
```

### 5. Declarative FLWOR Queries

ModelScript embeds first-class **FLWOR** (`for`–`let`–`where`–`order by`–`return`) expressions directly in the expression grammar for querying collections, CST nodes, and simulation trajectories:

```ts
let criticalNodes =
  for node in nodes
  let margin := node.limit - node.temperature
  where margin < 15.0 && node.active == true
  order by margin asc
  return { id: node.id, margin: margin };
```

---

## Multi-Target Compiler (`ModelScriptCompiler`)

`ModelScriptCompiler` (`languages/modelscript/src/index.ts`) lowers the linear-memory CST across three code generation backends:

| Backend           | Emitter Class   | API Methods                                                                        | Target Output                                                                                   |
| :---------------- | :-------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **JavaScript**    | `JsEmitter`     | `compileToJs(source)` / `executeJs(source, context)`                               | Executable ES module with lowered FLWOR pipelines (`.filter().sort().map()`)                    |
| **WebAssembly**   | `WasmEmitter`   | `compileToWat(source)` / `compileToWasm(source)` / `executeWasm(source, fn, args)` | Textual WAT S-expressions and binary `.wasm` modules with `@unmanaged` linear-memory offsets    |
| **Native Binary** | `NativeEmitter` | `compileToNative(source, { outPath, entryFn?, cc?, cflags? })`                     | WASM lowered to C via `wasm2c`, then compiled with the host C compiler (`$CC`, default `clang`) |

```ts
import fs from "node:fs";
import { ModelScriptCompiler } from "@modelscript/modelscript";

const compiler = new ModelScriptCompiler();
await compiler.init();

const source = fs.readFileSync("kernel.msx", "utf8");
const { js } = compiler.compileToJs(source); // ES module source
const wasm = await compiler.compileToWasm(source); // Uint8Array
const result = await compiler.executeWasm(source, "main", []);
const binary = await compiler.compileToNative(source, { outPath: "build/kernel" }); // requires wasm2c + clang
```

---

## Command Line Interface (`msx compile` & `msx lint`)

Compile, lint, and run ModelScript source modules directly from the terminal:

```bash
# Lint ModelScript modules for syntax, type errors, and unmanaged struct layout
msx lint kernel.msx

# Compile a ModelScript module into flattened DAE or WebAssembly bytecode
msx compile MainModule kernel.msx --flattener=wasm --timing
```

---

## Salsa Query Engine & Linear-Memory Struct Layout

`ModelScriptQueryEngine` (`languages/modelscript/src/queries.ts`) provides memoized semantic queries over the CST:

- **`structLayout(rawStructNode)`**: Computes deterministic 32-bit WebAssembly linear-memory byte layouts (`StructLayout`) for every `struct_declaration`:
  - `bool`: 1 byte (alignment 1)
  - `i32`, `u32`, `f32`, `usize`, `string`, `ptr<T>`, `Array<T>`, `Slice<T>`: 4 bytes (alignment 4)
  - `i64`, `u64`, `f64`: 8 bytes (alignment 8)
  - Automatically inserts natural alignment padding (`alignOffset`) between fields and aligns the total struct byte size to the maximum field alignment (`maxAlign`).
- **`inferExpressionType(rawNode, scope)`**: Infers static types across literals, binary/unary expressions, struct field access, function calls, and FLWOR `return` clauses (`Array<ReturnType>`).

---

## Semantic Linter & Error Codes

`ModelScriptLinter` (`languages/modelscript/src/linter.ts` and `languages/modelscript/src/errors.ts`) enforces 10 static analysis rules across syntax, name resolution, type checking, FLWOR clauses, and struct/function calls:

### Diagnostics for ModelScript (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M1001` | error | `parse-error` | Parse error. |
| `M2001` | error | `undefined-variable` | Variable '<name>' is not declared in current scope. |
| `M2002` | error | `duplicate-declaration` | Identifier '<name>' is already declared in this scope. |
| `M2003` | error | `unknown-type` | Type '<typeName>' is not recognized. |
| `M3001` | error | `type-mismatch` | Type mismatch: cannot assign '<sourceType>' to '<targetType>'. |
| `M3002` | error | `invalid-binary-operand` | Operator '<op>' cannot be applied to operands of type '<type>'. |
| `M4001` | error | `non-iterable-collection` | Expression '<expr>' in 'for' clause is not iterable. |
| `M4002` | error | `flwor-unbound-variable` | Variable '<varName>' in FLWOR clause is not bound in preceding 'for' or 'let' clauses. |
| `M5001` | error | `argument-count-mismatch` | Function '<fnName>' expects <expected> arguments, but got <actual>. |
| `M5002` | error | `unknown-struct-field` | Struct '<structName>' has no field named '<fieldName>'. |

---

## Polyglot TGG Rules

`@modelscript/modelscript` registers two Triple Graph Grammar (TGG) synchronization rules in `languages/modelscript/src/language.ts` for bidirectional projection with Modelica:

| Rule Name                           | Source Pattern        | Target Pattern (`modelica`)     | Semantics                                                                                              |
| :---------------------------------- | :-------------------- | :------------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ModelScriptStructToModelicaRecord` | `StructDeclaration`   | `ClassDefinition` (`record`)    | Synchronizes a `@unmanaged struct` declaration with a Modelica `record` definition                     |
| `ModelScriptParamToModelicaMod`     | `VariableDeclaration` | `ComponentClause` (`parameter`) | Synchronizes a top-level constant or variable binding with a Modelica component parameter modification |

CANONICAL URL: https://modelscript.org/languages/modelica

# Modelica 3.x (`.mo`)

`@modelscript/modelica` (`languages/modelica`) is the flagship physical modeling language of ModelScript. It provides a complete Modelica 3.x compiler pipeline—from a native WebAssembly GLR parser and Salsa query engine to an AssemblyScript/TypeScript arena flattener (`ModelicaFlattener`) and the full Modelica Standard Library (MSL 4.0.0).

---

## Compilation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    MO[".mo Source"] --> GLR["WASM GLR Parser"]
    GLR --> IDX["SymbolIndexer & WorkspaceIndex"]
    IDX --> SALSA["QueryEngine (Salsa)"]
    SALSA --> LINT["CompilerLints & Semantic Lints"]
    SALSA --> FLAT["ModelicaFlattener (Hybrid WASM/TS)"]
    FLAT --> DAE["DAEBuilder (Linear Memory)"]
    DAE --> SIM["BLT / Pantelides / IDA / CVODE / WebGPU"]
```

---

## Core Language Coverage

- **Class Specializations**: `model`, `block`, `connector`, `expandable connector`, `record`, `type`, `package`, `function`, `operator`, `operator record`, `operator function`
- **Inheritance & Redeclarations**: Multiple `extends`, `redeclare`, `replaceable`, `constrainedby`, `inner` / `outer` dynamic scoping, and deep hierarchical class modifications
- **Equations & Algorithms**: Differential equations (`der(x)`), `connect(a, b)` (both potential/flow and `stream` connectors), `if`/`for`/`when` equations, `initial equation`, and imperative `algorithm` / `initial algorithm` sections
- **Synchronous Clocks (Modelica 3.3+)**: `Clock`, `sample`, `hold`, `previous`, `subSample`, `superSample`, `shiftSample`, `backSample`

---

## Polyglot & Physical Extensions (`languages/modelica/src/extensions/`)

Beyond standard Modelica 3.x, `@modelscript/modelica` includes first-class compiler extensions for 3D CAD geometry, multiphysics FEA/CFD studies, formal verification, and localization:

1. **Embedded 3D CSG & STEP Export (`shape-flattener.ts`, `csg.ts`, `cad.ts`)**:
   - `ShapeFlattener` extracts `Modelica.Mechanics.MultiBody.Visualizers.FixedShape` components, parametric dimensions, and `Placement` transformations directly from flattened models.
   - Compiles visualizers into parametric OpenSCAD scripts (`npx msx csg ModelName file.mo`) or exports watertight ISO 10303-21 STEP B-Rep geometry via the `modelscript/exportShapeToStep` LSP command.
2. **Embedded FEA & CFD Multiphysics Studies (`study-flattener.ts`, `studies.ts`)**:
   - `StudyFlattener` (`modelscript/flattenStudy`) extracts embedded structural and fluid study annotations, material properties, and boundary conditions from Modelica components to synthesize CalculiX (`.inp`) and SU2 (`.cfg`) solver decks.
3. **Octagon Abstract Interpretation & Formal Safety Verification (`src/formal/`)**:
   - `ModelicaCfgLowerer` (`modelica-cfg-lowerer.ts`), `ModelicaAbstractEvaluator` (`modelica-abstract-evaluator.ts`), and `ModelicaStaticAnalyzer` (`modelica-analyzer.ts`) lower flattened DAE equations and `algorithm` statements into relational Control Flow Graphs evaluated over the **Octagon Abstract Domain** ($\pm x_i \pm x_j \le c$).
   - `PhysicalInvariantBridge` (`physical-invariant-bridge.ts`) proves division-by-zero freedom, square-root/logarithm domain safety, and physical state invariants (`domain.octagon()`).
4. **Gettext `.po` / `.pot` Internationalization (`po.ts`)**:
   - Extracts translatable description strings and `Dialog`/`Documentation` annotations into GNU Gettext `.pot` templates and merges localized `.po` catalogs (`npx msx i18n`).

---

## Semantic Linter (`languages/modelica/src/lints/`)

ModelScript enforces 307 OpenModelica-compatible diagnostic rules across six modular analyzers:

| Module                             | Representative Checks                                                                                             |
| :--------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `syntax-placement.ts`              | `M1001`–`M1003`: Parse errors, missing tokens, empty array constructors                                           |
| `queries.ts`                       | `M2001`–`M2005`: Duplicate elements, unresolved variables/classes/modifiers, identifier mismatches                |
| `types-expressions.ts`             | `M3001`–`M3006`: Binding/modifier/argument type mismatches, array dimension checks                                |
| `hierarchy-variability.ts`         | `M4001`–`M4005`: Circular `extends`, duplicate modifications, `protected` access violations, variability ordering |
| `connections-streams.ts`           | `M3003`–`M3004`: Connector plug-compatibility, stream connector rules, cardinality checks                         |
| `synchronous-clocks.ts` & `cfa.ts` | Clock partitioning rules, uninitialized discrete variables, structural singularity diagnostics                    |

## Modelica MCP Server Tools (`@modelscript/mcp`)

The `@modelscript/mcp` server and `@modelscript/modelica` MCP adapter expose 9 Modelica domain tools (plus polyglot closed-loop synthesis and calibration tools) to AI agents:

| MCP Tool                  | Description                                                                                                              |
| :------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `modelica_load`           | Loads `.mo` files or Modelica Standard Library packages into the persistent workspace session                            |
| `modelica_parse`          | Parses Modelica source code with the WASM GLR parser and returns CST nodes and syntax diagnostics                        |
| `modelica_flatten`        | Flattens a Modelica class via `ModelicaFlattener` and returns the flat Modelica DAE representation                       |
| `modelica_lint`           | Runs all 307 semantic and structural lint rules on a Modelica file or package                                            |
| `modelica_simulate`       | Flattens, runs BLT/index reduction, integrates the DAE over $[t_0, t_{\text{stop}}]$, and returns trajectory time-series |
| `hybrid_simulate`         | Executes a hybrid continuous Modelica DAE + discrete-event DEVS simulation                                               |
| `modelica_doe`            | Executes a multi-parameter Design of Experiments (Full Factorial / Latin Hypercube) batch sweep                          |
| `modelica_sensitivity`    | Computes local finite-difference or forward sensitivity matrices $\partial y_i / \partial p_j$ for target outputs        |
| `modelica_query`          | Queries the Salsa `QueryEngine` for class components, resolved types, variabilities, and modifications                   |
| `modelica_diff_calibrate` | Calibrates Modelica parameters against target CSV trajectory data via L-BFGS / Adam gradient optimization                |

---

## SysML v2 Transformer & Polyglot TGG Rules

- **Direct AST Transformer (`modelicaToSysML2` in `languages/modelica/src/transformers/sysml2.ts`)**: Converts complete Modelica packages and models into idiomatic SysML v2 textual notation (`part def`, `port def`, `attribute`, `connect`).
- **10 Bidirectional TGG Rules (`languages/modelica/src/language.ts`)**:
  - **Modelica $\leftrightarrow$ SysML v2 (6 rules)**: `ModelicaModelToSysML2PartDef`, `ModelicaConnectorToSysML2PortDef`, `ModelicaComponentToSysML2Part`, `ModelicaParameterToSysML2Attribute`, `ModelicaConnectorInstanceToSysML2Port`, `ModelicaConnectToSysML2Connection`
  - **Modelica $\leftrightarrow$ OWL2 (2 rules)**: `ModelicaModelToOWL2Class`, `ModelicaParameterToOWL2DataProperty`
  - **Modelica $\leftrightarrow$ STEP (2 rules)**: `ModelicaRevoluteToStepRevolute`, `ModelicaPrismaticToStepPrismatic`

# SysML v2 & KerML (`.sysml`, `.sysml2`, `.kerml`)

`@modelscript/sysml2` (`languages/sysml2`) implements the OMG **Systems Modeling Language v2 (SysML v2)** and **Kernel Modeling Language (KerML)** textual notation, pairing a bundled KerML/SysML v2 standard library snapshot with a suite of formal verification, safety analysis, direct DAE compilation, and enterprise synchronization engines.

---

## Supported Extensions

| Extension           | Description                                                                            |
| :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.sysml`, `.sysml2` | OMG SysML v2 textual architecture, requirement, state, action, and verification models |
| `.kerml`            | OMG Kernel Modeling Language (KerML) metamodel & library definitions                   |

---

## Supported SysML v2 Constructs

- **Structural Modeling**: `package`, `part def`, `part`, `attribute def`, `attribute`, `item def`, `item`, `port def`, `port`, `connection def`, `connection`, `interface def`, `interface`, `flow`, `allocation def`, `allocate`
- **Behavioral & State Modeling**: `action def`, `action`, `state def`, `state`, `transition`, `First` / `then` succession flows, `fork`, `join`, `decide`, `merge`, ` calc def`, `calc`
- **Requirements & Verification**: `requirement def`, `requirement`, `satisfy`, `verify`, `verification def`, `concern`, `stakeholder`, `view`, `viewpoint`, `constraint def`, `constraint`, `assume`, `require`

---

## Formal Verification & Safety Analysis Engines

`@modelscript/sysml2` includes seven specialized formal verification modules in `languages/sysml2/src/`:

1. **Activity Control-Flow & Petri-Net Soundness (`activity-cfa.ts`, `activity-soundness.ts`, `activity-verifier.ts`)**:
   - Lowers SysML v2 `action def` successions (`first A then B`), `fork`/`join`, and `decide`/`merge` nodes into Workflow Nets (1-safe Petri nets).
   - Verifies **Option to Complete**, **Proper Completion**, **No Dead Transitions**, **Lack of Synchronization** (parallel branches converging into a `merge` instead of a `join`), and **Deadlock at Join** (exclusive `decide` branches converging into a `join`).
2. **Decision Table Completeness & Disjointness (`decision-table-verifier.ts`)**:
   - Analyzes guarded `decide` branches and requirement tables via interval covering and SMT/constraint checking to detect **Missing Cases** (uncovered input domain gaps) and **Overlapping Rules** (non-deterministic guard collisions).
   - Exposed via CLI: `npx msx verify-decisions architecture.sysml`.
3. **Assume-Guarantee Contract Verification (`contract-verifier.ts`, `multidomain-contract-bridge.ts`)**:
   - Extracts `assume constraint { ... }` and `require constraint { ... }` blocks from `requirement def` and `part def` hierarchies.
   - Verifies **Contract Compatibility** ($\bigwedge A_{\text{env}} \neq \bot$) and **Refinement Soundness** across composite sub-parts ($A_{\text{parent}} \Rightarrow A_{\text{child}}$ and $\bigwedge G_{\text{children}} \Rightarrow G_{\text{parent}}$), bridging directly into the Multi-Domain Theory Coordinator.
4. **Hierarchical State Machine Verifier (`state-machine-verifier.ts`)**:
   - Checks `state def` machines for **Unreachable States**, **Deadlock / Trap States** (non-final states with no outgoing transitions), **Non-Deterministic Transitions** (overlapping guards on the same trigger event), and **Missing Initial States**.
5. **Hybrid Automaton Flowpipe Bridge (`hybrid-flowpipe-bridge.ts`)**:
   - Couples discrete SysML v2 `state def` mode transitions with continuous Modelica DAE dynamics to compute Taylor-model / interval reachability flowpipes and verify that unsafe states are unreachable over time horizon $[0, T]$.
6. **Fault Tree & Physics-Informed Safety Analyzer (`safety-analyzer.ts`, `physics-safety-bridge.ts`)**:
   - Synthesizes Fault Trees from SysML v2 failure modes and interconnections, computes **Minimal Cut Sets (MCS)** via MOCUS/top-down boolean reduction, evaluates top-event failure probabilities, and cross-checks physical failure thresholds against simulated Modelica/FEA/CFD peak stresses and temperatures.
7. **Boundary-Value & MC/DC Test Vector Synthesizer (`boundary-test-synthesizer.ts`)**:
   - Automatically generates boundary-value ($x = c - \epsilon, c, c + \epsilon$) and Modified Condition/Decision Coverage (**MC/DC**) test vectors for every `requirement def` and `calc def` constraint.
   - Exposed via CLI: `npx msx generate-tests architecture.sysml`.

---

## Direct SysML v2 $\rightarrow$ DAE Lowering & Enterprise Interchange

- **Direct Arena DAE Lowering (`sysml2-dae-lowerer.ts`)**: Compiles SysML v2 `calc def`, `constraint def`, `attribute` bindings, and `flow` connections directly into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` without requiring an intermediate Modelica code-generation pass.
- **`.sysmlx` JSON-LD & Container Export (`sysmlx-interchange.ts`, `sysml2-container-exporter.ts`)**: Serializes and imports OMG SysML v2 REST/JSON-LD payloads (`.sysmlx`) and multi-artifact engineering containers.
- **Enterprise MBSE Gateway (`enterprise-sync-gateway.ts`)**: Synchronizes SysML v2 packages, elements, and cross-domain traceability links with **Dassault Cameo Teamwork Cloud (TWC)**, **OpenMBEE MMS**, and standard **OMG SysML v2 REST API** repositories (`npx msx sysml sync`).

---

## Polyglot TGG Rules (22 Cross-Domain Mappings)

`@modelscript/sysml2` defines 22 bidirectional Triple Graph Grammar (TGG) rules in `languages/sysml2/src/language.ts` spanning **Modelica** (14 rules), **OWL2** (5 rules), and **STEP** (3 rules):

| Target Language           | Rule Names                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| :------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **`modelica` (14 rules)** | `SysML2PartDefToModelicaModel`, `SysML2AttributeDefToModelicaType`, `SysML2PortDefToModelicaConnector`, `SysML2ConnectionDefToModelicaModel`, `SysML2ActionDefToModelicaBlock`, `SysML2ConstraintDefToModelicaBlock`, `SysML2RequirementDefToModelicaBlock`, `SysML2PartToModelicaComponent`, `SysML2AttributeToModelicaParameter`, `SysML2PortToModelicaConnector`, `SysML2ConnectionToModelicaConnect`, `SysML2FlowToModelicaConnect`, `SysML2StateToModelicaBlock`, `SysML2TransitionToModelicaWhen` |
| **`owl2` (5 rules)**      | `SysML2PartDefToOWL2Class`, `SysML2AttributeUsageToOWL2DataProperty`, `SysML2PortUsageToOWL2ObjectProperty`, `SysML2PartUsageToOWL2Individual`, `SysML2RequirementToOWL2Class`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **`step` (3 rules)**      | `SysML2PartDefToStepProduct`, `SysML2PartUsageToStepAssemblyUsage`, `SysML2AttributeToStepProperty`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
