# MSC Adams Multibody Dynamics

ModelScript features comprehensive, native support for **MSC Adams** (`.adm`, `.cmd`), the classic industrial standard for mechanical systems simulation and multibody dynamics (MBD). Engineers can parse legacy Adams View command files and solver datasets, perform Grübler-Kutzbach spatial mobility analysis, evaluate 3D joint constraint residuals, and project mechanisms to modern SIMPACK and Modelica formats.

---

## Capabilities & Supported Formats

| Format                      | Extension | Description                                                                                                                                                           |
| :-------------------------- | :-------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Adams Solver Dataset**    | `.adm`    | Numerical dataset specifying rigid parts (`PART`), marker frames (`MARKER`), kinematic joints (`JOINT`), force elements (`SPRINGDAMPER`, `BUSHING`), and constraints. |
| **Adams View Command File** | `.cmd`    | Interactive parametric command scripts defining mechanism geometry, design variables, and simulation runs.                                                            |

### Key Architectural Features

- **Lexer & Parser:**
  - Robust deck ingestion supporting scientific notation (`1.5D-03`), inline comments (`!`), line continuations (`...`), and block cards.
  - Lossless serialization back to standardized `.adm` solver format via `serializeAdams()`.
- **Spatial 3D Kinematics:**
  - Full evaluation of Euler 3-1-3 and Tait-Bryan 1-2-3 rotation matrices.
  - Analytical joint constraint formulation for standard spatial joint primitives (Revolute, Spherical, Prismatic, Cylindrical, Planar, Universal).
- **Grübler-Kutzbach Mobility Analysis:**
  - Calculates mechanism degrees of freedom ($M = 6(n - 1) - \sum c_i$).
  - Identifies redundant kinematic constraints and overconstrained multi-loop linkages.
- **Multibody Linters (`M7301`–`M7310`):**
  - Flags missing ground parts, dangling marker references, unphysical inertia tensors violating the triangle inequality ($I_{xx} + I_{yy} \ge I_{zz}$), massless moving parts, and negative spring/damping parameters.
- **Cross-Domain Projections:**
  - **SIMPACK MBD:** Maps parts, markers, and spatial joints to SIMPACK `.spck` XML models.
  - **Modelica MultiBody:** Synthesizes standard `Modelica.Mechanics.MultiBody` parts and joint components.

---

## Command Line Interface (`msx adams`)

```bash
msx adams <action> [files...] [options]
```

| Action            | Description                                                                    | Key Options                                                     |
| :---------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **`lint`**        | Runs structural validation, inertia verification, and kinematic sanity checks. | —                                                               |
| **`mobility`**    | Evaluates spatial degrees of freedom and overconstrained loops.                | —                                                               |
| **`to-simpack`**  | Projects Adams mechanism to SIMPACK XML (`.spck`).                             | `--out=<file.spck>`                                             |
| **`to-modelica`** | Projects Adams mechanism to `Modelica.Mechanics.MultiBody`.                    | `--out=<file.mo>`                                               |
| **`simulate`**    | Lowers to a DAE and integrates it in time.                                     | `--stop-time`, `--step`, `--stabilization=baumgarte\|algebraic` |

### Examples

```bash
# Calculate mechanism spatial degrees of freedom
msx adams mobility FourBarLinkage.adm

# Validate inertia tensors and marker references
msx adams lint LandingGear.adm

# Convert Adams dataset into SIMPACK XML format
msx adams to-simpack RobotArm.adm --out=RobotArm.spck

# Compute mechanism mobility (degrees of freedom)
msx adams mobility ExcavatorMechanism.adm
```

---

| `M7307` | warning | `coincident-joint-markers` | Joint '<jointId>' uses identical I and J markers ('<iMarker>'). |
| `M7308` | error | `negative-spring-damping` | Spring-damper '<springId>' defines non-physical negative <param> (<value>). |
| `M7309` | error | `missing-ground-part` | Dataset does not define a ground reference body ('PART/... GROUND'). |
| `M7310` | warning | `unconstrained-part` | Part '<partId>' is completely disconnected from joints or force elements (floating rigid body). |

# EnergyPlus Building Simulation (`.idf`, `.epjson`)

`@modelscript/energyplus` (`languages/energyplus`) provides compiler, thermal lumped-capacitance DAE lowering, and bidirectional TGG synchronization for **US Department of Energy (DOE) EnergyPlus** building energy and HVAC models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format                     | Description                                                          |
| :-------- | :------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.idf`    | EnergyPlus Input Data File | Industry-standard comma/semicolon delimited building simulation deck |
| `.epjson` | EnergyPlus JSON Schema     | Structured JSON schema representation of EnergyPlus models           |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Lumped-Capacitance Multi-Zone Thermal DAEs

- Translates architectural thermal zones and building envelopes into continuous energy balance DAEs:
  $$C_{z,i} \frac{dT_{z,i}}{dt} = \sum_{j} \dot{Q}_{\text{cond},ij} + \sum_{k} \dot{Q}_{\text{conv},ik} + \dot{Q}_{\text{solar}} + \dot{Q}_{\text{internal}} + \dot{Q}_{\text{HVAC}}$$
- **Envelope Conduction**: Multi-layer wall, floor, and roof constructions with layer-resolved thermal conductivity $k$, density $\rho$, and specific heat $c_p$.
- **Window & Fenestration Optics**: U-factor, Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC), and visible transmittance shading calculations.
- **Internal Loads**: Schedules for lighting, occupancy sensible/latent heat release, and plug-load equipment dissipation.

### 2. Direct DAE Lowering

- Compiles building geometry and HVAC schedules directly into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` linear memory arena, enabling co-simulation with dynamic grid power models ([`@modelscript/pscad`](./pscad.md)) and district energy networks.

### 3. Bidirectional Triple Graph Grammar (TGG) Sync

- Implements bidirectional TGG rules (`energyplus-sync.ts`) synchronizing EnergyPlus thermal zones with:
  - **Modelica (`Modelica.Thermal` / IBPSA Buildings)**: Automatic translation into acausal thermal components and fluid loops.
  - **STEP CAD (ISO 10303)**: Validates physical geometric volume and boundary surface areas against 3D architectural CAD envelopes.

---

## Static Analysis & Pre-Flight Linter Rules

### Diagnostics for EnergyPlus (8 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M7901` | error | `unmatched-interzone-surface` | Interzone surface '<surfName>' in zone '<zoneName>' specifies outside boundary object '<targetSurf>' which does not exist or has mismatched reciprocal boundary. |
| `M7902` | warning | `non-convex-surface-polygon` | Surface polygon '<surfName>' in zone '<zoneName>' violates planar convexity, which may impair solar raytracing and view factor calculations. |
| `M7903` | error | `missing-thermal-properties` | Material '<matName>' has non-positive thermal property '<prop>' (<val>), violating second law of thermodynamics. |
| `M7904` | error | `unconnected-hvac-zone` | HVAC component '<hvacName>' references non-existent thermal zone '<zoneName>'. |

| `M7907` | error | `unreferenced-construction` | Building surface '<surfName>' references undefined construction '<constName>'. |
| `M7908` | error | `zero-thickness-material` | Opaque material '<matName>' has invalid non-positive thickness (<value>m). |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash

# Lower thermal zones to ModelScript linear memory DAE arena
msx energyplus to-dae CommercialOffice.idf --out=office.dae.json

# Project into standard Modelica IBPSA Buildings library components

```

# EPANET Water Distribution Networks (`.inp`)

`@modelscript/epanet` (`languages/epanet`) provides native parsing, hydraulic simulation, DAE lowering, and formal verification for **US EPA EPANET** pressurized drinking water distribution networks and municipal water infrastructure.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format            | Description                                                                       |
| :-------- | :---------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.inp`    | EPANET Input File | Industry-standard network topology, pipes, pumps, valves, and water quality decks |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Todini Global Gradient Method (GGM) Hydraulic Solver

- Implements the Todini Global Gradient Algorithm (`todini-ggm.ts`) for quadratic/nonlinear pipe network equilibrium:
  - **Conservation of Mass at Junctions**:
    $$\sum_{k \in \text{in}(i)} Q_k - \sum_{k \in \text{out}(i)} Q_k = D_i$$
  - **Conservation of Energy across Pipe Loops**:
    $$h_i - h_j = h_{L,ij} = r Q_{ij} |Q_{ij}|^{\alpha - 1}$$
- Supports **Hazen-Williams**, **Darcy-Weisbach**, and **Chezy-Manning** head loss friction models.

### 2. Multi-Component Hydraulic Elements

- **Pumps**: Head gain curves modeled via 3-point polynomial and power-law relationships ($h_p = h_0 - a Q^b$).
- **Tanks & Reservoirs**: Dynamic elevated storage tanks with hydrostatic pressure differential equations:
  $$A_{\text{tank}} \frac{dh}{dt} = \sum Q_{\text{in}} - \sum Q_{\text{out}}$$
- **Control Valves**: Pressure Reducing Valves (PRV), Pressure Sustaining Valves (PSV), and Flow Control Valves (FCV).

### 3. Direct DAE Lowering & Modelica Projection

- Compiles the entire municipal pipe and tank network into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` SoA linear memory arena.
- Projects EPANET networks into standard `Modelica.Fluid` pipes, reservoirs, and centrifugal pumps for joint thermo-fluid studies.

---

## Static Analysis & Pre-Flight Linter Rules

### Diagnostics for EPANET (8 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M8101` | error | `isolated-hydraulic-node` | Hydraulic node '<nodeId>' is isolated with no connecting pipes or pumps. |
| `M8102` | warning | `negative-pressure-risk` | Junction '<nodeId>' elevation (<value>m) exceeds maximum network source head (<value>m), risking cavitation and dry-out. |
| `M8103` | error | `non-monotonic-pump-curve` | Pump head curve '<curveId>' violates decreasing monotonicity: head increases from <value> to <value> between flow <value> and <value>. |
| `M8104` | error | `zero-length-pipe` | Pipe link '<pipeId>' has non-positive physical length (<value>m). |
| `M8105` | error | `zero-diameter-pipe` | Pipe link '<pipeId>' has non-positive internal diameter (<value>mm). |
| `M8106` | error | `duplicate-node-id` | Duplicate node identifier '<nodeId>' detected in water network topology. |
| `M8107` | error | `duplicate-link-id` | Duplicate link identifier '<linkId>' detected in water network topology. |
| `M8108` | error | `unreferenced-node-in-link` | Link '<linkId>' references undefined endpoint node '<nodeId>'. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Lint an EPANET municipal water network
msx epanet lint MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp

# Solve steady-state network hydraulics (Todini GGM) and print pressures
msx epanet solve MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp

# Lower network dynamics into ModelScript linear DAE arena
msx epanet to-dae MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp --out=network.dae.json

# Project into standard Modelica.Fluid components
msx epanet to-modelica MunicipalWaterNetwork.inp -o MunicipalPipes.mo
```

# EPA SWMM Stormwater & Urban Hydrology (`.inp`)

`@modelscript/swmm` (`languages/swmm`) provides zero-regex parsing, 1D Saint-Venant dynamic wave hydraulic routing, DAE lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **US EPA Stormwater Management Model (SWMM 5.x)** urban drainage, sewer collection, and flood mitigation networks.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format              | Description                                                                                                      |
| :-------- | :------------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.inp`    | EPA SWMM Input File | Industry-standard stormwater network deck (junctions, conduits, outfalls, subcatchments, pumps, weirs, orifices) |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. 1D Saint-Venant Dynamic Wave Routing

- Models open-channel and pressurized sewer hydraulics via the one-dimensional **Saint-Venant equations of unsteady flow**:
  - **Conservation of Mass (Continuity)**:
    $$\frac{\partial A}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = q_{\text{lateral}}$$
  - **Conservation of Momentum**:
    $$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( \frac{Q^2}{A} \right) + g A \frac{\partial H}{\partial x} + g A S_f = 0$$
    where $H = z + d$ is hydraulic head, $S_f$ is friction slope, and $S_0$ is conduit bed slope.
- Uses **Manning's open-channel equation** for friction slope:
  $$Q = \frac{k_m}{n} A R_h^{2/3} S_f^{1/2} \quad \implies \quad S_f = \frac{n^2 Q |Q|}{k_m^2 A^2 R_h^{4/3}}$$
  where $n$ is Manning roughness, $A$ is flow cross-sectional area, and $R_h = A / P_{\text{wetted}}$ is hydraulic radius.

### 2. Node & Link Hydraulic Structures

- **Junctions & Storage Units**: Continuous water stage mass conservation:
  $$A_{\text{node}} \frac{dH_i}{dt} = \sum Q_{\text{in}} - \sum Q_{\text{out}} + Q_{\text{inflow}} - Q_{\text{flood}}$$
- **Conduits**: Circular, rectangular, trapezoidal, and irregular natural river cross-sections with entrance/exit minor head loss coefficients.
- **Outfalls**: Free, normal, tidal, and fixed water elevation boundary conditions.
- **Regulators**: Orifices, transverse/side-flow weirs, and variable-speed lift pumps.

### 3. Direct DAE Lowering

- Compiles the entire stormwater collection network into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` struct-of-arrays linear memory arena.
- Enables co-simulation of municipal drinking water networks ([`@modelscript/epanet`](./epanet.md)) and drainage networks within the same computational arena.

### 4. Bidirectional Modelica 3.x Projection

- Projects SWMM nodes and channels into `Modelica.Fluid` open-channel tanks, flow conduits, and boundary reservoirs.

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

The SWMM linter verifies network graph integrity and hydraulic feasibility before simulation:

### Diagnostics for EPA SWMM (13 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M8201` | error | `dangling-node-reference` | Link '<linkId>' references undefined <role> node '<nodeId>'. |
| `M8202` | warning | `adverse-conduit-slope` | Conduit '<conduitId>' has adverse slope: inlet elevation (<value>) is lower than outlet elevation (<value>). |
| `M8203` | error | `missing-cross-section` | Conduit '<conduitId>' has no hydraulic cross-section definition in '[XSECTIONS]'. |
| `M8204` | error | `unsupported-outfall-type` | Outfall '<outfallId>' specifies unsupported boundary condition type '<type>'. |
| `M8205` | warning | `surcharge-overflow-risk` | Junction '<junctionId>' rim elevation (<value>) is lower than connected conduit crown (<value>), creating surcharge overflow risk. |
| `M8206` | error | `duplicate-node-id` | Duplicate node identifier '<nodeId>' declared in network. |
| `M8207` | error | `duplicate-link-id` | Duplicate link identifier '<linkId>' declared in network. |
| `M8208` | error | `negative-roughness` | Conduit '<conduitId>' specifies non-positive Manning's roughness coefficient (n = <n>). |
| `M8209` | error | `zero-length-conduit` | Conduit '<conduitId>' specifies non-positive length (<len>). |
| `M8210` | warning | `isolated-network-node` | Junction '<nodeId>' has no connected conduits or hydraulic links (isolated node). |
| `M8211` | error | `subcatchment-outlet-not-found` | Subcatchment '<subId>' references non-existent discharge outlet '<outletId>'. |
| `M8212` | error | `weir-offset-negative` | Weir '<weirId>' specifies negative crest height offset (<offset>). |
| `M8213` | error | `invalid-discharge-coefficient` | Link '<linkId>' specifies non-positive discharge coefficient (Cd = <cd>). |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect junctions, conduits, outfalls, and subcatchments
msx swmm inspect UrbanDrainage.inp

# Run pre-flight semantic diagnostics
msx swmm lint UrbanDrainage.inp

# Route steady-state hydraulic flow using Manning formulation
msx swmm route-flow UrbanDrainage.inp

# Lower network topology into ModelScript linear DAE arena
msx swmm to-dae UrbanDrainage.inp

# Project into Modelica 3.x fluid network components
msx swmm to-modelica UrbanDrainage.inp -o StormwaterNetwork.mo
```

# Aspen Plus & HYSYS Chemical Process (`.in`, `.inp`, `.bkp`)

`@modelscript/aspen` (`languages/aspen`) provides zero-regex parsing, vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) flash computation, distillation column MESH equations, DAE lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **Aspen Plus** and **Aspen HYSYS** chemical flowsheet input decks.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension      | Format                | Description                                                                          |
| :------------- | :-------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.in` / `.inp` | Aspen Plus Input File | Keyword-sectioned chemical process flowsheet, unit operations, stream thermodynamics |
| `.bkp`         | Aspen Backup Deck     | Serialized ASCII Aspen model topology and stream definitions                         |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Rachford-Rice Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium (VLE) Flash Solver

- Solves isothermal ($T$-$P$) and adiabatic ($P$-$H$) flash equilibrium via the **Rachford-Rice equation**:
  $$f(\psi) = \sum_{i=1}^{C} \frac{z_i (K_i - 1)}{1 + \psi (K_i - 1)} = 0$$
  where $\psi = V/F$ is the vapor fraction, $z_i$ is the feed mole fraction, and $K_i(T, P)$ is the equilibrium ratio:
  $$K_i = \frac{y_i}{x_i} = \frac{\gamma_i P_i^{\text{sat}}(T)}{\phi_i P}$$
- Uses modified **Antoine vapor pressure** equations:
  $$\ln P_i^{\text{sat}} = A_i - \frac{B_i}{T + C_i}$$
- Implements subcooled liquid ($\sum z_i K_i < 1$) and superheated vapor ($\sum z_i / K_i < 1$) state identification with monotonic Newton-Raphson bracket solving.

### 2. Unit Operations & Distillation Columns

- **Mixers & Splitters**: Rigorous material balance ($\sum F_{\text{in}} = \sum F_{\text{out}}$) and energy conservation ($\sum \dot{H}_{\text{in}} = \sum \dot{H}_{\text{out}}$).
- **Heaters & Coolers**: Specified duty ($Q$) or target outlet temperature/vapor fraction.
- **Flash Separators**: Multi-component 2-phase and 3-phase phase separation vessels.
- **RadFrac Equilibrium Distillation Columns**: Rigorous stage-by-stage **MESH equations** (Material balance, Equilibrium, Summation, Heat/enthalpy balance).

### 3. Direct Linear-Memory DAE Lowering

- Compiles flowsheet topology, stream molar balances, and component enthalpies directly into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` struct-of-arrays linear memory arena without intermediary AST allocations.
- Emits continuous DAE systems with algebraic stream constraints for joint dynamic simulation with pipeline networks ([`@modelscript/lps`](./lps.md)) and multiphase transient pipelines ([`@modelscript/olga`](./olga.md)).

### 4. Bidirectional Modelica 3.x Projection

- Translates unit operations into standardized `Modelica.Fluid` or OpenIPSL thermal-fluid models with acausal fluid ports (`m_flow`, `p`, `h`, `Xi`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

The Aspen analyzer inspects flowsheet connectivity, phase equilibria, and thermodynamic consistency:

### Diagnostics for Aspen Plus / HYSYS (15 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M8101` | error | `unconnected-stream-port` | Stream '<streamName>' connected to block '<blockName>' inlet has no producing source block outlet. |
| `M8102` | error | `tear-stream-unconverged` | Circular flowsheet loop detected involving block '<blockName>' without designated tear stream. |
| `M8103` | error | `invalid-eos-parameter` | Component '<compName>' lacks critical properties for property method '<propertyMethod>'. |
| `M8104` | error | `negative-component-fraction` | Stream '<streamName>' specifies negative component molar fraction for '<compName>' (<val>). |
| `M8105` | warning | `column-reboiler-heat-deficit` | Column '<blockName>' duty results in non-positive reboiler boil-up. |
| `M8106` | error | `duplicate-block-id` | Duplicate block ID '<blockId>' declared in flowsheet. |
| `M8107` | error | `duplicate-component-id` | Duplicate component ID '<compId>' declared in COMPONENTS. |
| `M8108` | warning | `fractions-sum-invalid` | Component mole fractions in stream '<streamName>' sum to <value>, expected 1.0. |
| `M8109` | error | `feed-stage-out-of-range` | Column '<blockName>' feed stage <stage> is out of bounds (1..<nStages>). |
| `M8110` | error | `product-stage-out-of-range` | Column '<blockName>' product stage <stage> is out of bounds (1..<nStages>). |
| `M8111` | warning | `missing-flowsheet-entry` | Block '<blockName>' has parameter declarations but is not connected in FLOWSHEET. |
| `M8112` | error | `stream-temperature-negative` | Stream '<streamName>' specifies non-physical absolute temperature <temp> K. |
| `M8113` | error | `stream-pressure-negative` | Stream '<streamName>' specifies non-positive pressure <pres> bar. |
| `M8114` | error | `radfrac-stages-too-few` | RadFrac column '<blockName>' has fewer than 2 stages (<nStages>). |
| `M8115` | error | `reflux-ratio-negative` | Column '<blockName>' reflux ratio (<rr>) must be non-negative. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect flowsheet components, blocks, and stream properties
msx aspen inspect MethanolWaterPlant.inp

# Run pre-flight semantic diagnostics
msx aspen lint MethanolWaterPlant.inp

# Solve isothermal flash VLE for a feed stream
msx aspen solve-flash MethanolWaterPlant.inp --stream FEED

# Lower flowsheet to ModelScript linear DAE arena
msx aspen to-dae MethanolWaterPlant.inp

# Project into Modelica 3.x acausal fluid stream model
msx aspen to-modelica MethanolWaterPlant.inp -o MethanolPlant.mo
```

================================================================================

# SBML Systems Biology & Biochemical Kinetics (`.sbml`, `.xml`)

`@modelscript/sbml` (`languages/sbml`) provides zero-regex streaming XML parsing, biochemical reaction network kinetics solving, 4th-order Runge-Kutta ODE simulation, linear DAE lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML Level 2 & 3 Core)** cellular, metabolic, and signaling network models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format            | Description                                                                               |
| :-------- | :---------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.sbml`   | SBML Model File   | Standard biochemical XML schema encoding compartments, species, parameters, and reactions |
| `.xml`    | SBML XML Document | General XML format containing standard SBML Level 2/3 definitions                         |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Biochemical Reaction Networks & Stoichiometry

- Parses hierarchical multi-compartment biochemical reaction networks:
  - **Compartments**: Cellular volumes (cytosol, mitochondria, extracellular space) with spatial dimensions (0D, 2D membrane, 3D volume).
  - **Species**: Chemical and protein concentrations or particle amounts ($[S_i] \ge 0$).
  - **Parameters**: Kinetic rate constants ($k_{\text{fwd}}, k_{\text{rev}}$), Michaelis constants ($K_m$), and Hill coefficients ($n$).
  - **Reactions**: Reversible and irreversible reaction fluxes ($v_j$) with stoichiometric coefficient matrices $N = [\nu_{ij}]$:
    $$\sum_{i} s_{ij} S_i \xrightarrow{v_j} \sum_{k} p_{kj} P_k$$

### 2. Kinetic Law Formulations & ODE Solver

- Evaluates dynamic reaction velocities across standard enzyme kinetics:
  - **Mass-Action Kinetics**:
    $$v = k_{\text{fwd}} \prod [R_i]^{s_i} - k_{\text{rev}} \prod [P_j]^{p_j}$$
  - **Michaelis-Menten Enzymatic Saturation**:
    $$v = \frac{V_{\text{max}} [S]}{K_m + [S]}$$
  - **Hill Cooperativity**:
    $$v = \frac{V_{\text{max}} [S]^n}{K_{0.5}^n + [S]^n}$$
- Solves the resulting non-linear **ordinary differential equations (ODEs)**:
  $$\frac{d[S_i]}{dt} = \frac{1}{V_{\text{comp}}} \sum_{j=1}^{R} \nu_{ij} \cdot v_j([S], p)$$
  using embedded 4th-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) integration or stiff SUNDIALS CVODE solvers.

### 3. Direct DAE Lowering

- Lowers reaction stoichiometric matrices and flux equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` linear memory arena.
- Enables co-simulation between cellular metabolic networks and pharmacokinetics / drug delivery fluid pipelines ([`@modelscript/aspen`](./aspen.md)).

### 4. Bidirectional Modelica 3.x Projection

- Projects SBML reaction systems into Modelica biochemical components and acausal substance substance-flow models.

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

The SBML analyzer validates stoichiometric consistency, undefined references, and physical rate bounds:

### Diagnostics for SBML (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M8801` | error | `missing-model-id` | SBML <model> element is missing required 'id' attribute. |
| `M8802` | error | `undefined-compartment-reference` | Species '<speciesId>' references undefined compartment '<compartmentId>'. |
| `M8803` | error | `undefined-species-reference` | Reaction '<reactionId>' references undefined <role> species '<speciesId>'. |
| `M8804` | error | `negative-compartment-size` | Compartment '<compartmentId>' defines non-positive size (<size>). |
| `M8805` | error | `negative-initial-amount-concentration` | Species '<speciesId>' specifies negative initial amount/concentration (<val>). |
| `M8806` | error | `empty-reaction` | Reaction '<reactionId>' must define at least one reactant or product. |
| `M8807` | warning | `missing-kinetic-law` | Reaction '<reactionId>' does not define a kineticLaw rate law equation. |
| `M8808` | error | `negative-stoichiometry` | Species reference for '<speciesId>' in reaction '<reactionId>' specifies non-positive stoichiometry (<stoich>). |
| `M8809` | warning | `undefined-kinetic-parameter` | Kinetic law formula in reaction '<reactionId>' references identifier '<id>' not found in parameters or species. |
| `M8810` | info | `circular-species-assignment` | Reaction '<reactionId>' lists '<speciesId>' as both reactant and product with identical stoichiometry; consider defining as modifier. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect compartments, species, parameters, and reactions
msx sbml inspect GlycolyticPathway.sbml

# Run pre-flight linting and stoichiometric validation
msx sbml lint GlycolyticPathway.sbml

# Simulate biochemical reaction kinetics ODEs with RK4
msx sbml simulate GlycolyticPathway.sbml --duration=20.0

# Lower biochemical reaction network to ModelScript linear DAE arena
msx sbml to-dae GlycolyticPathway.sbml

# Project into Modelica 3.x biochemical network model
msx sbml to-modelica GlycolyticPathway.sbml -o GlycolysisModel.mo
```

# Aerospace & Aviation

**Tagline:** Flight dynamics, propulsion & mission telemetry
**Summary:** Connect SysML v2 architectures and ReqIF requirements to JSBSim flight models, NASA ROCETS propulsion decks, and CCSDS telemetry, then simulate, verify, and export FMUs without leaving one toolchain.
**Headline:** From requirements to flight dynamics in a single, verifiable thread

**Target Languages:** `jsbsim`, `rocets`, `ccsds`, `easy5`, `sysml2`, `reqif`, `step`, `cfd`, `fea`, `fortran`
**Supported Standards:** SysML v2 / KerML, ReqIF, CCSDS OEM / OPM / XTCE, STEP AP242, FMI 2.0 / 3.0, SSP

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Requirements drift from analysis:** Requirements live in one tool, physics in another. Traceability is rebuilt by hand before every review.
- **Legacy Fortran & decks:** Decades of validated propulsion and flight code are locked in card decks and Fortran routines nobody wants to touch.
- **Certification evidence is manual:** Verification artifacts are assembled from screenshots and spreadsheets instead of generated from the models.

### Key Capabilities
- **6-DOF flight dynamics:** Parse JSBSim aircraft definitions and lower them to DAEs for simulation and linearization.
- **Propulsion transients:** Ingest ROCETS engine decks and turbomachinery maps, with a bridge for embedded Fortran user routines.
- **Mission telemetry:** Read CCSDS orbit and XTCE telemetry definitions and align them with simulated trajectories.
- **Formal verification:** Check SysML v2 constraints and requirement contracts with k-induction and SMT-backed proofs.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Capture:** SysML v2 architecture + ReqIF requirements
2. **Model:** JSBSim airframe, ROCETS engine, Modelica subsystems
3. **Simulate:** Stiff DAE solvers, Monte Carlo, surrogates
4. **Verify:** Requirement entailment & SARIF evidence

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx rocets simulate engine.roc
msx render SpacecraftPower spacecraft.sysml --view IBD -o ibd.svg
msx verify BrakingController brake.mo --format sarif
```

# Automotive & Mobility

**Tagline:** AUTOSAR, powertrain & autonomous-driving scenarios
**Summary:** Bring AUTOSAR architectures, Simulink controllers, GT-SUITE powertrains, and ASAM OpenDRIVE / OpenSCENARIO scenarios into one workspace, then co-simulate, check safety margins, and export FMUs.
**Headline:** Software-defined vehicles need a software-defined toolchain

**Target Languages:** `autosar`, `simulink`, `gtsuite`, `opendrive`, `openscenario`, `adams`, `simpack`, `ssp`, `modelica`, `c`
**Supported Standards:** AUTOSAR Classic & Adaptive, ASAM OpenDRIVE, ASAM OpenSCENARIO, FMI 2.0 / 3.0, SSP 1.0 / 2.0, ISO 26262 (via ReqIF)

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Toolchain sprawl:** Architecture, controls, plant, and scenario tools each speak their own format, so integrating them takes weeks.
- **Scenario coverage:** Proving AV safety means running thousands of scenarios, not a handful of hand-picked test drives.
- **Vendor lock-in:** Per-seat licenses limit who can run models, so CI and supplier collaboration suffer.

### Key Capabilities
- **AUTOSAR RTE simulation:** Inspect and lint ARXML, project it to SysML v2, and simulate runnable scheduling.
- **Simulink → Modelica:** Parse .slx / .mdl block diagrams and translate them to equation-based Modelica.
- **Scenario safety:** Orchestrate OpenSCENARIO runs on OpenDRIVE roads with time-to-collision and RSS margin checks.
- **Co-simulation:** Package FMUs with SSP and orchestrate multi-rate co-simulation.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Architect:** AUTOSAR ARXML → SysML v2
2. **Integrate:** Simulink controllers + GT-SUITE plant
3. **Scenario:** OpenDRIVE roads, OpenSCENARIO maneuvers
4. **Deliver:** FMI 3.0 FMUs & SSP packages

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx autosar lint BrakeController.arxml
msx simulink to-modelica Suspension.slx --out=Suspension.mo
msx fmu DC_Motor motor.mo --fmi-version 3 --type cs
```

# Rail

**Tagline:** Vehicle dynamics, track geometry & EN 14363
**Summary:** Read GENSYS and SIMPACK models, run track-vehicle simulations with measured irregularities, and generate EN 14363 acceptance and UIC 518 ride-comfort evidence automatically.
**Headline:** Railway vehicle dynamics and homologation, open and reproducible

**Target Languages:** `gensys`, `simpack`, `adams`, `modelica`, `step`, `csv`
**Supported Standards:** EN 14363, UIC 518, STEP AP242, FMI 2.0 / 3.0

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Homologation is slow:** Acceptance reports take weeks of manual post-processing and are hard to reproduce.
- **Tool silos:** Vehicle dynamics, track data, and CAD geometry live in separate tools and formats.
- **Opaque legacy models:** Validated models are hard to inspect, diff, or review in pull requests.

### Key Capabilities
- **Track-vehicle simulation:** Track geometry, irregularities, and wheel-rail contact lowered into a single DAE.
- **EN 14363 acceptance:** Automated homologation checks with HTML reports.
- **Ride comfort:** UIC 518 comfort indices across speed and track-quality sweeps.
- **Model translation:** Translate SIMPACK and Adams mechanisms to Modelica for open simulation.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Import:** GENSYS .calc / SIMPACK .spck
2. **Inspect:** Topology, mobility & lint
3. **Simulate:** Track irregularities & contact
4. **Certify:** EN 14363 homologation report

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx gensys lint ManchesterBenchmark.calc
msx gensys verify --y-force 40 --q-force 80 --axle-load 160
msx gensys report ManchesterBenchmark.calc --format html --out homologation.html
```

# Power Systems & Grid

**Tagline:** EMT, power flow & grid-code compliance
**Summary:** Run PSCAD/EMTDC electromagnetic transients, PSS/E transmission power flow, and OpenDSS distribution studies in one open toolchain, with IEEE 2800 and NERC PRC-029 ride-through verification built in.
**Headline:** Grid-code compliance, from PSCAD to IEEE 2800 in one pipeline

**Target Languages:** `pscad`, `psse`, `opendss`, `modelica`, `c`, `fortran`, `csv`
**Supported Standards:** IEEE 2800-2022, NERC PRC-029-1, IEEE C37.111 COMTRADE, PSS/E RAW v30–35, CIGRE black-box DLLs

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Interconnection queues:** Inverter-based resources need extensive EMT and ride-through studies before they can connect.
- **Black-box vendor models:** OEM controller DLLs only run inside specific desktop tools on specific operating systems.
- **Fragmented studies:** Transmission, distribution, and EMT models are maintained separately and drift apart.

### Key Capabilities
- **EMT simulation:** Native PSCAD project ingestion and electromagnetic transient solving.
- **Ride-through verification:** Automated IEEE 2800 LVRT/HVRT and NERC PRC-029 checks with JSON reports.
- **Power flow & DER hosting:** PSS/E transmission cases and OpenDSS unbalanced distribution and hosting-capacity analysis.
- **COMTRADE waveforms:** Read and write IEEE C37.111 transient recordings for comparison against field data.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Import:** PSCAD .pscx, PSS/E .raw, OpenDSS .dss
2. **Simulate:** EMT & power flow solvers
3. **Record:** COMTRADE waveforms
4. **Comply:** IEEE 2800 / NERC PRC-029 report

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx pscad verify-ieee2800 SolarPlant_250MW.pscx --tstop 3.0 --step 20us -o report.json
msx psse solve case.raw
msx psse diagram case.raw
```

# Oil, Gas & Subsurface

**Tagline:** Flow assurance, pipelines & reservoirs
**Summary:** Connect ECLIPSE reservoir decks, OLGA multiphase flow models, and PipelineStudio networks, and simulate transients, phase envelopes, and gas properties in one workspace.
**Headline:** Flow assurance from reservoir to export pipeline

**Target Languages:** `olga`, `lps`, `eclipse`, `aspen`, `sima`, `modelica`, `csv`
**Supported Standards:** ISO 20765-1, ISO 20765-2, FMI 2.0 / 3.0

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Siloed disciplines:** Reservoir, wells, pipelines, and facilities teams each use different simulators.
- **Costly transients:** Slugging, shutdown, and restart studies need many long runs across scenarios.
- **Hard-to-audit decks:** Large keyword decks are difficult to review, lint, and version-control.

### Key Capabilities
- **Multiphase transients:** Simulate OLGA subsea tie-backs and risers, and plot pipeline profiles.
- **Thermodynamics:** Flash calculations and phase envelopes from compositional fluid definitions.
- **Pipeline networks:** PipelineStudio TGNET/TLNET hydraulics with ISO 20765 gas properties.
- **Reservoir decks:** Parse and lint ECLIPSE reservoir input for traceable studies.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Reservoir:** ECLIPSE decks
2. **Flowline:** OLGA multiphase
3. **Network:** PipelineStudio hydraulics
4. **Facility:** Aspen process flowsheets

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx olga simulate subsea_tieback.opi --duration=3600 --out=traj.csv
```

# Electronics & Semiconductors

**Tagline:** SPICE, compact models, IBIS & S-parameters
**Summary:** Simulate SPICE netlists, compile Verilog-A compact models, and integrate IBIS buffers and Touchstone S-parameters with vector fitting and passivity enforcement.
**Headline:** Analog, RF, and signal integrity in one open toolchain

**Target Languages:** `spice`, `verilog-a`, `ibis`, `touchstone`, `modelica`, `c`
**Supported Standards:** IEEE 1857 Verilog-A / AMS, IBIS, Touchstone 1.0 / 2.0, SPICE netlists, FMI 2.0 / 3.0

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Fragmented EDA flows:** Circuit, device, and channel models each need a different simulator.
- **Non-passive macromodels:** Measured S-parameters produce unstable time-domain simulations if they aren't passive.
- **System context missing:** Electronics are rarely simulated together with the mechanical and thermal system around them.

### Key Capabilities
- **Circuit analysis:** SPICE operating point, transient, and AC analyses from the CLI.
- **Compact models:** Compile Verilog-A behavioral models to DAEs and export SPICE netlists.
- **Rational macromodels:** Vector fitting with Hamiltonian passivity enforcement for Touchstone data.
- **System-level projection:** Project circuits into Modelica for multi-domain studies.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Netlist:** SPICE + Verilog-A devices
2. **Channel:** Touchstone & IBIS models
3. **Simulate:** OP, transient & AC
4. **Integrate:** Modelica / FMU export

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx spice simulate LowPassFilter.cir --analysis op
msx spice simulate PowerSupply.cir --analysis tran --tstep 1e-6 --tstop 0.02 --out transient.csv
msx spice simulate AudioAmplifier.sp --analysis ac --format csv --out bode.csv
```

# Linter Rules Reference

ModelScript ships **803 diagnostic rules** across **43 languages**. This page is generated from each language's rule catalog (for example `languages/modelica/src/errors.ts`), so codes, severities and message templates match what the tools report. Text in `<angle brackets>` is filled in from your model.

## Running the linters

Diagnostics appear as you type in VS Code and the web IDE through the language server. From the command line:

```bash
# Languages handled by the unified linter (detected by file extension)
msx lint ./models
msx lint ./models --format json --strict

# Domain formats with their own command
msx spice lint SensorFrontEnd.net
```

The **CLI** column below shows which command reports each language's rules.

## Rule index

| Language                                  | Package                     | Rules | CLI                     |
| :---------------------------------------- | :-------------------------- | ----: | :---------------------- |
| [ModelScript](#modelscript)               | `@modelscript/modelscript`  |    10 | Language server / API   |
| [Modelica](#modelica)                     | `@modelscript/modelica`     |   307 | `msx lint`              |
| [SysML v2 / KerML](#sysml2)               | `@modelscript/sysml2`       |    48 | `msx lint`              |
| [ReqIF](#reqif)                           | `@modelscript/reqif`        |    10 | `msx reqif lint`        |
| [SSP](#ssp)                               | `@modelscript/ssp`          |    13 | `msx lint`              |
| [OWL2](#owl2)                             | `@modelscript/owl2`         |    24 | `msx lint`              |
| [STEP (ISO 10303)](#step)                 | `@modelscript/step`         |     8 | `msx lint`              |

| <span id="sbml-m8805"></span>`M8805` | `negative-initial-amount-concentration` | [error]    | Species '<code>&lt;speciesId&gt;</code>' specifies negative initial amount/concentration (<code>&lt;val&gt;</code>).                                                        |
| <span id="sbml-m8806"></span>`M8806` | `empty-reaction`                        | [error]    | Reaction '<code>&lt;reactionId&gt;</code>' must define at least one reactant or product.                                                                                    |
| <span id="sbml-m8807"></span>`M8807` | `missing-kinetic-law`                   | [warning] | Reaction '<code>&lt;reactionId&gt;</code>' does not define a kineticLaw rate law equation.                                                                                  |
| <span id="sbml-m8808"></span>`M8808` | `negative-stoichiometry`                | [error]    | Species reference for '<code>&lt;speciesId&gt;</code>' in reaction '<code>&lt;reactionId&gt;</code>' specifies non-positive stoichiometry (<code>&lt;stoich&gt;</code>).    |
| <span id="sbml-m8809"></span>`M8809` | `undefined-kinetic-parameter`           | [warning] | Kinetic law formula in reaction '<code>&lt;reactionId&gt;</code>' references identifier '<code>&lt;id&gt;</code>' not found in parameters or species.                       |
| <span id="sbml-m8810"></span>`M8810` | `circular-species-assignment`           | [info]       | Reaction '<code>&lt;reactionId&gt;</code>' lists '<code>&lt;speciesId&gt;</code>' as both reactant and product with identical stoichiometry; consider defining as modifier. |

DOCUMENT: Export Formats

# Export & Exchange Formats Reference

ModelScript serves as an open interoperability hub across systems engineering, multi-physics simulation, CAD/ECAD, formal verification, and regulatory compliance. Through `@modelscript/exchange`, `@modelscript/cad`, `@modelscript/runtime`, and `@modelscript/simulate`, the platform natively imports and exports **over 30 industry-standard formats**.

---

## 1. Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI 2.0 & FMI 3.0)

ModelScript compiles flattened DAE systems into self-contained `.fmu` archives (and imports external third-party `.fmu` binaries) conforming to the Modelica Association **FMI 2.0** and **FMI 3.0** specifications for both **Model Exchange (ME)** and **Co-Simulation (CS)**.

```bash
# Export an FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation FMU with embedded C99 source and WebAssembly binary
npx msx fmu DC_Motor motor.mo --fmi-version 3 --type cs --wasm --output DC_Motor.fmu

# Export a universal FMI 2.0 + 3.0 archive supporting both ME and CS
npx msx fmu ThermalPlant plant.mo --fmi-version both --type both --target all -o ThermalPlant.fmu

# Import an external third-party FMU and synthesize a typed Modelica wrapper block
npx msx import-fmu ./vendor/BatteryController.fmu -o BatteryControllerWrapper.mo
```

### Archive Layout & Capabilities

| Artifact Path                            | Standard      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| :--------------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `modelDescription.xml`                   | FMI 2.0 / 3.0 | Declares `ModelVariables`, causalities (`input`, `output`, `parameter`, `local`), physical units, `ModelStructure` (`Outputs`, `Derivatives`, `InitialUnknowns`), directional derivative sparsity patterns, and FMI 3.0 `Clock` / multidimensional array dimensions. |
| `sources/*.c`, `sources/*.h`             | ANSI C99      | Zero-dependency generated C99 implementation of `fmi2*` / `fmi3*` entry points, analytic Jacobians (`fmi2GetDirectionalDerivative` / `fmi3GetDirectionalDerivative`), and embedded RK4/BDF Co-Simulation steppers.                                                   |
| `binaries/<platform>/*.so\|.dll\|.dylib` | Native ABI    | Pre-compiled host shared libraries generated when `--compile` is passed.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `binaries/wasm32-wasi/<model>.wasm`      | WebAssembly   | Portable, sandboxed WASM FMU binary generated when `--wasm` or `--target wasm` is passed, executable directly in browser workers and edge runtimes.                                                                                                                  |

### Universal Binary FMUs & In-WASM CPU Emulation

A major limitation of traditional FMI co-simulation is platform lock-in: an FMU containing a Windows x86 `.dll` cannot run on Linux or Apple Silicon without native source access.

Through `@modelscript/exchange/pe-emulator`, ModelScript includes **user-space CPU emulators and binary loaders executing inside WebAssembly**:

- **Cross-Architecture Execution**: Runs legacy Windows x86/x64 (`.dll`), Linux ELF (`.so`), and macOS Mach-O (`.dylib`) binary FMUs directly inside Node.js, browsers, or cloud runners without installing Wine or virtual machines.
- **CPU Translation Engines**:
  - **x86 / x86-64 Engine (`x86-cpu.ts`)**: Decodes instruction prefixes, registers, and floating-point/AVX2 vector instructions into typed array memory operations.
  - **AArch64 Engine (`aarch64-cpu.ts`)**: Decodes 64-bit ARM instruction streams and executes floating-point NEON vectors.
  - **C Runtime Shims (`c-runtime-shims.ts`)**: Traps standard C library calls (`malloc`, `free`, `sin`, `cos`, `printf`, `memcpy`) and routes them directly to host memory for native execution speed.
- **In-Browser C Compilation Worker (`wasm-compiler-worker.ts`)**:
  - Compiles FMI C99 source code into sandboxed WebAssembly modules on the fly directly inside browser WebWorkers.
  - Eliminates the need for server-side GCC/Clang compilation infrastructure when simulating customer models in the browser.

---

## 2. System Structure and Parameterization (SSP 1.0 & SSV 1.0)

ModelScript natively parses, lints (`SSP_*` and `SSV_*` rules), simulates, and packages **Modelica Association SSP 1.0** system containers:

| Extension | XML Namespace                                                  | Purpose                                                                                                                                                   |
| :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.ssp`    | ZIP Container                                                  | Bundles `SystemStructure.ssd`, `resources/*.fmu` components, parameter sets (`*.ssv`), and signal dictionaries (`*.ssm`).                                 |
| `.ssd`    | `http://ssp-standard.org/SSP1/SystemStructureDescription`      | Defines hierarchical system architectures, FMU component references, typed connectors, causal signal connections, and `<ssd:DefaultExperiment>` metadata. |
| `.ssv`    | `http://ssp-standard.org/SSP1/SystemStructureParameterValues`  | Externalizes parameter sets (`Real`, `Integer`, `Boolean`, `String`, `Enumeration`, and units) for variant management without recompiling FMUs.           |
| `.ssm`    | `http://ssp-standard.org/SSP1/SystemStructureParameterMapping` | Maps abstract parameter names in `.ssv` catalogs to concrete hierarchical component paths.                                                                |

```bash
# Lint an SSP architecture and its SSV parameter bindings
npx msx lint SystemStructure.ssd NominalParams.ssv

# Export a multi-project PSCAD workspace to an SSP 1.0 container
npx msx pscad export-ssp GridInterconnection.pswx -o GridInterconnection.ssp
```

---

## 3. Formal Verification Formats

The `msx export-formal` command translates SysML v2 models (constraints, requirements, and state machines) into three formal verification formats for external solvers and model checkers:

```bash
# Export constraints to SMT-LIB v2.6 for Z3 / cvc5 (logic auto-detected as QF_LRA or QF_NRA)
npx msx export-formal FlightControl.sysml --format smt2 -o fcs.smt2

# Export state machines to nuXmv with an extra safety invariant
npx msx export-formal FlightControl.sysml --format nuxmv --module FlightControl --invariants "altitude >= 0" -o fcs.smv

# Export assume-guarantee contracts to OCRA
npx msx export-formal FlightControl.sysml --format ocra -o fcs.oss
```

| Format Flag | Extension | Target Toolchains | Encoding Semantics                                                                                                                     |
| :---------- | :-------- | :---------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `smt2`      | `.smt2`   | Z3, cvc5          | SMT-LIB v2.6 with a `set-logic` directive (`--logic QF_LRA\|QF_NRA\|QF_IDL\|ALL`) and optional `--minimize` / `--maximize` objectives. |
| `nuxmv`     | `.smv`    | nuXmv             | Symbolic transition system module with optional `INVARSPEC` (`--invariants`) and `LTLSPEC` (`--ltl`) properties.                       |
| `ocra`      | `.oss`    | OCRA              | Contract-based component specification; `--module` sets the top-level component name.                                                  |

---

## 4. CI/CD Quality Gates & Regulatory Compliance Dossiers

The `msx verify` and `msx dhf` commands serialize static diagnostics, formal proof certificates, and requirement traceability matrices into industry-standard CI/CD and regulatory formats:

```bash
# SARIF v2.1.0 for GitHub Code Scanning / Azure DevOps Security Tab
npx msx verify system.mo --format sarif --report linter-report.sarif

# CTRF (Common Test Report Format) JSON for unified CI dashboards
npx msx verify system.mo --format ctrf --report ctrf-report.json

# JUnit XML for Jenkins, GitLab CI, and CircleCI test summaries
npx msx verify system.mo --format junit --report junit-report.xml

# FDA 21 CFR Part 820 / ISO 13485 / ISO 26262 Design History File (DHF) Dossier
npx msx verify system.mo --format dhf --report dossier.md
npx msx dhf export ./workspace --format markdown -o DHF_Dossier.md
```

| Format              | Schema / Standard             | Key Payload Contents                                                                                                                                        |
| :------------------ | :---------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **SARIF** (`sarif`) | OASIS SARIF v2.1.0            | Rule descriptors (`M1000`–`M6040`, `S1001`–`S5008`), physical file locations (1-indexed line/column spans), severity levels, and counterexample code flows. |
| **CTRF** (`ctrf`)   | CTRF v0.0.0 JSON              | Standardized `results.summary` (`tests`, `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`) and per-property verification duration and witness traces.                          |
| **JUnit** (`junit`) | JUnit XML                     | `<testsuites>` and `<testcase>` elements with `<failure>` stack traces for falsified invariants or lint errors.                                             |
| **DHF** (`dhf`)     | FDA 21 CFR 820.30 / ISO 13485 | End-to-end Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM), formal proof summaries, simulation verification evidence, and SHA-256 artifact integrity digests.        |

## 5. Systems Engineering & Requirements Interop (SysML v2, ReqIF, OSLC, OWL2)

ModelScript bridges descriptive MBSE specifications and semantic knowledge graphs with executable physics:

| Standard                         | Extensions / Media Types                                                  | CLI Command / API                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                         |

| **OMG ReqIF 1.2**                | `.reqif`, `.reqifz`                                                       | `msx reqif <import\|export>`                                                     | Bidirectional mapping between DOORS/Polarion ReqIF `SPEC-OBJECT` / `SPEC-RELATION` hierarchies and SysML v2 `requirement def` / `satisfy` blocks.                                   |
| **OASIS OSLC 3.0 & TRS 3.0**     | `.ttl`, `.jsonld`, `.rdf`                                                 | `msx oslc <export\|serve>`                                                       | Exposes requirements (`oslc_rm:Requirement`) and architecture resources (`oslc_am:Resource`) with Tracked Resource Set (TRS 3.0) incremental change logs and delegated UI previews. |

## 6. Industrial Digital Twin & Open Hardware Packaging (DDP, AASX, OKH)

For manufacturing handover, Industry 4.0 asset integration, and open-source hardware certification, ModelScript supports three complementary packaging standards:

```bash
# Pack a workspace into an ISO/PAS 81346 Digital Data Package (.ddp)
npx msx ddp pack ./workspace -o PumpStation.ddp

# Convert a DDP archive into an IDTA Asset Administration Shell v3.0 (.aasx) package
npx msx ddp to-aasx PumpStation.ddp -o PumpStation.aasx
```

| Standard                      | Format / Endpoint                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                 |
| :---------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ISO/PAS 81346 DDP**         | `.ddp` (ZIP + XML/JSON)                            | Structures multi-domain engineering deliverables by function (`=`), product (`-`), and location (`+`) reference designation aspect trees.                   |
| **IDTA AAS v3.0**             | `.aasx` (Open Packaging Conventions) & `?lens=aas` | Packages Asset Administration Shells containing standardized `Nameplate`, `TechnicalData`, `HandoverDocumentation`, and `SimulationModels` (FMU) submodels. |
| **DIN SPEC 3105 / OSHWA OKH** | `okh.json` / `okh.toml` & `?lens=okh`              | Generates Open Know-How (OKH v1.0) manifests detailing bill of materials (BOM), CAD/ECAD design files, manufacturing tolerances, and SPDX licenses.         |

## 9. Surrogate Modeling & Machine Learning (ONNX, C99, Modelica ROM)

The `msx surrogate` pipeline exports trained Reduced-Order Models (MLP neural networks, multivariate polynomials, and Radial Basis Functions) with embedded domain-validity guardrails:

```bash
# Train an MLP surrogate and export ONNX, standalone C99, and pure Modelica (.mo) simultaneously
npx msx surrogate Compressor compressor.mo \
  --inputs "rpm,pressureRatio" \
  --input-bounds "rpm:1000:12000,pressureRatio:1.1:4.5" \
  --outputs "massFlow,efficiency" \
  --format all \
  --out-file build/compressor_rom
```

- **ONNX (`.onnx`)**: Serializes weights, biases, input normalization scalers, and activation layers (`Tanh`, `ReLU`, `GELU`) as a standard ONNX protobuf graph for deployment in ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, or PyTorch. Can also be imported via `--from-onnx`.
- **Standalone ANSI C99 (`.c` / `.h`)**: Zero-dependency static C inference function with compile-time weight arrays and bounding-box extrapolation flags for embedded MCU deployment.
- **Modelica Block (`.mo`)**: Self-contained Modelica `block` containing pure matrix/vector equations, `isExtrapolating` boolean output port, and `assert()` guardrails.

## 10. Simulation Trajectories & Scientific Data (CSV, JSON, MAT v4, HDF5, Parquet)

Simulation and Monte Carlo runners (`msx simulate`, `msx mc`, and Cloud HPC workers) produce structured time-series outputs:

```bash
# Export standard RFC 4180 CSV trajectory
npx msx simulate DC_Motor motor.mo --stop-time 5.0 --format csv > trajectory.csv

# Export structured JSON trajectory with variable metadata and solver statistics
npx msx simulate DC_Motor motor.mo --stop-time 5.0 --format json > trajectory.json
```

| Format                      | Source / Consumer                                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| :-------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **CSV (`.csv`)**            | `msx simulate --format csv`, `msx mc --format csv`, `@modelscript/csv` | Leading monotonic `time` column followed by state, derivative (`der(...)`), and algebraic variable columns; directly consumable by `Modelica.Blocks.Tables.CombiTimeTable` and `msl-comparison-runner`. |
| **JSON (`.json`)**          | `msx simulate --format json`, `msx mc --format json`                   | Contains `time: number[]`, `signals: Record<string, number[]>`, `units: Record<string, string>`, `events`, and solver convergence telemetry.                                                            |
| **MATLAB Level 4 (`.mat`)** | OpenModelica / Dymola compatibility                                    | Dual-matrix (`Aclass`, `name`, `description`, `dataInfo`, `data_1` parameters, `data_2` trajectories) binary format for legacy post-processing scripts.                                                 |
| **Apache Parquet & HDF5**   | Cloud HPC (`msx cloud download`) & Digital Twin Archive                | Columnar Zstandard-compressed trajectory storage for multi-gigabyte Monte Carlo ensembles and long-horizon operational twin logs.                                                                       |

# MCP Server & IDE Workbench Reference

ModelScript provides first-class AI agent integration via the **Model Context Protocol (`@modelscript/mcp`)** alongside a comprehensive polyglot **VS Code Extension & Web IDE (`@modelscript/ide-client`, `@modelscript/lsp`)**. Both surfaces share the same zero-allocation WebAssembly GLR parsers, Salsa `QueryEngine`, and linear-memory `DAEBuilder`.

---

## Part I: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server

The `@modelscript/mcp` package exposes ModelScript's compilation, simulation, formal verification, ontology reasoning, Triple Graph Grammar (TGG) synchronization, and requirements traceability engines to MCP-compatible AI coding assistants (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity, Zed, and custom LLM orchestrators).

### 1. Deployment Modes & Transports

ModelScript supports three MCP execution architectures:

#### A. Local `stdio` Server (`modelscript-mcp`)

For local desktop AI agents, run the `modelscript-mcp` binary over standard input/output (`StdioServerTransport`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "modelscript": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelscript/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "MODELICAPATH": "/path/to/ModelicaStandardLibrary"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### B. Hosted Enterprise SSE Gateway (`/api/v1/mcp`)

The ModelScript Enterprise Hub (`apps/api/src/routes/mcp.ts`) exposes a multi-tenant HTTP Server-Sent Events (SSE) MCP gateway with built-in compute credit metering:

- **`GET /api/v1/mcp/sse`**: Establishes a persistent SSE stream (`text/event-stream`), authenticates the caller via `Authorization: Bearer <JWT | ms_bot_*>`, and returns a session-scoped `endpoint` event (`/api/v1/mcp/messages?sessionId=<uuid>`).
- **`POST /api/v1/mcp/messages?sessionId=<uuid>`**: Receives JSON-RPC 2.0 `tools/call` and `resources/read` requests, checks organization compute credit balances via `BillingService` (1 credit per lightweight query, 5 credits for `modelica_simulate` / `hybrid_simulate` / `modelica_doe` / `modelscript_closed_loop_synthesize`), and streams results over the SSE channel.

#### C. In-WASM AOT Polyglot Dispatch (`PolyglotMcpHost`)

In browser workers and edge sandboxes (`packages/mcp/src/polyglot-server.ts`), `PolyglotMcpHost` dynamically synthesizes MCP tool schemas from every registered `LanguageDefinition` (`defineLanguage({ mcp: { tools, resources } })`). When a tool declares an `aotExport` symbol, `PolyglotMcpHost` writes the arguments directly into WebAssembly linear memory (`__newString`), invokes the compiled AssemblyScript kernel (`mcpDispatchTool(toolId, targetPtr, paramsJsonPtr)`), and reads back the JSON result with zero JS object marshaling overhead.

---

### 2. Complete Reference of All 52 Core MCP Tools

The canonical MCP server (`packages/mcp/src/tools.ts`) registers **52 specialized engineering tools** grouped across nine functional domains:

#### Domain 1: Modelica Compilation, Simulation, Linearization & Sensitivity (11 Tools)

| Tool Name              | Required Arguments                                                                          | Optional Arguments                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                           |
| :--------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `modelica_load`        | `path: string`                                                                              | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Load a `.mo` file or package directory from disk into the stateful MCP workspace session and return all discovered class FQNs.                                        |
| `modelica_parse`       | —                                                                                           | `code?: string`, `path?: string`                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Parse Modelica source text or a file using the native WASM GLR parser and return CST syntax diagnostics and top-level class names.                                    |
| `modelica_flatten`     | `className?: string`                                                                        | `name?: string`, `code?: string`, `path?: string`, `includeMetrics?: boolean`                                                                                                                                                                               | Flatten a hierarchical Modelica class into a canonical DAE (`ArenaDAEPrinter` output) and return structural BLT/Pantelides metrics and flattened source text.         |
| `modelica_lint`        | —                                                                                           | `code?: string`, `path?: string`                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Execute all `M1xxx`–`M6xxx` static lint rules and Salsa semantic queries, returning structured diagnostics with line/column spans.                                    |
| `modelica_simulate`    | `className: string`                                                                         | `code?: string`, `path?: string`, `tStart?: number` (`0`), `tEnd?: number` (`1`), `dt?: number` (`0.01`), `tolerance?: number` (`1e-6`), `method?: "euler" \| "rk4" \| "dopri5" \| "bdf" \| "radau5" \| "cvode" \| "ida"` (`"rk4"`), `variables?: string[]` | Flatten, index-reduce (Pantelides + BLT tearing), and numerically simulate a Modelica model, returning downsampled time-series trajectories and solver statistics.    |
| `hybrid_simulate`      | `className: string`                                                                         | `code?: string`, `path?: string`, `tStart?: number` (`0`), `tEnd?: number` (`10`), `dt?: number` (`0.01`), `maxEvents?: number` (`500`)                                                                                                                     | Run hybrid continuous/discrete event-driven simulation with zero-crossing root finding (`when` clauses, `reinit()`, state machines, and synchronous clocks).          |
| `modelica_doe`         | `className: string`, `parameters: Record<string, number[]>`                                 | `code?: string`, `path?: string`, `tEnd?: number` (`1`), `dt?: number` (`0.01`), `metrics?: string[]`                                                                                                                                                       | Execute a Cartesian/factorial Design of Experiments (DoE) sweep across parameter combinations and return terminal/summary metrics for each run.                       |
| `modelica_sensitivity` | `className: string`, `parameters: string[]`, `outputs: string[]`                            | `code?: string`, `path?: string`, `tEnd?: number` (`1`), `dt?: number` (`0.01`), `perturbation?: number` (`0.01`)                                                                                                                                           | Compute normalized local sensitivity Jacobians ($\frac{\partial y_i}{\partial p_j} \cdot \frac{p_j}{y_i}$) via central finite differences or forward AD.              |
| `modelica_query`       | `queryType: "list_classes" \| "class_info" \| "components" \| "equations" \| "connections"` | `className?: string`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Query the active Salsa `SymbolIndex` for class specializations, typed component declarations, equations, or `connect()` topology edges.                               |
| `modelica_linearize`   | `className: string`                                                                         | `code?: string`, `operatingPoint?: Record<string, number>`, `inputs?: string[]`, `outputs?: string[]`                                                                                                                                                       | Linearize a Modelica DAE around an equilibrium point to extract explicit LTI State-Space matrices ($A, B, C, D$), eigenvalues, damping ratios, and stability margins. |
| `modelica_tune_pid`    | `className: string`                                                                         | `code?: string`, `controllerType?: "P" \| "PI" \| "PID"`, `targetBandwidthRadPerSec?: number`, `maxSensitivityMs?: number`                                                                                                                                  | Synthesize $K_p, K_i, K_d, N$ controller gains for a linearized Modelica plant using Skogestad IMC (SIMC) and sensitivity-constrained loop shaping.                   |

## Part II: VS Code Extension & Web IDE Workbench

The official ModelScript extension (`modelscript.modelscript`, source in `apps/ide/` and `packages/lsp/`) runs both in **VS Code Desktop** (Node.js extension host) and **VS Code for the Web / `ide.modelscript.org`** (100% browser WebWorker host).

### 1. Polyglot Language Server (`@modelscript/lsp`)

A single unified Language Server Protocol instance provides incremental language intelligence across the registered languages (`.mo`, `.sysml`, `.kerml`, `.msx`, `.pscx`, `.pswx`, `.scad`, `.stp`, `.step`, `.owl`, `.ssp`, `.ssd`, `.ssv`, `.csv`, `.su2`, `.cfg`, `.inp`, `.gbr`):

- **Real-Time Diagnostics**: Incremental GLR parsing + Salsa `lint__*` queries + cross-file unit/type checking.
- **Navigation & Refactoring**: Go-to-Definition, Find All References (across `.sysml` $\leftrightarrow$ `.mo` $\leftrightarrow$ `.msx` boundaries), Workspace Symbol Search, Rename Symbol, and Document Outline.
- **Code Lenses & Inlay Hints**: Inline equation/variable balance badges (`[Balanced: 14 vars / 14 eqs]`), inferred SI unit inlay hints, and one-click `▶ Simulate`, `⚡ Verify`, and `📐 Render Diagram` CodeLenses above every `model`, `part def`, and `verification def`.

### 2. Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) Simulation Debugger

ModelScript registers a full **Debug Adapter Protocol** implementation (`"type": "modelscript"`) that lets engineers step through continuous-time DAE integrations, state-machine transitions, and zero-crossing events exactly like stepping through imperative code:

- **Time & Condition Breakpoints**: Set breakpoints on equation lines, `when` clauses, state transitions, or conditional simulation expressions (e.g., `time >= 2.5` or `der(omega) < 0`).
- **Execution Controls**: `Continue`, `Step Over` (advance one solver step $\Delta t$), `Step Into` (step into Newton-Raphson / event-iteration micro-steps), `Step Back` (reverse-time trajectory scrubbing), and `Restart`.
- **Live Inspection Scopes**: Inspect `States (x)`, `Derivatives (der(x))`, `Algebraic Variables (y)`, `Parameters (p)`, `Discrete / Clocked`, and `Solver Telemetry (h, localError, jacobianCond)` in the VS Code Variables and Watch panes.

```json
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "type": "modelscript",
      "request": "launch",
      "name": "Debug Modelica Simulation",
      "model": "Modelica.Mechanics.Rotational.Examples.First",
      "program": "${file}",
      "stopTime": 5.0,
      "solver": "rodas4p",
      "breakOnZeroCrossing": true
    }
  ]
}
```

### 3. Virtual Filesystems & Interactive Notebooks (`.monb`)

- **Virtual FileSystem Providers**:
  - `modelica://`: Read-only browsable virtual filesystem mounting the bundled Modelica Standard Library (MSL) and installed registry packages (`modelica_modules/`).
  - `memfs://`: Ephemeral in-memory workspace used in the browser IDE (`ide.modelscript.org`).
  - `github://`: Zero-clone direct browsing and editing of remote GitHub repositories.
- **ModelScript Interactive Notebooks (`modelscript.monbNotebook`)**:
  - Native VS Code `NotebookSerializer` and `NotebookController` for `.monb` files.
  - Supports polyglot code cells (`modelica`, `sysml2`, `modelscript`, `scad`, `sparql`) that share a reactive kernel session, rendering interactive Bode plots, time-series charts, 3D CAD viewports, and SVG schematics directly below each cell.

### 4. Custom Document Editors & Engineering Workbench Panels

The extension contributes **9 custom visual editors** and **over 20 specialized engineering webview panels**:

| Custom Editor / View ID                         | Bound File Types / Trigger               | Capabilities                                                                                                                                                        |
| :---------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `modelscript.diagramEditor`                     | `.mo`, `.sysml`, `.pscx`                 | Bi-directional graphical schematic & SysML v2 (BDD/IBD/State/Activity) editor; dragging components or routing wires updates the underlying source CST in real time. |
| `modelscript.monbNotebook`                      | `.monb`                                  | Literate engineering notebook combining Markdown/LaTeX narratives with live simulation and verification cells.                                                      |
| `modelscript.fmuViewer`                         | `.fmu`                                   | Inspects FMI 2.0/3.0 `modelDescription.xml`, causal ports, dependency sparsity matrices, and runs interactive test simulations on `.fmu` files.                     |
| `modelscript.sspEditor`                         | `.ssp`, `.ssd`, `.ssv`                   | Visual block-diagram editor for wiring multi-FMU co-simulation topologies and editing `.ssv` parameter tables.                                                      |
| `modelscript.reqifEditor`                       | `.reqif`, `.reqifz`                      | Tabular requirements specification editor with suspect-link indicators and one-click SysML v2 synchronization.                                                      |
| `modelscript.cadViewer`                         | `.stp`, `.step`, `.scad`, `.stl`, `.glb` | Hardware-accelerated Three.js / WebGL 3D CAD viewport with section planes, B-Rep face selection, and kinematic animation playback.                                  |
| `modelscript.gerberViewer`                      | `.gbr`, `.drl`                           | Multi-layer 2D/3D PCB copper, solder mask, silkscreen, and drill stackup inspector.                                                                                 |

| **BLT & Tearing Matrix Inspector**              | `modelscript.inspectBlt`                 | Visualizes the Tarjan Block Lower Triangular incidence matrix, Pantelides differentiated equations, and Cellier-Elmqvist tearing variables.                         |
| **Formal Verification & Counterexample Center** | `modelscript.verify`                     | Interactive dashboard for running BMC/$k$-induction/IC3/STL falsification and replaying falsifying counterexample traces step-by-step on the schematic.             |
| **Digital Thread & RTM Explorer**               | `modelscript.digitalThread`              | Interactive graph explorer showing end-to-end traceability across OWL2 $\to$ SysML v2 $\to$ Modelica $\to$ CAD $\to$ Verification DHF.                              |

### 5. Three-Tier AI Engineering Copilot

The IDE integrates an engineering-aware AI assistant (`modelscript.aiChatView`) that operates across three configurable inference tiers:

1. **Tier 1 — Zero-Cloud Browser WebGPU (`Qwen3-0.6B` / WebLLM)**: Runs 100% locally inside the browser or desktop GPU using quantized WebGPU weights for air-gapped syntax completion, equation explanation, and unit conversion with zero data egress.
2. **Tier 2 — Local Workstation Inference (`Ollama` / `vLLM` OpenAI-compatible)**: Connects to a local model server (`http://localhost:11434`) with automatic tool-calling bound to the in-process `@modelscript/mcp` tools.
3. **Tier 3 — Hosted Frontier Models + MCP Gateway**: Connects frontier reasoning models to the workspace's live `@modelscript/mcp` server (or `/api/v1/mcp/sse`), enabling autonomous closed-loop synthesis (`modelscript_closed_loop_synthesize`), differential calibration (`modelica_diff_calibrate`), and multi-domain TGG reconciliation (`tgg_reconcile_slot`).

---

## Part III: Social AI Agents & Autonomous Bots

ModelScript features native autonomous bot support across the social engineering network (`apps/api` and `apps/web`), allowing automated agents to participate in engineering discussions, verify physical equations, run continuous DAE simulations, and attach interactive artifact views.

### 1. Bot Registration & Scopes

Users can register autonomous bots in **Settings $\to$ Autonomous Bots** or programmatically via `POST /api/v1/users/me/bots`:

- **Dedicated Bot Identity**: Bots receive a unique handle (e.g. `@dynamics_bot`), custom display name, bio, avatar, and system persona prompt.
- **`ms_bot_*` Bearer Tokens**: Authenticate bot calls against social endpoints, the git repository engine, and the MCP SSE gateway.
- **Granular Capability Scopes**:
  - `social:read`: Read public engineering threads, parent contexts, and mentions.
  - `social:write`: Post responses, explanations, and quotes into social threads.
  - `social:simulate`: Execute DAE solvers (SUNDIALS CVODE/IDA) and synthesize interactive trajectory plots.
  - `modelica:validate`: Compile and check Modelica CST syntax and static semantics.

### 2. Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) Inference

Bots can run on instance-default models or configure private credentials:

- **BYOK Cloud API Keys**: Supports Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic API keys directly configured on the bot.
- **Custom Inference Endpoints**: Point to local `Ollama` (`http://localhost:11434/v1`), `vLLM`, or private enterprise LLM gateways.
- **Inference Models**: Select from specialized models including `gemini-1.5-flash`, `gemini-1.5-pro`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-4o`, `deepseek-r1`, or `qwen-2.5-coder`.

### 3. Mention Processing & Live WebSocket Indicators

When an engineering post or comment mentions an automated bot (`@dynamics_bot`):

1. **Background Queue**: The API enqueues the job into `bot_mention_queue` with anti-loop recursion safeguards (bot mentions cannot trigger nested bot replies).
2. **Real-Time WebSocket Indicators**: The backend streams live status updates over `/api/v1/collab/stream`:
   - `thinking`: The bot is parsing prompt equations and generating physical models.
   - `simulating`: The bot is running numerical integrators and preparing trajectory data.
   - `done`: The reply is posted and the UI automatically appends the completed card.
3. **Interactive Artifact Synthesis**:
   - `morsel`: Inline interactive Modelica code view with syntax highlighting and verification badges.
   - `vega-plot`: Interactive Vega-Lite timeseries charts with state variable selection and trajectory zoom.
